## Step P3-07 — 2026-08-03: the recalibration stack, and two numbers it refuses to invent

**Inputs.** `calib/temperature.py::{fit_temperature, apply_temperature, STACK_ORDER}` (P2-13,
the exact convex β = 1/T bisection); the P3-02 `calib` column contract (859 positives + 230
decoys, every one on the `fold_random == "train"` rung, asserted disjoint from val/test at
build time); the Stage-2 binary-head contract `Stage2Model.forward -> "tbox_logit"`, shape
`(B,)`, one raw logit. **Process.** `src/tbox_finder/calib/recalibrate.py` ships the ADR-0005
D11 stack for the Stage-2 head: `temperature_scale` fits T, `prior_shift` applies the
Saerens/Elkan log-odds correction, and `calibrated_posterior` returns **both** the named
posterior (temperature-scaled, pre-shift — the GATE-2-gated object) and the prior-shifted one,
with `gated_posterior_key` naming the former inside the payload. **Outputs.** One module, one
test module (108 tests), no data artifact and no fitted T — see the last paragraph.

**There is one temperature fit in this repo, and this is not a second one.** Stage 2's head is
a single logit; stacking it as `[0, z]` makes P2-13's multi-class fit *identically* the binary
one, because `softmax([0, βz])[1] = σ(βz)`, so its NLL is exactly the binary cross-entropy at
`βz` — the same reduction `stage2/losses.py` already uses to route the binary term through the
audited focal-CE kernel. The adapter therefore touches the *inputs* and never the arithmetic,
and P2-13's two degenerate-limit refusals (perfect separation ⇒ β → ∞; worse-than-uniform ⇒
β → 0) carry through unchanged. The cost of delegating is that "A agrees with B" becomes a
tautology, so the primary test is neither: for `z = [+a, +a, −a]`, `y = [1, 0, 0]` the
stationarity condition `Σ z_i(σ(βz_i) − y_i) = 0` collapses to `3σ(βa) = 2`, giving
**`β* = ln2/a` exactly**. A second case at a second scale (`4σ = 3` ⇒ `β* = ln3/a`), a ternary
search in the *test* that minimises the value rather than rooting the derivative, and a
manufactured-miscalibration draw that recovers `T ≈ 2.5` from 20,000 rows are the independent
confirmations; the delegation check is present and labelled secondary.

**"T fit only on `calib`, never test" is a property of the code, not a claim about the caller.**
`temperature_scale` takes the whole table plus a per-row rung label and selects the `calib`
rows itself, so there is no argument through which a graded row can reach the fit. Three
refusals surround that: an **empty** selection raises with the full census (the all-`False`
calib column filters clean and fits on nothing, which reads exactly like a working filter); an
**unrecognised rung token** raises rather than being skipped (a row that silently vanishes
shrinks the calibration set while every count still looks fine); and a **single-class** calib
rung raises. `assign_rung` re-derives the P3-02 invariant — a calib row lives in the `train`
rung — at the point of use, and tests missingness with `masking.is_missing`, because
`bool(float("nan")) is True` and under the training env's pandas 3 a null cell arrives as NaN,
so the naive guard would promote a row with **no** calibration flag straight into the fit.

**The fixtures are asymmetric on purpose.** The rung arms are 7 calib / 4 train / 3 val / 5
test, and both the calib and test arms are independently fittable, so the inversion test can
run both ways round: swapping the two senses is asserted to change `n_fitted` *and* to produce
exactly the T of the test arm fitted alone. Balanced arms with count-only assertions would
refuse the right number of the wrong rows and pass.

**Two numbers this step declines to produce, and why that is the deliverable rather than a
gap.** (1) **No deployment prior is pinned.** PRD.md:188 and ADR-0005:80 give the genome-scale
prevalence only as prose, `~10³–10⁴:1` (negatives per positive); nothing in the repo encodes a
value. Pinning a scalar would be a new blinded-frozen default needing ADR sign-off, and
defaulting one silently would put a fabricated quantity into every downstream posterior. So
both priors are required keyword arguments with no defaults, a half-specified shift raises, and
`DEPLOYMENT_PRIOR_RANGE` exists only as the band a supplied prior is *reported* against — a
predicate shown to discriminate, since ADR-0005 D7's own `100:1` benchmark prevalence must fall
outside it. (2) **No T is fitted here.** Nothing in the repo reads a Stage-2 checkpoint back —
`stage2_heads.pt` and `lora_adapter/` have write sites and no readers, and `train.py::evaluate`
discards per-row logits — so real `calib`-split logits do not yet exist. This step ships and
certifies the machinery; producing the scores, and with them the first real T, belongs to the
step that first needs a calibrated posterior (P3-08/P3-10). A T invented to fill the gap would
look exactly like a measured one.

**Path drift, recorded not silently taken.** imp.md names
`src/tbox_finder/calibration/recalibrate.py`; the module lands at
`src/tbox_finder/calib/recalibrate.py` because a `calib/` package already exists and two
near-homonymous calibration namespaces is a permanent confusion. imp.md's `calibration/` paths
have drifted once already on their own — `calibration/ece.py::binned_ece` shipped as
`metrics.py::binned_ece` at P0-31 — and P3-02 carries an identically-shaped recorded
correction. The P3-07 block in imp.md now records this one.

**Validation.** `test_recalibrate` **108 pass**, `test_temperature` 81 pass (unchanged), full
unit tier 3,125 pass with the same 12 failures the untouched `main` shows in this runner (a
py3.11/numpy-2.4.2 local env, not the pinned CI stack); ruff 0.15.15 + black 25.11.0 clean.
**15 source sabotages, each RED against its NAMED test, each restored byte-identically** (fold
sense inverted, emptiness guard removed, unknown-token refusal removed, `is_missing` weakened
to `is None`, P3-02 invariant dropped, shift direction inverted, `+` flipped to `−`, gated key
repointed at the shifted posterior, a deployment prior given a default, the half-specified
guard removed, the PRD band widened to swallow D7's `100:1`, the branch-wise sigmoid replaced
by the overflowing one, single-class guard removed, priors of exactly 0/1 admitted,
`prior_from_odds_ratio` inverted).

**Decisions.** No new ADR and no §7 item-2 sign-off: D11 pins the stack order and the named
posterior, both of which this implements verbatim, and the one value that would have needed a
pin is the one the module refuses to supply. **Commit.** Feature branch
`p3-07-calibration-stack`; squash SHA derived at the phase-exit gate.

## Step P3-07 (review r1) — 2026-08-03: two fail-open guards, and a boolean parse that was already written

**Two review sources, deduplicated to six fixes.** CodeRabbit r1 on `88879fd` returned 1
actionable + 1 nitpick; a 44-agent adversarial pass over the same diff returned 20 findings, 10
surviving two independent refuters. The overlap is the interesting part: **both** independently
found the same defect at the `int64` cast, from opposite directions.

**Fix 1 — the "labels must be binary 0/1" guard was vacuous.** It ran *after*
`y.astype(np.int64)`, which truncates toward zero, so the check saw only what the cast had
already produced. Demonstrated, not argued: `temperature_scale(z=[1,1,−1], y=[1.0, 0.4, 0.6])`
**succeeds** and returns `T = 1.4427030259199125`, bit-identical to the fit for `[1,0,0]` — a
target the caller wrote as `0.6` was silently scored a negative. A `NaN` label cast to the
int64 sentinel and surfaced as `range [-9223372036854775808, 1]`, a message pointing at the
wrong problem. The domain check now happens in the original dtype: booleans and integers pass,
floats must be finite and integral, any other dtype is refused by name.

**Fix 2 — `bool(calib)` closed the NaN hole and left the string hole open.** The guard existed
*because* pandas 3 delivers a null as `NaN` and `bool(nan) is True`; one step further out,
`bool("False")` and `bool("0")` are also `True`. A string-typed `calib` column would therefore
promote its explicit **negatives** into the set `T` is fitted on, with every count agreeing.
Reproduced end to end: `rung_labels(calib=["True","False",…], …)` returned `["calib"]*6`.

**And the fix for it was already in the repo, which is the actual lesson.**
`stage2/train.py::_bool_or_none` is exactly this parse — tri-state, `masking.is_missing`-based,
`{"true","1"}/{"false","0"}`, raising on anything else — written for the fold columns and
documented as also reading `calib`. It could not be imported here (that module is
torch-adjacent; this one is deliberately numpy-only), so the parse was **promoted down** to
`masking.py`, beside the `is_missing`/`row_text` it completes, with `NULL_TOKENS` moving with
it. `stage2.heads.NULL_TOKENS` is now a re-export and `stage2.train._bool_or_none` a
delegation: one vocabulary, one parse, three call sites. Writing a fourth copy here would have
been the cheaper diff and the wrong one
([[promote-dont-duplicate-is-a-correctness-rule]]).

**Fixes 3–6, all test-side, all found by sabotage rather than by reading.** (3) The
single-class guard is a **disjunct**, `n_pos == 0 or n_pos == n_fitted`, and only the
all-positive half was tested — with the other half deleted, an all-negative calib carve (the
realistic P3-02 join failure) returns a **cleanly converged, fully certified** `T`. Both halves
are now parametrized. (4) `test_shape_and_domain_violations_raise` used a bare
`pytest.raises(ValueError)`, and both of this module's own guards could be deleted with the
test still green, because the delegated fitter raises its own differently-worded error further
in; it now matches on this module's text. (5) The empty-calib refusal asserted only its first
clause, leaving the census and the `GRADED_RUNGS` count — the only place that constant is read
— unchecked; all three are asserted. (6) The payload's `source_prior`/`target_prior` were
written and never read, so **swapping the two assignments left the suite green** while emitting
an artifact that recorded the deployment prior as the calib prevalence.

**One finding fixed by deletion.** The docstring cited the known-prior closed form as "Elkan
2001, Theorem 1"; a reviewer put it at Theorem 2 (Theorem 1 being the cost-threshold result).
The numbering could not be verified against the paper from here, so the theorem number is
**gone** rather than guessed — a citation pointing at the wrong theorem is worse than one
pointing at the paper, and the DOI'd Saerens reference is the traceable half anyway.

**Not fixed, with reasons.** Ten findings were refuted by their own verifiers and are recorded
rather than acted on — among them "the calib certificate is self-referential and vacuous"
(refuted: the selection is by identity against `CALIB_RUNG`, and the inversion test asserts the
swapped fit equals the test arm's own `T`), "`RUNG_VOCABULARY` is not closed because `.strip()`
admits padded tokens" (`" calib "` is a legitimate parquet spelling of `calib`; `"  "` is
refused), and a naming divergence between this module's flat `stack_order` and
`temperature.py`'s nested one (the two artifacts have no coupling path and different
validators).

**Validation.** `test_recalibrate` **138 pass** (was 108); `test_temperature` 81,
`test_masking` + `test_stage2_heads` + `test_stage2_train_smoke` 411 pass together — the
promotion is behaviour-preserving on both sides. Full `unit+golden+ml` tier: the worktree's 14
failures are a **strict subset** of the 31 that untouched `main` produces in this local runner
(py3.11 / numpy 2.4.2, the only local env with pytest), i.e. zero regressions; CI runs the
pinned stack. ruff 0.15.15 + black 25.11.0 clean. **24 source sabotages, each RED against its
NAMED test, each restored byte-identically** (up from 15; the nine new ones cover the strict
boolean parse, all three label-domain branches, both halves of the single-class disjunct,
`GRADED_RUNGS`, the payload prior swap, the payload provenance, and the 1-D logits guard).

**Commit.** Feature branch `p3-07-calibration-stack`; squash SHA derived at the phase-exit gate.

## Step P3-07 (review r2) — 2026-08-03: one finding, and the GitHub check that lied about it

**The gate check said `pass`; no review had run.** After the r1 push, the `CodeRabbit` PR check
went green with the body *"Review rate limited"*, and `pulls/100/reviews` showed exactly one
review, on the **step** commit — `a721d06` was unreviewed. This is the CLAUDE.md §5.1 trap
verbatim: a rate-limit notice is an **absence**, not a pass. Rung 1 of the ladder — the
CodeRabbit **CLI**, a separate path from the throttled GitHub app — ran the round instead,
scoped with `--committed --base-commit 88879fd` to the six files r1 actually touched.

**One minor finding, and it is right.** `masking.bool_or_none` — the parse r1 had just promoted
— stringifies before matching, so a **float** flag becomes `"1.0"`/`"0.0"`, matches no spelling,
and raises. That looked at first like correct fail-closed behaviour on a schema fault, until the
shape was checked: `pd.Series([True, None, False]).astype(float)` and a `boolean`-dtype cast to
float64 **both** produce `1.0 / nan / 0.0`. The NaN was already the missing case; the `1.0` and
`0.0` beside it are a well-formed nullable-boolean column, and refusing them aborts a legitimate
run. So the parse now accepts a **finite Real equal to exactly 0 or 1** before the text path.
`0.5`, `1.5`, `-0.5`, `2` and `-1` still raise — they are schema faults and nothing about this
widening touches them.

**Note the inherited-behaviour point.** This was not introduced by P3-07: it is the behaviour
`stage2/train.py::_bool_or_none` has had since P3-06, now visible because the parse moved to a
shared home and got read by a reviewer. Fixing it once fixes it for the fold readers too, which
is the whole argument for having promoted it rather than forked it.

**Validation.** `test_recalibrate` **146 pass**; `test_masking` + `test_stage2_heads` +
`test_stage2_dataset` + `test_stage2_train_smoke` + `test_temperature` + `test_no_leakage` = 502
pass beside it. Full `unit+golden+ml`: **14 failures, still a strict subset of `main`'s 31** in
this runner — `comm -13` over the two `^FAILED` sets is empty, so zero new failures, asserted
rather than eyeballed. ruff + black clean. **Two more sabotages, both bitten and both
directions**: removing the acceptance turns the float test red, and widening it to *any* finite
real (so `0.5` reads `True`) turns the refusal test red — a one-sided sabotage would have missed
the second, which is the failure that actually matters here.

**Commit.** Feature branch `p3-07-calibration-stack`; squash SHA derived at the phase-exit gate.

## Step P3-08 — 2026-08-03: with/without-aux ablation on the calibrated Stage-2 binary head

**Inputs.** The six P3-06 LoRA checkpoints under `data/processed/checkpoints/stage2_rinalmo/`
(the ablation pair is the shipped-config production arm `aux1.0_lr1e-4` and its
learning-rate-matched control `aux0.0_lr1e-4`); `data/processed/stage2_dataset.parquet`
(30,542 rows; calib 1,089 / val 3,067 / test 3,045); the P3-07 calibration stack; and
`metrics.binned_ece` / `average_precision` / `block_bootstrap_ci`.

**Process.** This step had to build the thing it was specified to consume. Nothing in the
repo read a Stage-2 checkpoint back — `stage2_heads.pt` and `lora_adapter/` had write sites
and zero readers, and `stage2/train.py::evaluate` thresholds `tbox_logit` at zero and keeps
only a scalar accuracy — so the per-row binary logits the calibration stack eats did not
exist. `src/tbox_finder/stage2/eval.py` therefore ships the **score producer**
(`load_stage2_checkpoint`, `score_rows`) alongside the ablation entry
(`aux_ablation_check`). Both arms were scored forward-only on the laptop RTX 4060 over all
7,201 calib+val+test rows, 12 min 33 s wall for the pair, and the per-row logits are written
to `reports/p3/stage2_scores.json` because P3-09 and P3-10 need exactly that table and it
costs GPU minutes to regenerate. Temperature is fitted on `calib` and nowhere else, and the
grading rung is `test` per ADR-0004 A7.

**Outputs.** `src/tbox_finder/stage2/eval.py`; `reports/stage2_aux_ablation.json`;
`reports/p3/stage2_scores.json` (7,201 rows x 2 arms); `tests/unit/test_aux_ablation_check.py`
(62 pass, no torch); `tests/ml/test_stage2_eval_smoke.py` (12 pass on the pinned ml-rna stack).

**Validation.** `gate.overall_pass` is **false**, and that is the result rather than a
failure to deliver. The with-aux production arm fits `T = 1.140627` and grades an
in-distribution ECE of **0.005662** on the named (temperature-scaled, pre-prior-shift)
posterior — 8.8x under the ADR-0005 D11 gate of 0.05 — while the **no-aux arm has no
temperature at all**: its calib carve is *perfectly separated* (0 of 1,089 rows on the wrong
side of zero), so the exact minimiser is the beta to infinity limit and `fit_temperature`
refuses it. Two clauses are false in consequence
(`in_distribution_ece_is_computable`, `temperature_positive_and_converged`) and no number was
put where the missing ECE would have gone. On the axis that survives, test AUPRC is 0.999824
with-aux against 0.999897 no-aux, a difference of 7.4e-5.

**Decisions.** Three, all recorded rather than taken. (1) The imp.md gate grades degradation
"beyond a pre-registered tolerance" and **no such tolerance exists** anywhere in `PRD.md`, the
ADRs, `conf/` or `src/`; ADR-0005 D16's own sentence admits an absolute reading (with-aux must
still hold the D11 grade — it does) and a delta reading (tau undefined). Both are computed,
neither is resolved, and `ablation.verdict` is `requires_signoff`. (2) AUPRC is graded on
logits, not on the posterior: `z -> z/T` is strictly monotone so it cannot move average
precision, but sigma() saturates to exactly 1.0 at these margins and would tie the ranking
away. (3) The adapter load is *measured* — every adapter and head tensor is compared
bit-exactly against the file and non-zero `lora_B` blocks are counted — because PEFT only
*warns* on missing keys and initialises `lora_B` to zero, so a silently-unloaded adapter is
the untuned backbone producing a complete and meaningless report.

**Caveat carried forward.** The with-aux fit rests on **exactly one** misclassified calib row
of 1,089. That single record is the entire signal for beta; without it the production arm
would be unfittable too, and P3-10's GATE-2 grade currently hangs on it. Median absolute
logit is 8.26 with-aux against 14.45 no-aux, which is the mechanism: the aux terms shrink the
head's margins and are what keep it calibratable at all.

**Commit.** Feature branch `p3-08-aux-ablation`; squash SHA derived at the phase-exit gate.

### P3-08 review round 1 (CodeRabbit CLI) — 5 findings, all real, all fixed

The GitHub app's `CodeRabbit` check went **green carrying only a "Review rate limited" notice**,
which is an absence rather than a pass (CLAUDE.md §5.1); the gate was met instead by the
**CLI** path, `coderabbit review --committed --base main`. Note for future sessions: `--plain`
was removed in CLI 0.7.1 and now exits 1 with a usage dump, which reads exactly like a dead
path — CLAUDE.md's documented invocation was stale and has been corrected.

**The finding that changed a reported result.** `reading_absolute.passes` was set to `None`
whenever *either* arm lacked an ECE — but the absolute reading of D16 asks only whether the
**with-aux** arm still holds the D11 grade, and that arm has an ECE. The run therefore had a
definite verdict all along: **the absolute reading PASSES** (0.005662 vs the 0.05 gate). The
delta reading remains undecidable, which is a property of the control, not of the production arm.

**Two guards that were only accidentally correct.** (1) The cluster-presence test was
`isinstance(raw, float)`; `np.float64` satisfies it and today's column happens to be float64,
but a float32 NaN would have been read as *clustered*, keyed `cluster:nan`, and collapsed
every unrelated decoy into one bootstrap block — the exact failure `block_keys` exists to
prevent, reintroduced by a type check. The value is now normalised before the NaN test and a
non-numeric id is refused by name. (2) `auprc_rank_invariant` compared two floats for exact
equality. `z / T` is strictly monotone in exact arithmetic but only *non-decreasing* in
float64, so a rounding collision could flip a gate clause with no ranking loss behind it. The
invariant is now stated directly — scaling created no ties — with the tie count and the AP
delta recorded beside it.

**A leak, in a public repo.** The committed artifacts embedded absolute developer paths
(`/home/...`), permanently publishing the OS user name and local layout for paths that resolve
on exactly one machine. Now repo-relative, with the sha256 beside each path carrying the
identity. The first version of that fix **broke the run**: relativising the path the loader
*opens* is not the same job as relativising the path the report *records*, and the two are now
separate fields.

**Two of the five fixes were initially UNTESTED, and sabotage is what said so.** Reverting the
absolute-reading fix and reverting the tie-count fix both left all 70 tests green. The
absolute-reading case needed a fixture where only the **control** lacks an ECE — the shipped
run's own configuration, which every existing fixture had on the other side. The tie case is
unreachable through `grade_arm` at all, so the check was extracted as `ranking_preserved` and
tested directly on a *found* float64 collision where scaling destroys ranking information
while leaving average precision exactly unchanged. Both sabotages now bite their named test.

**Reproducibility, measured rather than assumed.** Three independent scoring runs of the two
arms produced **bit-identical** logits for all 7,201 rows (`max |delta| = 0`), which is what
the length-sorted deterministic batching is for.

**Validation after r1.** `test_aux_ablation_check` **72 pass**; ml tier **12 pass**;
unit+golden+ml **3,758 passed** with the 14 failures still a strict subset of main's 31
(`comm -13` empty). ruff + black clean. Artifacts carry **zero** absolute paths;
`validate_report` returns clean.

### P3-08 review round 2 (CodeRabbit CLI) — 2 findings, both real, both fixed

**A provenance bug in the fast path.** `scoring.batch_size` recorded the flag *this process*
was invoked with, even when `--scores-from` re-graded logits produced under a different
batching. Batch composition perturbs the bf16 reductions — which is exactly why `score_rows`
sorts deterministically — so the artifact could have documented a batching that never touched
those numbers. It now takes the cached run's own value, and the report says plainly that it
was regraded (`regraded_from_cached_scores`) and from which sidecar.

**A docstring that overclaimed.** `validate_report` said an empty problem list meant the
report was "well-formed **and** passing". It is not: it checks that the recorded clauses match
the re-derived ones and that `overall_pass` agrees with them. The shipped report is honestly
failing *and* fully valid, and conflating the two would invite someone to "fix" a truthful
artifact. Now "well-formed and self-consistent", with a test asserting a deliberately-failing
report still validates.

**The fix was taken as an opportunity to make the shortcut's refusals testable.** The
`--scores-from` reconciliation lived inside `main`, so its guards needed a GPU to reach and had
none of their own tests. It is now `reconcile_cached_scores`, graded in the numpy tier:
mismatched dataset digest, a different row set at the *same count*, and a missing arm are each
refused by name. Re-grading a stale cache is the one failure this shortcut can introduce and
the one that would look most like success — seconds instead of minutes, a complete report, and
numbers belonging to different rows.

**Validation after r2.** `test_aux_ablation_check` **78 pass**; ml tier **12 pass**;
unit+golden+ml **3,766 passed**, the 14 failures still a strict subset of main's 31
(`comm -13` empty). ruff + black clean. Artifact regenerated: 0 absolute paths,
`validate_report` clean, headline numbers unchanged. **3 further sabotages**, each RED against
its named test, each restored byte-identically.

### P3-08 review round 3 (CodeRabbit CLI) — 2 findings, both real, both fixed

**A docstring pointing at a key that does not exist.** The module docstring told a reader to
look for `ablation.verdict_delta_reading`; the report writes `ablation.reading_delta.verdict`.
A pointer that does not grep is worse than none, because it reads as authoritative.

**The leak guard was Linux-only.** The end-to-end check greped for `/home/`, so an artifact
regenerated on macOS (`/Users/...`) or Windows (`C:\Users\...`) would have passed it while
leaking exactly what the guard exists to catch. It now walks the JSON and asserts that **no
string value is absolute at all** — structural rather than a list of prefixes, since what makes
a path a leak is that it is absolute, not which OS produced it. The detector carries its own
non-vacuity test (planted paths of all three shapes must be found, a relative path must not),
and the widened check was verified by planting a `/Users/...` path in the real artifact: it
goes red, where the previous `/home/` grep would have stayed green.

**Validation after r3.** `test_aux_ablation_check` **79 pass**; unit+golden+ml unchanged at
3,766+ with zero regressions; ruff + black clean; artifact regenerated and clean.

### P3-08 review round 4 (CodeRabbit CLI) — 1 finding, real, fixed

**An operator-precedence bug in the refusal classifier.** `_classify_refusal` read
`"no rows" in text or "zero" in text and "calib" in text`; Python binds `and` tighter than
`or`, so the first disjunct stood alone and **any** "no rows" refusal was labelled
`empty_calib_rung` — including one raised about a *graded* rung, which has nothing to do with
calib. The branch name claims calib under both readings, so both readings must require it.
Now parenthesised, with a table-driven test over all five refusal shapes plus a control, and
sabotage-verified: reverting the parentheses turns exactly the `'test'`-rung case red.

**Validation after r4.** `test_aux_ablation_check` **85 pass**; unit+golden+ml **3,773
passed**, the 14 failures still a strict subset of main's 31 (`comm -13` empty). ruff + black
clean. CI green on the pinned stack across all three jobs.

### P3-08 §7 stops — SETTLED by user sign-off (AskUserQuestion, 2026-08-03)

**Decision 1 — the absolute reading of D16 governs.** D16 asks whether the aux heads degrade
"the calibrated primary head's GATE-2 grade", and that grade (D11) is a pass/fail: ECE ≤ 0.05.
The check is therefore whether the with-aux arm still *holds* it — which it does, at 0.005662.
**No tau is pinned and no ADR is amended.** The delta against the no-aux arm stays reported,
not gated; `reading_delta.tolerance` remains `None` and `validate_report` still refuses any
report that pins one. Both readings are still computed and the tau-window on which they would
disagree is still published, because a decision is only auditable beside the alternative it
rejected. `ablation.verdict` is now **derived** from the governing reading's own evidence by
`verdict_from_absolute_reading` and re-derived by the validator, so a report cannot carry a
verdict its numbers contradict.

**The ablation's answer: `aux_does_not_degrade_the_gate2_grade`.**

**Decision 2 — accept and record the uncalibratable control now; pin the degenerate-limit rule
at the phase-exit gate.** The no-aux arm's perfectly-separated calib carve is reported as
measured, with no temperature invented. `gate.overall_pass` stays **false**, and the report now
says explicitly what that does *not* mean: it is not evidence that the aux heads degraded
anything, it is the recorded consequence of the *control* being uncalibratable. ADR-0005 D11
gains a degenerate-limit rule at P3 exit, because P3-10 grades GATE-2 and will meet the same
fact — and the option of enlarging or re-stratifying the calib carve until a misclassified row
appears was rejected as choosing the measurement to obtain the answer.

**Validation after the sign-off.** `test_aux_ablation_check` **86 pass**; ml tier **12 pass**;
unit+golden+ml **3,774 passed**, the 14 failures a strict subset of main's 31 (`comm -13`
empty). ruff + black clean. Artifact regenerated: `validate_report` clean, 0 absolute paths,
headline numbers unchanged.

### P3-08 review round 5 (CodeRabbit CLI) — 2 findings, both real, both fixed

**A census that returned a fake zero.** `separation_census` returned 2 keys on an empty rung
and 10 on a populated one, so a consumer reading `is_perfectly_separated` off the committed
report would hit a `KeyError` — and the empty path is *reachable*, because `grade_arm` records
`calib_separation` even when the fit refused **because the calib rung was empty**. Worse,
`n_misclassified_at_zero: 0` on an unmeasured rung reads exactly like a measured result, which
is the same substitution this module refuses to make for `ece`. Both paths now return the same
key set, with `None` for everything that was not measured.

**No validation at the boundary where JSON becomes numbers.** `ArmScores` is built from an
external file by `reconcile_cached_scores`, and a nested list satisfies the length check (an
`(n, k)` array has `len n`) while a NaN or Infinity would flow all the way to the fit before
anything objected — far from the file that carried it. Shape and finiteness are now checked
where the data enters.

**Validation after r5.** `test_aux_ablation_check` **91 pass**; ml tier **12 pass**;
unit+golden+ml **3,779 passed**, the 14 failures a strict subset of main's 31 (`comm -13`
empty). ruff + black clean. **2 further sabotages**, each RED against its named test, each
restored byte-identically.

## Step P3-09 — 2026-08-04: the binned-ECE certification + the small-N-robust OOD-ECE estimator with block-bootstrap CIs

**Inputs.** `metrics.{reliability_bins, binned_ece, block_bootstrap_ci}` (P0-31);
`coverage.OOD_ECE_MIN_N = 20` (P0-27 / ADR-0005 Amendment A2); `masking.{is_missing,
NULL_TOKENS}`; `splits.{FOLD_SCHEME_COLUMNS, COMMITTED_TABLE_COLUMNS}` (drift-guard only).
**Process.** ADR-0005 D13 asks for a small-N-robust OOD estimator **distinct** from D11's
binned one, and imp.md asks for the shared block resampler at
`eval/resample.py::block_bootstrap`. Both roadmap symbols already existed under other names:
`binned_ece` shipped at P0-31 and `block_bootstrap` shipped as `metrics.block_bootstrap_ci`.
Neither was re-implemented. The resampler was **moved** to its roadmap home
(`src/tbox_finder/eval/resample.py`) with `metrics.block_bootstrap_ci` left as a one-line
delegation, and `binned_ece` is **re-exported** from the new `src/tbox_finder/calib/ece.py`,
so imp.md's `{binned_ece, ood_ece}` pair is importable from one place with one implementation
behind it. The genuinely new code is `ood_ece` — a leave-one-out **Beta-kernel**
Nadaraya–Watson estimate of `ĝ(p) = E[y|p]`, from which both of D13's admissible forms are
read off the same `ĝ`: the smoothed/kernel `L1` calibration error (the reported number) and
the proper-scoring-rule Brier/Bregman decomposition (reported beside it with its residual).
The disjunction D13 states is therefore satisfied without choosing one branch on the ADR's
behalf. Also new: `blocks_by_key`, which builds resampling blocks from a **named** split
column and refuses the record-identifier columns by name — before this, "resamples at block
granularity" was a property of each call site, and nothing in the repo could refuse a
record-keyed grouping.
**Outputs.** `src/tbox_finder/eval/resample.py` (`block_bootstrap`, `blocks_by_key`,
`BLOCK_GRANULARITY_COLUMNS`, `RECORD_LEVEL_COLUMNS`); `src/tbox_finder/calib/ece.py`
(`ood_ece`, `kernel_conditional_mean`, `select_bandwidth`, `brier_decomposition`);
`masking.is_null_token` (promoted; `stage2.heads._is_null_token` now delegates);
`tests/unit/test_ece.py` (42), `tests/unit/test_block_bootstrap.py` (21),
`tests/ml/test_eval_gate.py` (+2). No report artifact and no DVC object — P3-09 ships
estimators; the graded artifact is P3-10's.

**The measurement that decided the design.** Nothing is unbiased at N = 20, so the direction
of each candidate's bias was measured (40 seeded replicates per cell, uniform posteriors,
against a known truth) rather than assumed:

| estimator | calibrated, truth 0.000 | | | squashed T=2.5, truth 0.123 | | |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| | n=20 | n=50 | n=200 | n=20 | n=50 | n=200 |
| kernel plug-in | 0.132 | 0.098 | 0.051 | 0.153 | 0.106 | 0.100 |
| kernel + debias | 0.053 | 0.039 | 0.017 | 0.077 | 0.051 | 0.063 |
| binned + debias (D11) | 0.068 | 0.048 | 0.024 | 0.065 | 0.062 | 0.060 |
| binned plug-in | 0.280 | 0.175 | 0.085 | 0.337 | 0.220 | 0.146 |

Two things follow. **A binned estimator cannot be used at the D13 unit**: 15 equal-mass bins
over 20 rows read **0.280 on perfectly calibrated data**, 5.6× the GATE-2 threshold, purely
from binning noise — the concrete form of the published result and the reason A2 specifies an
estimator that needs no per-bin fills. And **debiasing buys a lower floor by destroying the
magnitude**: on genuinely miscalibrated data both debiased columns saturate at ~0.06
regardless of N against a truth of 0.123, i.e. they converge to about half the real drift.
Since D13 compares the reported OOD ECE against a *pinned drift bound*, the magnitude is the
quantity — so `ood_ece` reports the **plug-in**, whose bias is upward, decays with N, and is
conservative in the direction that matters (over-stating drift makes a "calibrated-negative
PASS" harder to earn, never easier).

**A finding this step records but does not resolve.** The same table shows the *gated* D11
estimator saturating at ~0.060 against a truth of 0.123. `metrics.binned_ece`'s docstring
already flags "final certification of the debiasing term is a P3-exit / ADR concern"; this is
measured evidence for that pending decision, not a change to it. **No D11 behaviour moved
here** and GATE-2 is still graded at P3-10 on the estimator as it stands.

**Validation.** `test_ece` 42 + `test_block_bootstrap` 21 + `test_eval_gate` 12 = **72 pass**;
`test_masking` + `test_stage2_heads` + `test_gate4_metrics` + `test_recalibrate` +
`test_coverage_sim` pass alongside, so the `masking` promotion and the resampler move are
behaviour-preserving on both sides. Full unit+golden+ml in the worktree: **3,841 passed / 14
failed**, and the 14 are **exactly** the failures a matched baseline worktree at `main`
produces (`comm -13` empty, `comm -23` empty — a like-for-like comparison in a second
worktree, because the main checkout's data state differs and gives 31). ruff 0.15.0 + black
25.11.0 clean; `snakemake --lint` clean. **20 source sabotages, each RED against its NAMED
test, each restored byte-identically with `__pycache__` cleared both ways.**

**Decisions.** (1) *Path drift, recorded not silently taken* — imp.md names
`calibration/ece.py`; the module lands at **`calib/ece.py`**, inside the package P2-13
created, on the P3-07 precedent (two near-homonymous calibration namespaces is a permanent
import confusion). (2) *Promote, don't fork* — the resampler moved rather than being copied,
which makes any "metrics agrees with resample" test a tautology, so every check is a
hand-computed value or a structural property of the draw. (3) *The min-N floor has no
override* — `ood_ece` reads `coverage.OOD_ECE_MIN_N` directly and exposes **no** keyword for
it, because A2 froze it in code precisely so no committed report could contradict the pin; a
test flips the constant to prove the boundary tracks it. (4) *Below the floor the estimate is
withheld from the graded key* — `ood_ece` is `None`, the value is recorded under
`inadmissible_point`, and no CI is computed, so a consumer cannot grade a number the ADR says
supports no verdict. (5) *No estimator hyperparameter is claimed as ADR-pinned* — bandwidth,
its selection rule, the L1 exponent and the plug-in choice are recorded in the payload and
flagged as implementer choices, the same standing as `binned_ece`'s debias term
(cross-ref ADR-0005 D11/D13/A2).

**One sabotage did not bite, and the gap was real.** Deleting `ood_ece`'s own `n < 2` raise
left `test_length_and_size_guards` green: the call fell through to `kernel_conditional_mean`,
whose guard raises a message containing the same words, and `pytest.raises` is satisfied by
*any* matching raise. Both guards are now matched on the message that names their own
function.

**Evidence gate (CLAUDE.md §10.1).** Binned-ECE small-sample bias [arXiv:2012.08668]; binning
sample-inefficiency [arXiv:1909.10155]; kernel calibration-error estimators applicable to
small samples [arXiv:2210.07810]; the proper-calibration-error decomposition [arXiv:2312.08589];
boundary-bias-free Beta kernels on the unit interval [DOI:10.1016/S0167-9473(99)00010-9]. All
accessed 2026-08-04.

### P3-09 review rounds (CodeRabbit CLI) — the GitHub check was green and empty

The GitHub `CodeRabbit` check read **pass** carrying only the Fair-Usage *"Review rate
limited"* notice, which CLAUDE.md §5.1 classes as an **absence**, not a pass. The gate was
carried by the CLI (`coderabbit review --committed --base main`), the path independent of
the throttled app. No Greptile credit spent.

**r1 — 1 finding, real.** `block_bootstrap` filtered replicates with `not isnan`, so an
`inf` replicate entered the list, dragged `upper` to infinity, and was still counted in
`n_boot` — which the docstring says counts *finite* replicates. Reproduced by execution
before accepting (`{'point': 2.0, 'upper': inf, 'n_boot': 50}`) and fixed to `isfinite`. No
committed CI moves: every statistic resampled in this repo is bounded. This was inherited
P0-31 behaviour; making the contract explicit is what exposed it.

**r2 — 4 findings.** ⚠ *Two were read late*: the CLI output was inspected while it was still
being written, and the first read showed only 2. **Read the CLI file only after `Review
complete`.** (1, major) The block-granularity control was weaker than its own docstring:
`_all_blocks_whole` counted *tags* and tested `count % block_size == 0`, so
`[("b",0),("b",0)]` scored as whole — two copies of one row with the other missing. Now
equal multiplicity across each block's own rows, with its own unit test; the record-level
matched control sharpens from **174/200 to 199/200** violations, which is itself evidence
the finding was material. (2) `__module__` does not prove object identity — added an `is`
assertion, sabotage-isolated by rebuilding a distinct `FunctionType` from the same code
object. (3) `ci_level`/`n_boot`/`q` were unvalidated public arguments. (4, major)
**REFUTED:** the review claimed the Brier-closure assertion "will reject a correct
decomposition" at a residual of −0.003265 and proposed replacing the estimator's output
with a constant. Residual measured **3.6e-16 / 5.6e-16 / 5.0e-16** at p = 0.5/0.2/0.9, and
the identity closes *exactly* because `cal + ref = p² − 2p·mean(ĝ) + mean(ĝ)` while
`brier = p² − 2p·(S/n) + S/n`, which agree iff `mean(ĝ) = S/n` — true for LOO with uniform
weights since the sum of `(S − yᵢ)/(n−1)` over i is `S`. The proposed change would also have
removed the estimator from its own test. The test now pins that *mechanism* and checks three
posteriors.

**r3 — 2 findings, both real, and one invalidated a guarantee this step claimed.** (1) The
r2 validation was too loose; `ci_level` is now an open `(0, 1)` fraction (the percentage form
`95` is a real way to land outside) and `n_boot` at least 1, so a reported `n_boot: 0` has
exactly one meaning. (2) The min-N pin was checked with
`ece.OOD_ECE_MIN_N is coverage.OOD_ECE_MIN_N` — **vacuous**, because CPython caches small
integers and a hand-typed `OOD_ECE_MIN_N = 20` satisfies `is` too (verified). It was
therefore blind to precisely the failure it existed to catch, and would have broken for the
*wrong* reason if an amendment moved the pin above 256. Replaced with an AST pin: the name
must be imported from `tbox_finder.coverage` and never re-assigned. Sabotage 25 substitutes
the literal and is now caught.

**Commit.** see PR [#102](https://github.com/bioedca/tbox-finder/pull/102).

## Step P3-10 — 2026-08-04: GATE-2's P3 half — the in-distribution ECE gate on the named posterior, and the leave-clade-out drift read beside it

**Inputs.** `reports/p3/stage2_scores.json` (P3-08; 7,201 rows × 2 arms over the calib/val/test rungs of the random split); `data/processed/stage2_dataset.parquet` (sha256 `376ad12b…` — the split table, because neither scores file carries taxonomy or clustering); `data/processed/checkpoints/stage2_rinalmo/aux1.0_lr1e-4`; `calib.recalibrate` (P3-07), `calib.ece` + `eval.resample` (P3-09), `metrics.binned_ece` (P0-31), `coverage.OOD_ECE_MIN_N = 20` (ADR-0005 A2).
**Process.** `src/tbox_finder/calib/gate2.py` fits `T` on the disjoint `calib` rung through P3-07's `temperature_scale` (which selects those rows itself — no argument here can admit a graded row into the fit), grades the **named** posterior on the `test` rung with the ADR-0005 D11 estimator, and reports two non-gated reads beside it: the deployment-prevalence ECE swept across the PRD's prose `10³–10⁴ : 1` band, and the D13 per-held-out-order OOD ECE with cluster-blocked CIs. `workflow/rules/calibration.smk` carries `stage2_scores_loo` → `gate2_ece` → `plot_gate2_figures`.
**Outputs.** `src/tbox_finder/calib/gate2.py`; `workflow/rules/calibration.smk`; `reports/gate2_p3_ece.json`; `reports/p3/gate2_figure_data.json`; `reports/p3/stage2_scores_loo.json`; `figures/calib/gate2_reliability.png`, `figures/calib/gate2_ood_by_order.png`; `tests/unit/test_gate2.py` (52); the `ood_ece` golden P3-09 deferred here, in `tests/fixtures/eval_gate_sample/expected.json`, with its discriminator in `tests/ml/test_eval_gate.py`; `paper/manuscript.qmd` §`sec-gate2` + `@fig-gate2`.

**GATE-2 (P3 half) PASSES: ECE 0.005662 ≤ 0.05.** Graded on the named posterior — temperature-scaled, **pre** prior-shift — on the `test` rung at its own prevalence (3,045 rows, 2,353 positives, prevalence 0.7727, 2,275 homology clusters), `T = 1.140627` fitted on the 1,089-row `calib` carve. Cluster-blocked bootstrap 95 % CI **[0.002700, 0.009410]** (B = 2,000); the value reproduces P3-08's `reading_absolute.observed_ece` exactly. The **plug-in** ECE is 0.008378 — reported beside the gated value because P3-09 measured the D11 debiasing term to *understate* real error at small n, and both readings clearing 0.05 by an order of magnitude is what makes the pass independent of that concern.

**THE GATED MARGIN IS BIN-CONCENTRATED, AND THE REPORT NOW SAYS SO.** The posterior is near-separated, so under equal-mass binning **12 of the 15 bins carry accuracy exactly 0 or 1** — they hold only rows at `p < 1e-4` or `p > 0.995`, where there is nothing to get wrong — while **one bin spans `p = 4.5e-5` to `0.9956`** (99.6 % of the probability axis) and absorbs the whole transition region. That bin's raw gap is **0.0985**, about twice the gate threshold; at weight 1/15 it contributes **83.1 %** of the reported 0.005662. The pass is honest and its evidence base is narrow — the same shape as the single misclassified calib row. `gate.bin_concentration` records the share, the saturated-bin count and the widest span, and a disclosure quotes the measured share; **nothing is gated on any of it**. The reliability figure draws each bin as a **segment over the range it actually covers** and does **not** join them: joining fifteen centres that sit in two piles plus one bridge draws a smooth, well-sampled-looking curve through probability ranges where nothing was measured.

**THE STEP HAD TO BUILD ITS OWN OOD POPULATION.** P3-08 scored only the random split's three rungs, so of the 30 ADR-0004 D5 leave-one-order-out units only 26 appeared at all and **5** cleared min-N — a coverage number that would have sat in a phase-exit artifact contradicting Amendment A2's *ex ante* 30-unit footprint while reading like a finding about the corpus. `gate2.score-loo` scores the full designated holdout with the production arm, reusing `stage2.eval`'s loader and scorer rather than a second implementation: **9,345 rows, 30 orders, 8,641 positives, all 30 clearing the floor.** ~28 min on the laptop 4060 at batch 4, flash-attention-2, the backend the arm trained under.

**Its OOD-ness is measured, not assumed, and one of the two checks is invisible at row level.** Re-deriving P3-06's admission predicate from the split table reproduces **9,059** training rows (4,795 pos / 4,264 neg) exactly, and against it the holdout has **0 shared rows** and — the check a row-level test cannot see — **0 shared orders** (19 trained orders vs 30 held-out, disjoint). `score_loo_holdout` refuses to run if either is non-zero: a clade the model has seen, scored under an "OOD" label, is a fabricated drift measurement.

**THE DRIFT IS PHYLUM-STRUCTURED, AND THE MACRO-AVERAGE DESCRIBES NEITHER MODE.** Macro-average OOD ECE **0.2113** (95 % CI [0.0984, 0.3250], blocked on the held-out order). Per unit it is cleanly bimodal:

| group | orders | OOD ECE range |
|---|---:|---|
| **Actinobacteria** (Pseudonocardiales, Propionibacteriales, Micromonosporales, Micrococcales, Streptomycetales, Streptosporangiales, Actinomycetales, Bifidobacteriales, Corynebacteriales) | 9 | **0.5923 – 0.7991** |
| everything else (Firmicutes, Tenericutes, Chloroflexi, Deinococcus-Thermus, Synergistetes, Proteobacteria) | 21 | **0.0007 – 0.1151** |

The two sets **do not overlap**, and every high-drift order is Actinobacteria (9/9); no non-Actinobacteria order exceeds 0.115. Against a ~90 %-Firmicutes training corpus, calibration fails at the phylum boundary rather than degrading smoothly with rank — which is PRD §12's ECE-vs-phylogenetic-distance read arriving as a step function. The report therefore carries `ood.by_phylum`, a **descriptive regrouping** of the same per-unit estimates (no pooled phylum-level estimate, no CI, no verdict — pooling would let the largest order speak for its phylum). It also vindicates the macro-average rule: *Lactobacillales* alone is **61.6 %** of held-out positives and is itself calibrated to **0.0034**, so a row-weighted summary would have reported near-perfect transfer while nine orders sat two orders of magnitude worse.

**Nothing unpinned was quietly pinned, and two values had to stay unpinned.** (1) **D13 condition (i)'s drift bound does not exist** — absent from `PRD.md`, ADR-0005, ADR-0006, `conf/` and `src/`, and D18's delegation map assigns only the min-N floor (A2). So the report answers condition (ii) per unit, records (i) as unpinned and (iii) as a P4 quantity, and leaves `calibrated_negative_pass` as `null`: a verdict from two of three conditions reads exactly like one from three. `validate_report` **refuses** a report that pins a bound or decides the verdict. (2) **No deployment prior is pinned** — the `~10³–10⁴ : 1` prevalence is prose only (PRD §11), so the prior-shifted ECE is swept across the band's endpoints plus its geometric interior (**0.5642 / 0.6814 / 0.7372**) and `validate_report` refuses a `pinned_target_prior`. Both are the shape P3-07 used for π_deploy and P3-08 for τ; pinning either is a new blinded-frozen default needing §7 sign-off.

**Two defects the shipped path had, both found by running it rather than reading it.** (1) `build_provenance` **hashes** every path in `outputs`, and neither output exists when it is called — the first full run would have died at the last line after ~40 min of bootstrapping. Outputs are now recorded as declared *names* under `extra`; hashing a report from inside itself is impossible anyway. (2) `prior_shift` returns shifted **logits** (deliberately — the correction is exactly additive there), and feeding them to `binned_ece` as probabilities produced a reported "ECE" of **6.29**. The sweep now routes through the shipped `calibrated_posterior`, and a guard refuses any value outside `[0, 1]`. A cheap `--max-units 3 --ood-n-boot 5` dry run of the *whole* entry point is what surfaced both ([[verify-the-line-you-ship]]).

**`is_science` is derived, not asserted.** GATE-4's report can hardcode it because its incomplete path raises and writes no file; this one always writes, so `--max-units` would otherwise land a truncated grade at the phase-exit path flagged as real science. It is now the conjunction of the three completeness clauses, re-derived by `validate_report`, and two sabotages (hardcoding it; reading only one of the three) are caught.

**Validation.** `reports/gate2_p3_ece.json` re-validates **clean** under the shipped code with all 19 clauses re-deriving identically and `overall_pass = true`. 66 `test_gate2` + the extended eval-gate tier; full unit+golden+ml **3,912 passed / 14 failed**, the 14 **exactly** a matched baseline worktree's set at `main` (`comm` empty both ways — the main checkout gives a different count because it holds the LFS/DVC data a fresh worktree lacks, so the baseline had to be a second worktree). ruff 0.15.0 + black 25.11.0 + `snakemake --lint` clean; `snakemake -n gate2_ece` resolves `stage2_dataset → stage2_scores_loo → gate2_ece`. **64 sabotages, each RED against its NAMED test, each restored byte-identically.** Two did not bite on the first pass and both gaps were real: an all-TRUE fixture made `overall_pass = all(clauses)` and `overall_pass = True` indistinguishable (now checked on a report with one clause deliberately FALSE), and the disclosure test matched a phrase that survived deleting the clause that introduced it (now matched on provenance marker *and* substance).

**Decisions.** Path drift, recorded not taken silently: the module lands at `src/tbox_finder/calib/gate2.py`, not imp.md's `calibration/gate2.py` — the same correction as P3-07 and P3-09, since two near-homonymous calibration namespaces is a permanent import confusion. No ADR amended and no §7 sign-off sought: nothing pinned changed. **Three items now stand for the P3-exit ADR round** — D11's missing degenerate-limit rule (P3-08), the D11 debias term's measured saturation (P3-09), and D13's unpinned drift bound (this step).

**Commit.** see PR [#103](https://github.com/bioedca/tbox-finder/pull/103).

### P3-10 review round 1 — CodeRabbit CLI (3 findings) **and** the GitHub app (5), only one in common

Both paths ran: the CLI (`coderabbit review --committed --base main`) and — unsolicited — the
GitHub app, which means automatic review is **enabled** again after being off on 2026-08-03.
The overlap was a single finding, so running both was additive rather than redundant.

**(both, major) The committed report carried this machine's filesystem layout.** Four fields —
two `provenance.extra.declared_outputs`, the `provenance.inputs` key for the LOO scores, and
`scoring.loo_scores` — held absolute paths including the OS user name and a
`.claude/worktrees/p3-10-gate2-ece` checkout, in a **public** repo. The sibling entries beside
them were repo-relative, so the artifact was also un-diffable across machines: a re-run
elsewhere changes an `inputs` *key* without any content changing. Root cause is running from
the main checkout with absolute paths into a linked worktree. Fixed by routing every recorded
path through P3-08's `stage2.eval.repo_relative`, which already relativises against **both**
roots — the repo has three forks of that helper and this step deliberately added no fourth.
`provenance.inputs` keys are normalised *after* hashing, because `build_provenance` must be
handed a path it can actually open. **The report was regenerated, not hand-edited.**

**(app, major) Diverting an invalid report was not enough on a RE-run.** `_output_path` sends a
rejected report to `<name>.invalid.json` but did not remove the canonical path, so a previously
accepted report stayed there with older numbers and older provenance — a stale grade reading as
current, beside a fresh `.invalid.json`. The figure data was worse: written unconditionally to
the path `plot_gate2_figures` consumes, so the two committed artifacts could disagree. Both now
go through one `write_outputs`, divert together, and **unlink the canonical file** when
diverting, so its absence is the signal. Snakemake deletes a failed job's outputs and had been
masking this entirely; only a direct CLI run exposes it.

**A sabotage of the first fix did not bite, and the gap was real.** Reverting `main`'s call site
(`_output_path(args.figure_data, …)` → `Path(args.figure_data)`) left the suite **green**: the
test exercised `_output_path` but never that `main` *used* it. The write is now one
`write_outputs` function so the **pairing** is what is tested, and the sabotage bites.

**(app, minor) The reliability legend claimed one bin's count for every bin.** It read
`rows[0]["n"]` and said "rows each"; equal-**mass** binning only gives equal counts when `n`
divides by 15, which 3,045 happens to do — exactly the coincidence a label should not rest on.
`_bin_size_label` now reports a range unless every bin really matches.

**(app, minor) The eval-gate golden's three detection vectors were never asserted aligned.**
`det_labels` is sized from `len(prod_codes)` and `det_units` from `len(names)` plus the decoys;
one shared index reads all three, and `ood_ece`'s own length check cannot see a misalignment
because `y` and `block_labels` are both derived from the same `keep`. Asserted where the
vectors meet. The reviewer also noted that `n_excluded_no_block == 53` decomposes as 50 + 3
only while none of the 40 sampled dinucleotide sources is one of the 3 null-`order` records —
a property of the decoy **seed**, not of the construction. That decomposition is now asserted
explicitly, so a seed change fails with a readable cause instead of shifting a golden.

**(app, minor) `pytest.importorskip("numpy")` sat below the imports it guarded.** The
`tbox_finder` imports above it already pull numpy, so collection would fail before the guard
could run — it was inert. Removed rather than moved: the module's numpy dependency is hard and
its docstring already says the tier runs in CI's stack rather than skipping itself green.

**(CLI, minor) An observation recorded, NOT acted on.** The reviewer noted that 4 of the 704
leave-clade-out dinucleotide decoys carry positive logits (indices 8763, 8809, 9153, 9332 —
verified), a **0.57 %** decoy false-positive rate at threshold 0, and suggested a dedicated
negative-control FPR criterion. Measured and true; also true is that **864 of the 8,641**
held-out positives (**10.0 %**) sit at non-positive logits, which is the leave-clade-out
*recall* story and belongs to GATE-1 at P4. Adding an FPR criterion would be a **new gate** —
a blinded-frozen default requiring ADR sign-off (CLAUDE.md §7 item 2) — so it is recorded here
and not invented in a calibration step. GATE-2's Phase-3 half grades the D11 in-distribution
ECE on the 3,045 test rows, and nothing else.

### P3-10 review round 2 — CodeRabbit CLI, 6 findings (1 major, 5 minor), all real, all fixed

**The GitHub app did not review this round, and its check went green anyway.** `gh pr checks`
reported `CodeRabbit  pass` with the body *"Review rate limited"* — CLAUDE.md §5.1's trap
verbatim: a rate-limit notice is an **absence**, not a pass. Round 2's gate was carried entirely
by the CLI, the path independent of the throttled app. Across the two rounds the app reviewed
once and the CLI twice, which is the argument for running both rather than either.

**(major) The figure projection dropped the not-gated markers.** `gate2_figure_data.json` holds
`gate: 0.05` and `in_distribution.passes` beside the OOD ECEs, but none of the guards the source
report attaches to those same numbers (`ood.gated`, `why_not_gated`, `by_phylum_is`,
`macro_average_is`). A figure script reading only that file had no field telling it the
leave-clade-out numbers are ungated, so it could draw the 0.05 threshold across a panel where
Actinobacteria's mean is 0.68 and render a **reported** quantity as a gate failure. The guards
now travel with the data.

**(minor, real logic bug) `--max-units` recorded a truncation that did not happen.**
`truncated_to` was set whenever `max_units` was not `None`, so `--max-units 60` on a 30-unit
holdout turned `graded_every_loo_holdout_unit` FALSE while every unit had in fact been graded —
a completeness clause failing on a complete run. Now recorded only when the list was really cut.

**(minor, real inconsistency) The concentration indices broke ties the opposite way from the
test.** `_bin_concentration` compared `(value, index)` tuples, so `sorted(...)[-1]`/`max(...)`
resolved ties toward the **largest** index, while the test asserted `.index(max(...))` — the
**first**. A tie at the maximum is reachable precisely here: 12 of the 15 bins carry a debiased
gap of exactly 0.0. Selection is now by value with `.index()`, so both agree, and a dedicated
tie fixture pins it.

**(minor) A replicate shortfall was recorded without a reason — and chasing it explained the
mechanism exactly.** Two units reported fewer than the requested 200 replicates:
`Desulfuromonadales` 181 and `Pseudonocardiales` 193, both with 3 blocks. The kernel leaves out
by **row**, so a replicate is undefined only when every row shares one uid — i.e. when the draw
came entirely from a **singleton** block. Measured block sizes: `Desulfuromonadales` **[1, 1,
31]**, `Pseudonocardiales` **[1, 2, 49]**. For one singleton in three blocks the chance of
drawing it three times is 1/27 = 3.7 %, i.e. **7.4 of 200 — and Pseudonocardiales lost exactly
7**. Each unit now carries `n_boot_requested`, `n_boot_dropped` and the reason, so an auditor can
tell rejected resamples from a truncated bootstrap.

**A sabotage of that fix did not bite, and the gap was real** — the second time this session.
Replacing `n_boot_requested` with the *survived* count left the suite green, because the fixture
had no singleton block and so never dropped a replicate: `requested == survived` made the two
indistinguishable. The test now builds a 30-row unit with a deliberate singleton (10 of 40
replicates dropped) and asserts the shortfall is non-zero *before* asserting the accounting
closes.

**(minor) The two `schema_version` fields version different schemas.** The report body carries
`"1"` and the nested provenance envelope `"1.0"` (`provenance.SCHEMA_VERSION`); a consumer
comparing them would read a mismatch. They are now declared as different scopes in the artifact
itself rather than left to be inferred.

**(minor) A contradictory legend comment** — one half said "Below the axes", the other "ABOVE";
the code places it above. Stale half removed.

**The OOD test fixture was hand-built, and it had drifted.** Adding a shape check against the
shipped `grade_ood_units` immediately found **six** keys the fixture lacked (`why_not_gated`,
`by_phylum`, `adjudicable_fraction`, `n_boot`, `bootstrap_seed`, `n_units_sub_min_n`) — every
one a field no test resting on that fixture could have been covering. The fixture now *is* the
producer's output, so it cannot drift; the shape check was then dropped as a tautology
([[promote-dont-duplicate-is-a-correctness-rule]]).

**A `figure-data` subcommand was added** so the projection can be re-derived from a committed
report in seconds rather than by re-running the 40-minute leave-one-out bootstrap. It is the
same pure `figure_data(report)` call `grade` makes, and a test pins the two to be
byte-identical.

None touched the report, so no regeneration was needed.

**(minor) The divert was one-directional.** Round 2 made a rejected run remove the canonical

**The counts in `_bin_concentration`'s docstring and comment contradicted the report they

### P3-10 review round 5 — CodeRabbit CLI, 1 minor finding: a falsy zero erased a real outcome

**`or 0.0` treated an OOD ECE of exactly 0.0 as absent.** `plot_figures` selected each unit's

real outcome**, and 0.0 is falsy: its marker would vanish from the panel, its error bar become
NaN, and its sort key collapse onto that of a genuinely missing value. Now tested against

**A sabotage of the fix did not bite — the third time this session — and the gap was the same

selector is now the module-level `ood_point`, and the test calls **it** rather than a copy;

verifies the re-implementation ([[promote-dont-duplicate-is-a-correctness-rule]]).

Verified by hand under the `viz` env (§8.5 manual gate): `plot_figures` renders both PNGs, rc 0,
on a figure-data carrying a 0.0-ECE unit with no CI.

**Five rounds, 19 findings, all real, all fixed.** Rounds 4 and 5 each carried a single minor

### P3-10 review round 6 — CodeRabbit CLI, 1 minor finding: two fields named "singleton", meaning different things

**Both readings of the census were correct, and that was the problem.** The scores file records
`block_census.n_singleton_blocks: 0` while **3,424 of its 4,332 blocks contain exactly one row**.
The field is P3-08's, and under its own definition 0 is right: it counts rows with *no cluster
at all* (`n_rows_without_cluster`, also 0 — every leave-clade-out row is clustered). Under the
natural reading of the name it is wrong by 3,424.

That collision matters here specifically. Round 2 established that a bootstrap replicate is
undefined exactly when it is drawn entirely from a **one-row block**, and recorded
`n_boot_dropped: 19` for `Desulfuromonadales` and `7` for `Pseudonocardiales` on that basis. A
reader cross-referencing the two artifacts would see "0 singleton blocks" beside a non-zero drop
whose stated cause is singleton blocks, and reasonably conclude one of them is wrong.

**Fixed where it bites, not where it originated.** Renaming P3-08's field would touch a
committed report schema and its shape-lock test for a naming issue; instead each unit now
carries `n_blocks_of_size_one` — the count that actually governs its own drop — beside
`n_boot_dropped`, and the drop reason names the field it is *not*. The regenerated report confirms the mechanism across the whole range: `Pseudonocardiales`
**1** one-row block of 3 → 1/27 = 3.7 % → **7** dropped of 200; `Desulfuromonadales` **2**
of 3 → 2/27 = 7.4 % → **19**; and `Lactobacillales`, which has **2,366** one-row blocks but
**2,948** in total, drops **0** — the ratio governs, not the count, which is exactly why a
bare repo-wide singleton total explains nothing on its own.

**Six rounds, 20 findings, all real, all fixed.** The gated number has not moved once: ECE
0.005662 in every regeneration.

### P3-10 review round 7 — CodeRabbit CLI, 1 minor finding: a cache hint could discard a 28-minute run

**`if target != "cpu": torch.cuda.empty_cache()`.** `--device` accepts any string torch
accepts, so `mps` (or `xpu`) is reachable, and on a build without CUDA that call raises. The
raise lands **after** `score_rows` and **before** the payload is written, so the entire ~28
minute leave-clade-out scoring run would be lost to a cache hint. Now gated on
`torch.cuda.is_available() and str(target).startswith("cuda")`, factored into
`_should_release_cuda` so the predicate is testable without a GPU.

This is the same shape as the round-1 provenance defect — an incidental call at the tail of an
expensive function, positioned so its failure discards everything the function just produced.
Two of the three most costly defects this step found were of that kind, and neither is visible
from reading the happy path.

**The same pattern exists in `stage2/eval.py:1809` (P3-08).** Not changed here: it is another
step's module with a committed artifact and a shape-locked report, and the fix belongs with
whoever next regenerates it. Recorded so it is not rediscovered as new.

**Seven rounds, 21 findings, all real, all fixed.** ECE 0.005662 in every regeneration.

## Step P3-11 — 2026-08-04: the frozen D3+A3 reconciliation operator in the P3 integration path

**Inputs.** `src/tbox_finder/infer/reconcile.py::reconcile_windows` (P2-03, the operator ADR-0005 A3 froze in code); `src/tbox_finder/infer/scan.py::scan_window_ids` / `scan_encoded_windows` (P2-10a); `src/tbox_finder/infer/call.py::call_candidates` (P2-10c′-c-i); `data/window_dataset.py::tile_windows` at the pinned `WINDOW_NT = 1024 / STRIDE_NT = 512`; `labels.CLASS_ORDER`.
**Process.** The wiring this step is named for **already existed** — `scan_encoded_windows` ends in `reconcile_windows(logits, np.asarray(starts), seq_len)` (`scan.py:217`), the single tile→forward→reconcile site that `scan_sequence`, `eval/gate4.score_records` and `calib/temperature`'s cross-check all route through, and `call_candidates` already consumes `Reconciled.log_probs` + `zero_flanked`. Rebuilding it here would fork an operator A3 froze precisely so it could not be forked, so the step **certifies the existing path** rather than adding a third composition site — which is what imp.md's own `Artifacts:` line (a test + this stanza, no `src/` module) and its `Rule/Entry:` (the P2 module, "imported here") already specify. `tests/unit/test_reconcile_windows_integration.py` composes tiling → encoding → the operator → the caller and sweeps a locus across one full 512-nt phase period.
**Outputs.** `tests/unit/test_reconcile_windows_integration.py` (66 tests). No `src/` change, no artifact, no ADR amendment, no DVC object.

**The gate passes, and it is a statement about the *call*, not just the posterior.** The same 160-nt locus (100 nt Stem_I + 30 Specifier + 30 Antiterminator) planted at **13 phases** of one 512-nt period — phase 0 puts its 5′ end exactly on a window boundary — yields **one** outcome: the candidate span is `[0, 160)` relative to the locus and `dominant_class` is `Stem_I`, at every phase, under **both** degradation models and at **four** thresholds. The reconciled arg-max is invariant too, compared as the exact per-position class vector over the locus plus 64 nt of carrier either side, which is the quantity `eval/gate4.py` grades boundary IoU on and the one PRD §6 names as the thing that must not be a 512-grid artifact.

**The invariance is not a property of one lucky threshold.** Measured across the whole sweep, the reconciled posterior never falls below **0.5567** on a locus position nor rises above **0.1136** on a carrier position, so every τ in `(0.114, 0.556]` gives the identical call. Four are asserted.

**THE MATCHED CONTROL IS WHAT GIVES THE SWEEP POWER, AND IT WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED.** The control is the naive per-tile stitch — score each position from the one window whose 512-nt tile owns it — with the same sequence, encoder, oracle and caller parameters; only the reduction differs. Over the identical sweep it yields **8 distinct outcomes under each model** against reconciliation's one: truncated loci, and at phases 0/16/480/511 (ramp) **no candidate at all**, and at phase 480 (step) a 64-nt fragment whose dominant element is `Antiterminator_Tbox_seq` rather than `Stem_I` — a locus that would reach Stage 2 with the wrong predicted element, which is exactly what the §6 strand-resolver reads to orient it. Its positive leg is asserted separately: at six phases where the grid happens to be kind the stitch reproduces the reconciled answer exactly, so it is grid-dependent rather than broken by construction.

**TWO FINDINGS THE STEP DID NOT SET OUT TO MAKE, BOTH FOR P3-12.**

1. **Seam-freeness is a property of the doubly-covered interior, and the single-covered part carries no flag.** `tile_windows` is tail-anchored and adds no window past either end, so on a 3,072-nt contig **1,024 positions — the first and last 512 — are covered once**, and the same locus planted in that terminus is *not* phase-invariant (4 distinct calls under `step`, 5 under `ramp`, including a total miss and two misnamed elements). PRD §6 words the claim as *"every **interior** nucleotide"*, so this is the boundary of the claim rather than a violation of it — but nothing marks it downstream: `zero_flanked` fires only for a window that ran off an end, which at this tiling never happens on a contig longer than one window, so the flag is identically `False` there. `Reconciled.coverage` records it; `Candidate` has no coverage field, so a locus called from single-window evidence is indistinguishable from one called from two. Left as a measured limitation rather than a `Candidate` schema change, which would touch a P2 module, its 22 tests and two committed report schemas.

2. **The call is phase-invariant; the reported strength is not.** `mean_p_elem` swings **0.6453 → 0.9997** (step) and **0.5709 → 0.8368** (ramp) across the phase sweep — averaging a truncated-context window in genuinely dilutes the posterior — and `peak_p_elem` is invariant only under hard truncation (under a ramp it moves 0.6078 → 0.8817). Not a defect of the operator, but any later locus rule that thresholds on *mean* (or, under graded degradation, *peak*) locus strength re-imports the 512-grid dependence that thresholding per position does not have.

**Two gaps in this step's own test, both found by sabotage rather than by reading.** (1) The first pad probe's power rested entirely on NaN tripping the operator's non-finite refusal; a **finite** leak raises no guard, and two runs that both leaked the same finite garbage would have agreed with each other and proved nothing. A second `loud` probe (a large finite pad logit) now covers that path, with a liveness assertion that the probe changes the pad logits and nothing else. (2) **D3's arg-max half was not covered at all** — the caller thresholds `1 − P(background)` and never reads `Reconciled.prediction`, so every assertion in the file left the arg-max untouched while `eval/gate4.py` grades boundary IoU on precisely that. Adding its sweep required raising the oracle's element logit clear of `2 × background`: at exactly `2 ×` the two covering windows tie at the ramp's midpoint offset and `np.argmax` resolves the tie to `background` — a fixture artifact that would have read as operator phase-dependence.

**Validation.** 66 tests green. **19 sabotages, 18 RED against their NAMED test, each restored byte-identically (sha256-verified, `__pycache__` cleared between runs); the one no-bite is the harness's own declared no-op control.** They cover the operator (coverage normalisation removed; the ADR-0005 (B) raw-logit reading A3 rejected; the `seq_len` clamp dropped so pads reach the reduction; zero-flank never/always set; coverage pinned to 1; prediction flattened and prediction shifted by one), the caller (zero-flank count dropped; a forked `log_softmax`; `dominant_class` read off a fixed index), the wiring (`window` passed for `seq_len`; the reconcile call moved off the last statement; the operator forked into the scanner), and the fixture's own honesty (degradation switched off; the pad probe neutralised; the phase sweep collapsed; the arg-max flank removed). Neighbouring suites re-run green alongside (`test_reconcile` 56, `test_infer_scan` 14, `test_infer_call` 22, `test_reconcile_golden` 15 — 212 with the new file). ## Step P3-11 (review r1) — 2026-08-04: three findings, all real, and one of them the reviewer under-counted

**Both review paths ran on `059c9d3`.** The **CLI** (`coderabbit review --committed --base main`) returned **`Review complete — No findings`** over both files; the **GitHub app** reviewed **automatically on push** — no `@coderabbitai review` was sent — and returned **3 nitpicks**, all real. Auto-review is therefore **enabled** again on this repo, detected per PR as CLAUDE.md §5.1 requires rather than carried from the last session's reading. The two paths **overlapped on nothing**, the same argument for running both that P3-10 recorded. CI was green throughout (`lint`, `pytest`, `snakemake` all pass; the `pytest` pass is also what confirms the 66 tests import and run in the **bare CI tier**, i.e. the file is genuinely torch-free).

- **The AST guards matched only `ast.FunctionDef`, so one keyword walked past them.** An `async def reconcile_windows` in another module would not have been reported as a fork, and an `async def scan_encoded_windows` would have been reported as *missing* rather than as unwired — a refusal that a keyword evades is not a refusal. Fixed at **three** sites; the review named **two**. Sabotage-verified with a cross-module `async` fork, which now turns `test_exactly_one_module_in_the_tree_defines_the_operator` red. Chasing it also pinned the test's **scope**: it collects the *modules* defining the name, so it owns the cross-module fork, while a second definition inside `reconcile.py` itself is plain shadowing that **`ruff` F811 rejects as a CI-blocking error** — verified by running ruff against a deliberately shadowed copy, not assumed. The docstring now says so, so the boundary is not read as a gap.
- **The stitch control's docstring claimed something false about the tail.** It said every position lands in the left half of its owning window; under tail-anchored tiling there is no window starting at 2560, so positions **2560–3071** fall back to owner 2048 at offsets 512–1023 — the **right** half. Measured: 2,560 left-half positions and exactly the last 512 right-half. The phase sweep lives in `[1024, 1696)`, entirely left-half, so **no assertion moved and no number changed**; the wording was wrong and a later reader could have taken "left half" for an invariant of the tiling. Stated explicitly instead.
- **The element mask assumed `background` holds the lowest class index.** `cls > _BG` selects element positions only while that is true; were `CLASS_ORDER` reordered, every class below background would silently stop receiving `_ELEMENT_LOGIT` and be scored as carrier — the whole file would then measure a **weaker fixture without failing**, which is the failure mode this file exists to avoid in its own subject. Now `(cls >= 0) & (cls != _BG)`. Because that is a **no-op under the shipped ordering**, it came with a test that re-points the oracle at a table where background sits mid-order and a class sits *below* it; the sabotage reverting the mask turns that test red, so the fix is not the kind that gets quietly reverted later for want of evidence.

**Validation.** 67 tests green (66 + the class-ordering test). **21 sabotages, 20 RED against their NAMED test**, each restored byte-identically; the single true no-bite is the harness's own declared no-op control. Neighbouring suites green alongside (213 with this file). ruff 0.15.0 + black 25.11.0 clean.

## Step P3-11 (review r2) — 2026-08-04: two findings, and both were the AST guards trusting their own shape

**CodeRabbit CLI: 2 minor findings, both real, both fixed.** The GitHub app had not re-reviewed the pushed commit at the time of writing; the CLI carried the round. Both findings share a root cause worth naming: an AST guard that checks the *shape* of a call rather than its *contents* is satisfied by a call that is wrong in exactly the way the guard exists to catch.

- **The wiring pin verified one argument of three.** It asserted the scanner's last statement returns `reconcile_windows(...)` with three positional args whose last is `seq_len` — so `reconcile_windows(other_logits, stale_starts, seq_len)` passed it, i.e. a regression reconciling the wrong tensor against the wrong offsets would have left this tier green while the whole file's claim to be testing *the shipped arithmetic* quietly became false. The expression is now compared as `ast.unparse` output against the literal `reconcile_windows(logits, np.asarray(starts), seq_len)` — insensitive to formatting, sensitive to every name in it. Two sabotages (swap the tensor; re-sort the offsets) now turn it red; **neither would have failed the previous assertion.**
- **The "derives no reduction of its own" guard looked only at local `def`s.** `scipy.special.logsumexp(...)` — or any imported reduction — passed it, so `infer/call.py` could have re-derived a distribution while the guard reported it owned none. It now collects the names the module *calls*, bare or qualified, alongside the names it defines. Sabotage-verified with a helper that **calls** a forbidden reduction without defining one, which the old check could not see.

**One stray file, and it was mine.** A `git commit -m "…"` whose body contained backtick-quoted code let bash command-substitute it; the redirect in `` `cls > _BG` `` created an empty file named `_BG` in the worktree (the shell also reported `cls: command not found`, which is what gave it away). The commit message landed with three fragments silently deleted, was amended before push, and the stray file was found by auditing `git status` rather than by any test. Commit bodies containing code go through `git commit -F -` with a **quoted** heredoc.

**Validation.** 67 tests green. **24 sabotages, 23 RED against their NAMED test**, each restored byte-identically; the single true no-bite remains the harness's own declared no-op control. ruff 0.15.0 + black 25.11.0 clean; worktree audited clean.

## Step P3-12 — 2026-08-05: the D3 locus-construction rule — threshold scope, co-occurrence, flank

**Inputs.** `src/tbox_finder/infer/call.py::call_candidates` + its private merge primitives (P2-10c′-c-i); `src/tbox_finder/infer/reconcile.py::reconcile_windows` (P2-03, the operator ADR-0005 A3 froze in code) as the upstream contract for `log_probs` / `zero_flanked` / `coverage`; `labels.CLASS_ORDER`; ADR-0005 **D3** [ADR-0005:46] and **A9 Pin 3** [ADR-0005:538]; PRD §6, §13.1, §5/§13.3.

**Process.** D3's locus-construction rule names five knobs, and `call_candidates` already shipped **three** of them — global threshold, gap-merge, minimum span — for the ρ-pilot, with the other two *deliberately* absent (its own docstring refuses co-occurrence, citing the same §5/§13.3 sentence this step's gate does). So P3-12 is a **promotion, not a new operator**, exactly as `TODO.md`'s standing note and `eval/mining_criterion.py`'s "Reuse, not fork" precedent required. The mask → gap-merge → min-span → `Candidate` step was lifted out of `call_candidates` into `call.candidates_from_mask`; `call_candidates` now builds the global mask and delegates, its signature, behaviour and output unchanged. `src/tbox_finder/infer/locus.py::construct_loci` supplies the *other* mask — D3's **threshold scope** — through the same function, then applies **required-element co-occurrence** and the **flank** on top. There is now exactly one span-merge site in the tree, and an AST test asserts it (`FunctionDef` **and** `AsyncFunctionDef`, the keyword P3-11's review found walking past a sibling guard).

**Outputs.** `src/tbox_finder/infer/locus.py` (`construct_loci`, `element_assignment`, `Locus`, `LocusError`, `RULE_PARAMETERS`, `no_rule_parameter_has_a_default`); `call.py` gains `candidates_from_mask` + `zero_flanked_array` and promotes `_ELEMENT_INDICES` → `ELEMENT_INDICES` (+ `NUM_ELEMENT_CLASSES`) rather than letting `locus.py` re-derive a copy free to go stale; `tests/unit/test_construct_loci.py` (504). No `.smk`, no artifact, no ADR amendment, no DVC object, LOCAL only.

**The co-occurrence rule is a count, and that is the anti-bias encoding.** D3 asks for "**recall-favoring** required-element co-occurrence" and warns *in the same clause* that "mandating canonical elements would re-impose the §5/§13.3 bias". `construct_loci` therefore exposes `min_distinct_elements` — **how many** distinct element classes a locus must carry — and exposes no parameter that can name **which**. That is checked, not asserted: relabelling the element classes by a 7-cycle (and permuting the per-class threshold map with them) leaves the surviving loci, their spans and their counts identical, under **both** scopes and every `k` from 0 to 7. A rule that acquired a "must contain Stem I" clause turns that test red.
