A second, structural test compares the keyword-only parameter set against `RULE_PARAMETERS` as a **set**, so a `required_classes=` added later fails the inventory instead of being waved through.

**⚠ THE RECALL FLOOR IS DISCHARGED AS A STRUCTURAL PROPERTY, AND THE NUMERIC ONE IS NOT THIS STEP'S TO MEASURE.** This block's gate reads "Stage-1 per-locus recall floor preserved on leave-one-order-out positives". A *measured* floor needs a frozen threshold, and D3 pins none until the §13.1 phase gate ("values frozen at the phase gate … never tuned on the test set"); this step's own `Artifacts:` line names a module, a unit test and a stanza — no scan, no checkpoint, no report. What is proved here instead is exact and stronger than a spot measurement: under `threshold_scope="global"` the mask is *bit-identical* to `call_candidates`'s (it is the same `element_posterior` call), every merged run contains at least one masked position, and every masked position is assigned an element class — so `n_distinct_elements >= 1` always and at `min_distinct_elements <= 1` the rule returns the **same spans** the bare caller found, verified over a τ × min_span × gap_merge grid. The rule cannot lower the floor; whatever the floor is, it survives. Any `k >= 2` trades recall for specificity and is a phase-gate value, which is why it has no default.

**Nothing is pinned, and the module has nothing to mistake for a pin.** All six rule parameters are keyword-only with **no default** (A9's `score_threshold` pattern), `no_rule_parameter_has_a_default` re-derives that from the live signature, and a test asserts the only module-level numbers are a `-1` sentinel and a class count derived from `CLASS_ORDER`. Nothing selects on strength: `mean_p_elem` / `peak_p_elem` ride along on the carried `Candidate` as reported quantities only — P3-11 measured `mean_p_elem` swinging **0.6453 → 0.9997** with the 512-window phase while the per-position call stayed exactly invariant, so a rule thresholding on mean strength would re-import the grid dependence the reconciliation operator exists to remove.

**⏭ ONE P3-11 INHERITANCE DISCHARGED AT ITS CHEAP END.** P3-11 left the singly-covered contig terminus measured but downstream-invisible, because `Candidate` has no coverage field and adding one touches a P2 module, its 22 tests and two committed report schemas. `Locus` is a **new** record, so `n_single_covered_span` costs no P2 schema change — a locus called from one window's evidence is now distinguishable from one called from two. Its absence is `None` (**not measured**), never `0`; a sabotage collapsing the two turns the test red. Contig-end padding is likewise counted over the flanked span (`n_zero_flanked_span`) beside the core-scoped `candidate.n_zero_flanked` — two intervals, two deliberately different names, after P3-10's two-fields-named-"singleton" collision.

**Ordering is load-bearing, and three independent references prove it.** Merge → co-occurrence → flank. Co-occurrence is read over the **core**, so widening the flank can never change which loci survive (at `flank = 10` the first core's padded span reaches inside the Specifier run — a rule counting over the span flips at `k = 2`); `min_span` is applied to the core, so a generous flank cannot rescue a run that failed the span cut; and flanking runs **after** gap-merging, so two cores the gap rule kept apart stay apart — if their padded spans intersect that is reported via `overlaps_neighbour`, never silently re-merged. Each of those three decisions is flipped in an independent pure-Python reference and **shown to disagree** on the fixture grid, so the agreement test is evidence rather than two implementations of the same mistake agreeing.

**⚠ TWO SABOTAGES DID NOT BITE, AND BOTH GAPS WERE REAL.** (1) Removing the per-class arg-max mask (`np.where(cleared, elem_probs, -inf)` → the raw posteriors) changed **nothing**, because every threshold set in the file made the strongest class and the cleared class the same one — the guard was decoration. It needed a position where the *strongest* class fails its own τ while a *weaker* one clears: Stem_I at 0.893 under τ = 0.95 against Specifier at 0.0095 under τ = 0.005, which must be named **Specifier**. (2) Disabling the parameter-inventory **set** comparison also changed nothing: the stub it was checked against carried a *default*, which the second half of the predicate catches anyway. The set comparison exists for a knob that was **added** — an unlisted `required_classes` has no default to find — so the check now runs against a stub with exactly that extra parameter. Same shape as [[all-true-fixture-cannot-test-a-conjunction]]: a fixture in which two branches agree cannot tell them apart.

**Validation.** 504 tests green. **29 sabotages, 28 RED against their NAMED test**, each restored by rewriting the original bytes and sha256-verified (`git checkout --` is a silent no-op on a file created *this* step), `__pycache__` cleared between runs; the one non-bite is the harness's own declared no-op control. Neighbouring suites green alongside (`test_infer_call` 22, `test_mining_criterion` 13, `test_reconcile_windows_integration` 23, `test_infer_rho_pilot` 37, `test_infer_scan` 14, `test_mine_round`, `test_reconcile_golden` — 231 together), which is what confirms the `call.py` promotion is behaviour-preserving for both production call sites. Full unit+golden+ml **4,481 passed / 16 failed** against a matched baseline worktree at `c255382` at **3,977 / 16** — failure sets **identical**, `comm` empty both ways. ruff 0.15.0 + black 25.11.0 clean; no `.smk` touched. **No ADR amendment, no §7 sign-off, no artifact, no DVC object.**

## Step P3-12 (review r1) — 2026-08-05: two findings, and one was a measured-looking number that was never measured

**Only the CLI reviewed.** `coderabbit review --committed --base main` returned **2 minor findings, both real, both fixed**. The GitHub app did **not** review: its `CodeRabbit` check went **`pass`** carrying only the Fair-Usage *"Review rate limited"* notice — CLAUDE.md §5.1's trap for the **fourth** step running, and an absence rather than a pass. No Greptile credit spent (§5.1a: a capacity absence with a real CLI review on the head is not an unmet gate). CI green throughout (`lint`, `pytest`, `snakemake`); the `pytest` pass is also what confirms the new module and its 504 tests import and run in the **bare CI Tier-1** environment, i.e. `locus.py` is genuinely torch-free.

- **(minor) A docstring cited a test that does not exist.** `locus.py`'s recall-floor paragraph pointed at `test_global_scope_at_k1_loses_nothing_the_caller_found`; the test is `test_global_scope_at_k_le_1_...`. An unresolvable cross-reference in the one paragraph that tells a reader where the floor claim is *checked* — the claim looks evidenced and the evidence cannot be found.
- **(minor, and the one worth carrying) A docstring stated a threshold boundary that was never measured.** The per-class-scope test claimed the global scope "keeps the Specifier run below 0.893". **0.893 is the per-class own-class posterior (0.94 × 0.95); the global scope thresholds `1 − P(background)`, which is 0.95 on every element position whatever its class.** The true global range is τ ∈ (0.05, **0.95**]. Measured rather than re-reasoned: τ = 0.95 keeps all three runs, τ = 0.9500001 loses them. The same conflation sat in the `_RUNS` comment, which gave one range for two scopes that do not share one — and the per-class ceiling is not 0.893 either, because 0.94 × 0.95 round-trips to **0.8929999999999999** and so never attains it. Both ranges are now stated separately with their measured endpoints. **No assertion moved** (every τ in the sweep lands the same side of both boundaries), but a file whose subject is measurement had a measured-looking number in it that no one had measured — the same shape as P3-11 r1's false "left half" claim about the tiling.
- **The fix came with a strengthening, not just a correction.** "The global scope cannot do this at any τ" was *argued* in prose and swept only below the boundary. The sweep now runs 0.05 → 1.0, crossing 0.95, so both sides are asserted.

**Validation.** 504 tests green; ruff 0.15.0 + black 25.11.0 clean. No shipped behaviour changed — both findings were prose, and the second is recorded because its being prose is exactly why it survived 29 sabotages: no sabotage of executable code can turn a wrong comment red.

## Step P3-12 (self-review) — 2026-08-05: the rule had never been fed the real operator's output

**Found by running the composition, not by reading it.** Every test in the file built its own log-posteriors; none ran `reconcile_windows` and handed the result to `construct_loci`. That left the actual upstream contract unexercised — `Reconciled` emits `float64` log-probs, a `bool` `zero_flanked` and an **`int32`** `coverage`, and `construct_loci` refuses a non-integer coverage on a dtype the synthetic fixtures never produce. [[verify-the-line-you-ship]]: the ad-hoc smoke that surfaced this **also failed on its first run**, and for a fixture reason worth recording — an all-zero logit tensor log-softmaxes to a **uniform** distribution, so `1 − P(background) = 0.875` at every position and the whole 3,072-nt contig came back as one locus. A degenerate oracle reads exactly like an operator defect.

Two tests now ship the composition: a tail-anchored 1024/512 tiling of a 3,072-nt contig with one 160-nt Stem_I locus planted at an interior position (core and flanked span both exact through the real operator), and the same locus planted in the **singly-covered terminus**. The second is the one that matters. It measures `coverage == 1` on **1,024 of 3,072** positions — P3-11's number, reproduced — asserts `zero_flanked` is `False` **everywhere** (tail-anchored tiling never runs a window off a contig longer than one window, so that flag cannot mark the terminus), and asserts the locus is **kept** with `n_single_covered_span = 288`, the whole flanked span. That is the P3-11 inheritance closed at the only place it was cheap to close: a `Locus` field, no `Candidate` schema change, and a *non-zero* assertion rather than a field only ever tested at zero.

**Validation.** 506 tests green. **31 sabotages, 30 RED against their NAMED test** (the two new ones: inverting the coverage dtype contract to `"f"` reddens 7 tests including the real-operator one; counting single coverage over the core rather than the flanked span gives 160 where 288 is right). One declared no-op control held. ruff 0.15.0 + black 25.11.0 clean.

## Step P3-12 (review r2) — 2026-08-05: a conversion that changes the value is not a conversion

**CLI only again**; the app's `CodeRabbit` check stayed `pass` on the Fair-Usage *"Review rate limited"* notice. **1 minor finding, real, fixed — and it was worse than reported.**

**`int()` silently truncates a locus-rule value, and every truncation runs clean.** CodeRabbit named `min_distinct_elements` and `flank`. Reproducing it by execution found the same defect on **all four** integer knobs, two of which live in the *shared* merge and therefore reached `call_candidates` too. Measured on the fixture, before any guard existed:

| knob | passed | acted on | consequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `min_distinct_elements` | 1.9 | 1 | kept `(110, 122)`, a **single-class** locus the caller excluded — the co-occurrence gate silently loosened |
| `min_span` | 25.9 | 25 | kept `(45, 70)`, a 25-nt run the caller excluded — the span cut silently loosened |
| `gap_merge` | 4.9 | 4 | stopped bridging the fixture's 5-nt gap — three cores where two were asked for |
| `flank` | 8.9 | 8 | one nucleotide of context less on each side than requested |

Each reports the parameter the caller *asked for* while acting on a different one, and these are precisely the values ADR-0005 D3 freezes at the §13.1 phase gate — the class of defect this module's whole no-default pin discipline exists to prevent, arriving through the type system instead of through a default.

**Fixed at the shared boundary, not in two places.** One `call.require_integer(name, value, exc)` — accepts `int` / `numpy` integers and an **integral** float (a YAML or JSON config legitimately yields `50.0`, and neither can change under conversion), refuses a fractional float and refuses `bool` (an `int` subclass, so `flank=True` would have been a flank of 1). `candidates_from_mask` and `construct_loci` both call it; the `exc` argument keeps the raising type attributable to the layer that refused (`CandidateError` vs `LocusError`). `call_candidates` gains the guard **by composition**, which is the second time this step the promotion has paid a dividend the fork would not have.

The test asserts more than the refusal: for each knob it also shows the integral float is accepted and agrees exactly with the int, **and** that the truncated value genuinely gives a different answer — a per-knob base chosen so that it does, because a case where truncated and intended agree would prove nothing.

**Validation.** 512 tests in this file, 746 across the affected suites. **34 sabotages, 33 RED against their NAMED test**, one declared no-op control held. Full unit+golden+ml **4,492 passed / 16 failed** against a matched baseline at `c255382` at **3,977 / 16** — failure sets **identical**, `comm` empty both ways. ruff 0.15.0 + black 25.11.0 clean.

⚠ Two sabotage anchors went stale in the same edit that fixed the finding (`if int(flank) < 0:` became `if flank < 0:`) and the harness reported them as **misses**. The harness asserts its anchor matches exactly once, so a stale anchor is loud rather than silent — but it is worth recording that a refactor invalidates a sabotage suite the way it invalidates a test, and a campaign re-run after a fix is not optional.

## Step P3-13 — 2026-08-05: strand from element order, and an alphabet handoff that refuses to guess

**Inputs.** `infer/locus.py::Locus` + `element_assignment` (P3-12); `infer/call.py::require_integer`; `stage2/tokenizer.py::transcribe` (the shipped PRD §6 T→U handoff); `data/processed/master_clean_v0.parquet` (23,535 records) for the measured element rank. **Process.** Two new modules — `infer/strand.py::resolve_strand` reads orientation off the predicted element order; `infer/handoff.py::transcribe_to_rna` orients and transcribes the flanked span into the RNA Stage-2 ingests sequence-only. `scripts/measure_element_order.py` produces the rank the resolver compares against, and the absence rule it shares with `scripts/measure_overlap_prevalence.py` was extracted into one `element_intervals` reader rather than copied. **Outputs.** `src/tbox_finder/infer/strand.py`, `src/tbox_finder/infer/handoff.py`, `scripts/measure_element_order.py`, `tests/fixtures/element_order/element_order_prevalence.json`, `tests/unit/test_strand_resolver.py` (51). **Validation.** unit green — the imp.md gate's three claims (order→orientation, ambiguous→both-strand carry, exact T→U) each hold a section. **Decisions.** ADR-0005 D15 implemented as a rank-concordance *sign*, pinning no value; cross-ref ADR-0005 D15, PRD §6/§13.1.

**⚠ `CLASS_ORDER` IS NOT THE 5′→3′ ORDER, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS ONE ELEMENT IN SEVEN.** The obvious constant to reach for is `labels.CLASS_ORDER`, which reads `background, Stem_I, Specifier, Stem_II, Stem_III, Antiterminator_Tbox_seq, Terminator, Discriminator` — a **softmax index** order, as its own comment says. Measured over the whole corpus (element-extent midpoints, pairwise within record), the 5′→3′ order is:

| rank | element | median midpoint | support for the adjacency to its left |
|---:|---|---:|---|
| 1 | `Stem_I` | 55.0 | — |
| 2 | `Specifier` | 92.0 | **0.997232** (n = 23,122) |
| 3 | `Stem_II` | 127.0 | 1.000000 (n = 21,474) |
| 4 | `Stem_III` | 188.0 | 1.000000 (n = 21,767) |
| 5 | `Discriminator` | 210.5 | 0.999784 (n = 23,127) |
| 6 | `Antiterminator_Tbox_seq` | 219.0 | 0.999828 (n = 23,208) |
| 7 | `Terminator` | 244.0 | 0.999915 (n = 23,439) |

`CLASS_ORDER` puts `Discriminator` **last**; the corpus puts it fifth, 5′ of the antiterminator's midpoint in **23,204** of 23,208 co-annotating records (3 the other way, 1 tied) — the ~3-nt discriminator sits in the 5′ half of the ~30-nt antiterminator extent, the nesting PRD §8 documents. Borrowing the softmax order would have mis-ranked it silently. The shipped constant is therefore re-derived from the committed measurement by test (`test_canonical_order_is_the_measured_order`), and a test asserts the two orders *disagree* so the shortcut cannot be taken back later by accident.

**⚠ THE ABSENCE RULE MATTERED, AND THE FIRST MEASUREMENT HAD IT WRONG.** A first pass that treated only NaN as "unannotated" reported `Stem_I` < `Specifier` at **0.9822** over 23,475 records. The corpus also uses **`-1` sentinels**, which that pass read as position −1 — sorting the Specifier to the 5′ end of every record missing it. Routing through the shared `element_intervals` reader (null **or negative** ⇒ absent) gives **0.997232 over 23,122**: 353 records dropped, and the weakest adjacency in the whole order tightened by a factor of six. The extraction is verified byte-identical on the ADR-0004 report it also feeds.

**Scientific-evidence gate (§10.1) — cleared, ≥2 independent agreeing sources** (accessed 2026-08-05): Zhang & Ferré-D'Amaré 2013, "Stem I contains the specifier trinucleotide … 3′ to stem I is the antiterminator domain" [PMID:23892783]; Suddala & Zhang 2019, "a 5′ Stem I domain … and a 3′ antiterminator/antisequestrator (or discriminator) domain" [PMID:31206978; DOI:10.1002/iub.2098]; Zhang 2020, "the Stem I, Stem II, and Discriminator domains" [PMID:32633085; DOI:10.1002/wrna.1600]. The first two already carry in-repo citations in PRD §3. Note the limit: the literature places the discriminator **within** the 3′ antiterminator domain and defines no order between them, so rank 5 vs 6 is a statement about annotation *extents*, not about domain order — recorded as such in the module, the script and the fixture.

**✅ THE RULE PINS NO VALUE, AND D15's TWO AMBIGUOUS CASES FALL OUT OF IT.** Each observed class is reduced to the **median** position of its predicted nucleotides; every pair of classes votes concordant or discordant against the canonical rank; `order_margin = n_concordant − n_discordant` is the Kendall-τ numerator. A **single confident element** yields no pair; a **scrambled order** cancels — D15's two named cases, with no tuned constant. `min_order_margin` is keyword-only with **no default** (the §13.1 freeze owns it), and at 1 the rule is exactly the sign of τ, i.e. parameter-free. Ambiguity is recall-favouring: `strands` carries `("+", "-")` and the handoff emits a payload for each, so a mis-resolution is a bounded false negative, never a false-novelty claim.

**⚠ THE MEDIAN IS LOAD-BEARING BECAUSE THE SPECIFIER IS NESTED IN STEM I.** Stem I is therefore **two runs** in the per-position assignment. A last-occurrence statistic places Stem I *after* the Specifier on a perfectly canonical locus and casts a discordant vote; the test computes both and shows the divergence rather than asserting the choice (sabotage S08 confirms `np.max` flips the call).

**⚠ FIVE REVERSE-COMPLEMENTS ALREADY EXIST AND NONE IS SAFE HERE.** `anchors.py:282`, `data/flank_context.py:198` and `mining/homolog_msa.py:468` are `str.maketrans` tables over `ACGTN` that leave an IUPAC ambiguity code **uncomplemented**; `data/window_dataset.py:277` maps it to `N`. On `ARYSWKMBDHVGC` the three give `GCVHDBMKWSYRT` and the fourth `GCNNNNNNNNNNT` against the correct `GCBDHVKMWSRYT` — a silently wrong minus strand handed to Stage-2, on exactly the MAG contigs where ambiguity codes are common. Biopython is not the fix either: it is **absent from `envs/ml-dna.yml`, `envs/ml-rna.yml` and the CI install** (so it would break both the P5 scan env and the bare-CI tier), and `Bio.Seq.complement` mangles out-of-alphabet input by design — its own tutorial shows `"EVRNAK"` → `"EBYNTM"`. `handoff.reverse_complement` is IUPAC-complete, case-preserving and **fails closed**; the other five are left to their own callers and tests, but this is the only one on the Stage-1 → Stage-2 path.

**⚠ `U` IS REFUSED, DELIBERATELY.** Admitting it would make the table non-involutive — `T` and `U` both complement to `A`, so a double reverse-complement silently rewrites `U` to `T`. The input here is scanned genomic DNA; RNA arriving means a caller has already transcribed.

**T→U is delegated, and the delegation is *observed*.** `stage2.tokenizer.transcribe` is the function the Stage-2 training table was built with, so inference must use it and not a copy that agrees today. Comparing outputs cannot show that — a fork returns identical strings — so the shipped module calls it as a **module attribute** (never a `from`-import, which is unpatchable) and the test substitutes it and asserts the return changes. Sabotage S21 replaces the call with a behaviourally identical fork and goes RED.

**⚠ THREE SABOTAGES DID NOT BITE ON THE FIRST PASS; TWO WERE REAL GAPS.** (1) *"strand is read from the core, not the flanked span"* was **vacuous**: the fixture's flank was pure background, so reading the wider span shifts every median by the same offset and leaves the order — and the call — identical. It now plants an unrelated element 30 nt away and a flank of 40 that reaches it, so the sabotage turns an ambiguous locus into a resolved one. (2) `derive_order`'s three refusals (an exact tie, a pair no record co-annotates, a non-total order) are **never exercised by the real corpus**, which gives a clean tournament — they now have their own synthetic fixtures plus a positive control, and three separate sabotages bite. (3) The third was a badly chosen mutation, not a gap: `!=` → `not <=` still catches an *added* knob. Re-aimed at the direction that misses it, and the reverse direction (a stale `RULE_PARAMETERS` entry naming a parameter the function no longer has) got its own test.

**Validation.** 51 tests in the new file, 702 across the affected suites. **35 sabotages, 35 RED against their NAMED test**, each restored by rewriting the original bytes and sha256-verified, `__pycache__` cleared between runs; the one non-bite is the harness's own declared no-op control. The campaign was **re-run after `black` reformatted `strand.py`**, since a reformat invalidates an anchor the way it invalidates a test. Full unit+golden+ml **4,543 passed / 16 failed** against a **matched baseline worktree** at `0048b6a` at **4,492 / 16** — failure sets **identical**, `comm` empty both ways. (A first comparison against the *main checkout* was not matched: it has `data/`, the worktree does not, so 30 data-dependent tests skip in one and fail in the other.) ruff 0.15.15 + black 25.11.0 clean; no `.smk` touched. **Commit.** <SHA>

## Step P3-13 (reviews r1–r5 + the app round) — 2026-08-05: five rounds, five real findings, and two fail-open paths

**Six review rounds ran: the CodeRabbit CLI five times, and the GitHub app once (automatically, on `ecc536b`).** Every round found something real. ⚠ Three of the five CLI rounds were taken while the app's `CodeRabbit` PR check read **`pass` carrying only a "Review rate limited" notice** — §5.1's trap, now for the fifth step running. ⚠ And a correction worth carrying: three commit messages state the app "has not reviewed", which was true when each was written (the reviews API returned nothing) and went **stale** when the automatic review landed. §5.1's rule to *detect* the review state per PR rather than carry a remembered value applies to a single PR over time, not only across PRs.

| round | reviewer | findings | the one that mattered |
|---|---|---|---|
| r1 | CLI | 2 minor | a test that passed on the **wrong branch** |
| r2 | CLI | 1 minor | the documented command **could not run** in the env that holds the corpus |
| r3 | CLI | 1 minor | an unranked class label was **fail-open**, one path silently |
| r4 | CLI | **1 major** | Copeland scores ranked a tournament that was **never complete** |
| r5 | CLI | 1 minor | malformed locus coordinates **sliced silently** |
| — | app (auto, on `ecc536b`) | 3 nitpicks | 2 fixed; the third **independently re-found r4's major** |

**⚠ r1 — A `pytest.raises` TEST CAN PASS ON A BRANCH IT DOES NOT NAME.** `test_build_element_rank_refuses_a_repeated_class` used `("Stem_I", *CANONICAL_ELEMENT_ORDER[1:-1], "Stem_I")`, which also **drops `Terminator`** — so `build_element_rank` raised on the *missing-class* branch and never reached the duplicate check. Verified by execution: the old fixture raises "must rank exactly the element classes", the corrected one "repeats a class". The refusal the test is named for was untested, and no sabotage existed for it — which is why the first campaign did not catch it. Same family as [[raises-test-needs-a-positive-control]]: asserting *that* it raised is not asserting *why*.

**⚠ r3 — TWO FAIL-OPEN PATHS, AND THE REALISTIC TRIGGER IS A SUBSTITUTION, NOT CORRUPTION.** `resolve_strand` accepted any integer label. Mixed with a known class, an unknown label reached `ELEMENT_RANK[...]` and raised a bare `KeyError` from inside the vote; **alone**, it never looked a rank up and returned an ordinary ambiguous `StrandCall` naming a class that does not exist. The way in is `Reconciled.prediction` — the arg-max over **all** classes, the quantity `eval/gate4.py` grades boundary IoU on — which encodes `background` as label 0, has no rank, and is **the same shape and dtype** as `element_assignment`'s output. Measured: `resolve_strand(locus, prediction, …)` died with `KeyError: 0`. The guard now names that swap in its message, because it is the likely cause.

**⚠ r4 — COPELAND SCORES RANK ONLY IF EVERY ELEMENT MET EVERY OTHER, EXACTLY ONCE.** `derive_order` summed wins over whatever pairs the report listed, then checked only that the scores were distinct — while its own docstring already claimed completeness as the contract. Duplicate the A-vs-B entry and drop A-vs-C and the scores come out **2 / 1 / 0**, all distinct, so an order is returned for a pair nobody measured. It matters because this function decides `CANONICAL_ELEMENT_ORDER` — the constant orienting every reported locus — from a **committed** file a future edit to the producer could regenerate. `measure()` emits `itertools.combinations` exactly once each *today*; that is a property of the current producer, not of the input `derive_order` accepts. Now refused: unknown element, self-pair, duplicate pair, and any missing pair (named). Re-running the measurement reproduces the committed fixture **byte-identically**, so no number moved.

**⚠ r5 — PYTHON MAKES BAD COORDINATES QUIET.** `handoff_loci` checked only `end > len(text)`. `text[-5:20]` wraps from the far end of the string; `text[20:10]` yields `""`. `Locus` is a plain frozen dataclass with no runtime validation, so one round-tripped through JSON hands Stage-2 a sequence that is **not** the one the payload's coordinates name — which downstream reads as an ordinary candidate. Now `0 <= start <= end <= len(sequence)` and `length == len(span)` are both enforced, and `Handoff.length` is taken from the **emitted span** rather than copied, so the field cannot disagree with `rna`.

**✅ THE APP AND THE CLI OVERLAPPED ON EXACTLY ONE FINDING OUT OF EIGHT — and that one was r4's major, which the app rated a nitpick.** Two independent reviewers converging on the same defect at opposite severities is the argument for running both, and for judging a finding on its content rather than its label.

**⚠ A REFACTOR INVALIDATED A SABOTAGE ANCHOR FOR THE SECOND TIME THIS STEP.** `black` reformatting `strand.py` staled none, but the r1 fix and the app's `require_iupac` extraction each staled one, both reported as **misses** rather than passes — the harness asserts every anchor matches **exactly once**. A campaign re-run after a fix is not optional.

**Validation at the reviewed head.** 57 tests in the file. **42 sabotages, 42 RED against their NAMED test**, one declared no-op control held. Full unit+golden+ml **4,549 passed / 16 failed** against the matched baseline worktree at `0048b6a` at **4,492 / 16** — failure sets **identical**, `comm` empty both ways. ruff 0.15.15 + black 25.11.0 clean; CI green. **Commit.** <SHA>

## Step P3-13-fixup — 2026-08-05: the two post-merge review findings on `5637e91`

**Inputs.** `scripts/measure_element_order.py::derive_order`;
`src/tbox_finder/infer/handoff.py::handoff_loci`; the committed 23,535-record measurement
`tests/fixtures/element_order/element_order_prevalence.json`; `tests/unit/test_strand_resolver.py`.
**Process.** Two CodeRabbit-CLI findings arrived **after** PR #106 was squash-merged, from a
review round that was still running while three later probes returned *"Review limit reached"* —
so the escalation to Greptile was made on an inference about capacity, not a fact about the round
in flight. Both are on merged code; neither moves a shipped number. **(1)** `derive_order` awarded
a pairwise win on `n_a_before_b > n_b_before_a` — a **plurality** — while its docstring claimed a
**strict majority**. **(2)** `handoff_loci`'s `Raises` block promised refusal on "a sequence
carrying characters outside the IUPAC alphabet", but validation ran per *emitted span* only, so
`handoff_loci("X", [], [])` returned `[]`.
**Outputs.** `derive_order` awards on `2 * n_a_before_b > n_both`, refuses with *"no strict
majority"* quoting the support it refused on, and now validates the denominator it divides by
(`n_a_before_b + n_b_before_a <= n_both`, neither negative) — a consistency `n_both` did not need
while it was only a presence check. `handoff_loci` returns a `HandoffResult`
(`payloads`, `n_outside_alphabet`, `n_outside_alphabet_in_spans`) instead of a bare list;
`count_outside_alphabet` and `_merge_spans` are new. 11 new tests (57 → 68 in the file).
**Validation.** `tests/unit/test_strand_resolver.py` **68 passed**; 713 across the affected suites
(`test_infer_call`, `test_reconcile`, `test_infer_scan`, `test_construct_loci`). The corrected
script was re-run against the real corpus (`data/processed/master_clean_v0.parquet`, 23,535
records, `tbox-finder-data`) and **regenerates `element_order_prevalence.json` byte-identically**
— the strongest available statement that the rule change moved nothing, and stronger than the
in-test re-derivation, which reads the artifact rather than producing it.
Full unit+golden+ml **4,560 passed / 16 failed** against a matched baseline worktree at `5637e91`
at **4,549 / 16** — failure sets **identical**, `comm` empty both ways, and the +11 is exactly the
new tests. **30 sabotages, 29 RED against their NAMED test** (re-run in full after the review fixes —
a fix stales an anchor the way a refactor does); the one non-bite is the harness's declared
no-op control. ruff 0.15.0 + black 25.11.0 clean; no `.smk` touched.
**Decisions.** The handoff fork was a **§7 stop, not a silent pick** (ADR-0005 D15 unamended,
no value pinned).

::: {.callout-important}
## The rule was a plurality, and both rules agree on all 21 committed pairs

On 40 / 39 / 21 the plurality rule awards A the pair on **40 %** support — an adjacency in the
rank that orients every reported locus, attested by a minority of the records that measured it.
Ties are not hypothetical here: one element is routinely a short annotation centred inside
another, and the committed measurement records **13** ties for `Stem_I`/`Specifier` (of 23,122)
and **1** for `Antiterminator_Tbox_seq`/`Discriminator` (of 23,208). Verified by execution that
**every one of the 21 committed pairs is decided by more than half** of its co-annotating records,
so re-deriving under the corrected rule reproduces `CANONICAL_ELEMENT_ORDER` exactly and
`element_order_prevalence.json` is untouched. The exposure was a **re-measurement** — a different
GTDB release, the P5 scan's own calls — deriving a rank the stated rule does not support, with
nothing failing. The two award branches are sabotaged **separately** (S01–S04): a `>=` slip or a
plurality revert on one branch alone survives a fixture that only exercises the other.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
## Validating the whole contig was the wrong fix, and the review's one-liner was it

CodeRabbit proposed `text = require_iupac(sequence)`. It makes the documented contract literally
true, and it is **anti-recall on exactly the MAG contigs PRD §6 targets**: one stray byte anywhere
on a megabase contig then refuses **every** locus called on it, and the caller has no way at this
layer to ask for the clean ones. Every byte that reaches Stage 2 was already validated. So the
resolution keeps the per-span refusal, makes the `Raises` block say precisely that, and **counts**
the out-of-alphabet characters the payloads do not carry — a filthy contig becomes visible without
becoming fatal. Judge the finding and the fix separately: the finding was real, the patch was not.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## `n_outside_alphabet_in_spans` is 0 on every successful return — so it is measured, not written

The per-span refusal fires first, which makes a literal `0` indistinguishable from a real
measurement and useless as a check — a quantity whose legitimate value is always zero is the shape
that lets a mask run clean while masking nothing. It is computed over the **union** of the emitted
spans (`flank` can push two loci into overlap, and per-span counting would double-count a shared
position and break `n_outside_alphabet_in_spans <= n_outside_alphabet`). Its test is the designed
control that **must** fire: substituting the transcriber removes the refusal and the field reports
the junk it now carries (S14/S15 RED).
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## Three sabotages did not bite first time; two were real gaps

**(1)** *"exactly half is not a majority"* was exercised on the **A** branch only (50/49/1), so a
`>=` slip on the **B** branch passed — the mirrored 49/50/1 case now ships. **(2)** The
empty-handoff test asserted `payloads == ()` on an empty locus list, which reads identically to
*emits nothing, ever*: replacing `payloads=tuple(payloads)` with `payloads=()` left it green. It
now carries a populated positive control ([[raises-test-needs-a-positive-control]] one level up —
asserting an emptiness needs the non-empty case beside it). **(3)** The third was badly aimed, not
a gap: `test_the_committed_measurement_supports_the_order_by_strict_majority` reads the committed
**artifact** and never calls the script, so mutating the script cannot touch it — re-aimed at the
fixture (S11/S11b/S11c), where all three bite.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## Review r1 (CLI, 2 minor, both real) — and one was dead code, not a hypothetical

**(a) A conditional assertion is a vacuous one when its guard is false, and this guard always
was.** The boundary check "the same character one position outside the span is counted, not
refused" ran under `if start > 0:` — and `CANONICAL_LAYOUT` begins at 0, so with `flank=0` the
locus starts at 0 and **that assertion never executed**. The review framed it as a future risk
("if the fixture ever produces `start == 0`"); measured, it was already dead. Its **proposed fix
(`assert start > 0`) would have failed** — the 5′ side has no room at this tiling. Re-aimed at
the 3′ side (`end` = 130 of 160) with the room stated as a **precondition**, so a fixture change
fails loudly instead of silently deleting the check. Judge the finding and the fix separately.

**(b) A `for` loop over an empty list asserts nothing.** The strict-majority check over the
committed measurement made a claim about **every one of the 21 pairs**, which is a statement
about the count as much as about each pair; a truncated or partially-written artifact satisfied
it in silence. The count now leads the test (sabotage S27 removes one pair from the fixture and
turns it RED).
:::

**Process.** ⚠ **Never merge with a review process still running.** Three CLI probes returning
*"Review limit reached"* answered *"is a new round available now"*, not *"is the round I already
launched finished"* — a delayed round completed after the merge with 1 major + 1 minor. Check for
in-flight background reviews before merging, not just the last probe's answer.

**Commit.** one atomic commit on `p3-13-fixup-order-and-handoff-scope`, parent `5637e91`.

## Step P3-14 — 2026-08-05: the end-to-end two-stage harness + the D15 strand-robustness diagnostic

**Inputs.** `data/processed/checkpoints/stage1_production/stage1.pt` (P2, DVC) ·
`data/processed/checkpoints/stage2_rinalmo/aux1.0_lr1e-4` (P3-06, DVC — the arm
`stage2.eval.production_arm_config()` names) · `reports/gate2_p3_ece.json` for the P3-10 fitted
`T = 1.140627294282911` · `data/interim/flank_context/context_v0.parquet` + the committed split
table for the fixture contigs · the P2-03/P3-11/P3-12/P3-13 inference operators.

**Process.** `src/tbox_finder/integration/two_stage.py` composes the PRD §6 path — reconcile →
`construct_loci` → `resolve_strands` → `handoff_loci` → Stage-2 binary logit → the P3-07
calibration stack → the §13.1 candidate table — and measures the diagnostic by re-scoring every
locus on the strand the resolver did *not* choose. It re-derives nothing: the counterfactual
payloads come from `dataclasses.replace(call, strands=BOTH_STRANDS)` fed back through the shipped
`handoff_loci`, and the posteriors from `recalibrate.calibrated_posterior`, whose own
`gated_posterior_key` names the column the table calls `stage2_named_posterior`. Four CLI legs:
`stage1` (torch, `ml-dna`) and `stage2` (torch, `ml-rna`) mint committed fixtures; `payloads` and
`run` are torch-free, and `run` is the only leg CI executes. `workflow/rules/integration.smk::two_stage_eval`
runs that leg. `scripts/mint_two_stage_fixture.py` builds the contig set.

**Outputs.** `reports/strand_robustness.json` · `reports/p3/two_stage_candidates.json` (27 rows) ·
`tests/fixtures/two_stage/{contigs.json, stage1_window_logits.npz, stage2_logits.json, expected.sha256}` ·
`tests/golden/test_two_stage_golden.py` (24) · `tests/unit/test_two_stage.py` (83). Candidate-table
digest `04bc8a557a1883e2aa4814b4c816c030c7c44e630cd25e71184c6670a9748648`. No DVC object; no
checkpoint; no W&B run. `infer/call.py` gains `rule_parameters_have_no_default` and `locus.py` /
`strand.py` now delegate to it (promotion, behaviour unchanged).

**Validation.** Golden green — the torch-free replay reproduces the committed digest exactly;
`strand_robustness_problems` returns `[]` on the committed report. Full unit+golden+ml
**4,669 passed / 14 failed** against a matched baseline worktree at `81b6cd1` at **4,562 / 14** —
failure sets **identical** (`comm` empty both ways), and the +107 is exactly the new tests.
**39 sabotages, 36 RED against their NAMED test**; the three non-bites are the declared no-op
control and two mutations inside the **torch-only** mint legs, which no CI-runnable test can
execute and which were verified by execution instead. ⚠ The campaign was re-run after **each** of the
three review rounds, and twice an anchor went stale — once because a fix rewrote the line, once because
`black` reflowed a dict comprehension onto one line. Both surfaced as **misses** rather than
passes only because the harness asserts each anchor matches exactly once. ruff 0.15.15 + black
25.11.0 + `snakemake --lint` clean.

::: {.callout-important}
## The diagnostic D15 asks for cannot be computed at P3, and the substitution is reported, not renamed

D15 defines the diagnostic as the "fraction of confirmed loci **tier**-invariant to strand
re-resolution". §13.3's tiers are assigned by the orthogonal-validation pipeline, which is **P6** —
there is nothing at P3 to be tier-invariant *of*. The report therefore carries
`tier_invariance: null` with the reason beside it and computes **two-stage-confirmation**
invariance in its place. Re-reading it against real tiers is owed at P6.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
## Measured: `confirmation_invariance = 0.0`, and that is D15 working, not failing

All 26 confirmed loci flip verdict under strand re-resolution (median |Δposterior| **0.9987**).
Read alone that number looks alarming; read with the truth block it is the opposite. The resolver
called **27 of 27** loci correctly, and `n_confirmed_on_wrong_strand_only` is **0** — the one
outcome D15 forbids. So the reading is: Stage-2 is almost perfectly strand-discriminative, which
makes the resolver *load-bearing* for every confirmed locus — a mis-resolution costs the locus
(a bounded false negative) and can never manufacture one (a false novelty). That is exactly the
degradation D15 specifies.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## An invariance of 1.0 and a strand-blind scorer are the same number, so two liveness controls ship beside it

Had Stage-2 ignored orientation it would have agreed with itself everywhere and reported *perfect*
robustness while measuring nothing — the shape that let a mask run clean while masking nothing.
`max_abs_posterior_delta` and `n_verdict_disagreements` are reported alongside and asserted
non-zero by the golden: a designed control that **must** fire.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## Two different non-determinisms, measured separately — and the first draft conflated them

**Stage-1 is not run-to-run bit-identical.** Re-running its leg on the identical contigs moved
**91 of 327,680** stored logits by up to **3.91e-3** — while changing **zero** per-position
predictions. The call is stable; the posterior is not. This alone is why the golden **replays**
committed model output instead of re-deriving it: a hash-diffing regression that re-scanned would
be flaky by construction.

**Stage-2 is the narrower case, and re-running it proved so.** Regenerating the `stage2` leg over
the same work list reproduced its artifact **byte-identically** — so it is run-to-run
*reproducible*. What is not invariant is **batch position**: a contig and its reverse complement
hand Stage-2 byte-identical RNA (26 of 28 distinct payload sequences were scored twice this way,
itself a check that the resolver + RC handoff round-trips), and those two scorings disagree in
**14 of 26** cases by up to **0.0292** of logit, because `score_rows` batches by token length and
the two land in different positions. ⚠ An earlier draft of this stanza and of the module docstring
said "neither stage is run-to-run bit-identical", which is **false for Stage-2** — the claim was
written before the leg was actually re-run. Corrected here: the caveat is on re-*batched* scoring,
not on re-running.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## The fixture had to be built to *break* two degeneracies, and a third bit anyway

(1) `flank_context` reverse-complements minus-strand rows on fetch, so `context_seq` is **always**
in the locus's own sense and every locus in it is on `+`. A fixture built straight from it could
not distinguish a working resolver from one hardcoded to `"+"`, so each record contributes the
slab **and** its reverse complement. (2) Four contigs are the **reverse** (PRD §12's
composition-exact null, not the RC — an RC is useless against an RC-equivariant scanner); Stage-1
finds **zero** loci in all four. (3) The unit file's synthetic carrier was `"ACGT"` repeated, which
is **its own reverse complement** — the `+` and `−` payloads came out byte-identical and two tests
failed on it. `_CARRIER` is now non-palindromic and a test asserts it.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## What the committed fixture does NOT exercise, said out loud

Every one of its 27 loci **resolves**, so D15's ambiguous / both-strand-carry-through branch — the
recall-favouring half of the rule — emits nothing there. `low_order_confidence_fraction: 0.0` is
therefore a property of the input, not evidence the branch works. The report carries
`ambiguity_path_exercised: false` as its own boolean rather than leaving that to be inferred from
a zero, the golden asserts it, and the branch is covered synthetically in the unit tier.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
## An inheritance for P5-01: a locus sitting ON the `min_span` floor is not orientation-stable

Review round 4 asked why contig `039baea1d6be` yields **2** loci forward and **1**
reverse-complemented. Measured, not guessed. Caduceus-PS is RC-*equivariant*, and the two
orientations very nearly agree — mapping the RC posterior back into the forward frame,
`max |Δ(1 − P(bg))|` is **2.5e-2**, mean **9.0e-4**. But equivariance is approximate in floating
point, and **16 of 1,536 positions** land on opposite sides of τ = 0.9 because of it.

One of those 16 decided a locus. Forward, the 5′-most position clearing τ in that cluster is
**536**, so gap-merge yields `[536, 586)` — **exactly 50 nt, exactly `min_span`**, kept by a
single position. Reverse-complemented, 536 (and 540–542) fall below τ, the 5′-most becomes 546,
the run is `[546, 586)` = 40 nt, and `min_span` drops it. The sibling locus `[602, 673)` is 71 nt
and is recovered identically in both orientations.

Not a harness defect, and not a Stage-2 effect — the operating point only sets `confirmed`, it
removes no rows. **P5-01 freezes τ and `min_span`**, and this says a locus at the floor is decided
by one position that an RC residual of ~1e-3 can move, so scanning one strand is not
interchangeable with scanning the other for such loci. Pinned by
`test_the_one_reverse_complement_asymmetry_is_a_min_span_boundary_effect` so the property is
recorded rather than rediscovered.
:::

**Decisions.** No ADR amendment and no §7 sign-off: D3 and D15 are implemented, not changed, and
**no value is pinned** — all eleven knobs on `run_two_stage` are keyword-only with **no default**
(`source_prior`/`target_prior` included, so declining the §11 prior-shift is an explicit `None`),
the `argparse` layer marks each one `required=True`, and `rule.pinned` is `false` in the report.
The Stage-2 operating point used, **0.5**, is the neutral decision boundary of a calibrated
posterior, explicitly *not* D3's "most-liberal posterior with FDP ≤ 10 %", which needs the P5 FDR
machinery. `is_science: false` / `gated: false`: this is a harness regression on a 20-contig
fixture, and P3-16 is the precision comparison.

**Review round 1 (CodeRabbit CLI): 11 findings, 10 real and fixed, 1 refuted by execution.**
The refuted one claimed `tests/fixtures/two_stage/stage1_window_logits.npz` was absent from the
index — `git ls-files`, `git cat-file` on HEAD and the GitHub contents API all report it present
at 520,490 bytes. Two majors were the same defect in two places: **absolute paths in a committed
artifact** (the report writer was already guarded; `scripts/mint_two_stage_fixture.py` was not),
now fixed by making `--context`/`--splits` **repo-relative by contract** with a `--data-root` for
the checkout that holds the data — a worktree has no `data/` of its own, and the obvious fix of
sharing `repo_relative` does not work because it anchors on *its own* checkout. A third was an
**unverified provenance claim**: `attn_implementation_matches_training` was written as a literal
`True`; it is now derived from the loaded model record, and the fixture was regenerated by the
shipped code so the committed artifact is not the old code's output. A fourth caught the
`stage1` leg's docstring claiming the mint check was **"bit-identical"** when it compared
`prediction` only — and could not be bit-identical, since the fixture stores float16. Measured
(max |Δ log-prob| = **4.11e-3**, 0 prediction mismatches), the claim corrected, and a bounded
posterior check added and shown to bite at a forced tolerance of 0. The `integration.smk`
docstring likewise described a no-defaults discipline its own `params` block does not apply;
the module defaults nothing, the rule supplies the fixture's provisional values, and
`--expect-digest` is what makes that safe — now stated accurately rather than aspirationally.

**Review round 2 (CodeRabbit CLI): 6 findings, all minor by label, all real, all fixed — and one
of them was a destructive bug.** `--expect-digest` compared **after** writing, so the single run
the guard exists for — a drift that changes the table — overwrote the committed golden and *then*
reported the mismatch. It now compares first and refuses to write. A second is a definition
correction that leaves the number unchanged and the meaning right:
`n_confirmed_on_wrong_strand_only` read **both** counterfactual verdicts, so a locus whose
*unemitted* opposite strand happened to score well counted as a false novelty — but a false
novelty needs the wrong strand to actually reach a candidate table. Restricted to the **emitted**
strands, and the test that covered it was rewritten, because it had asserted the weaker property:
it now lays the elements out in **reverse** so the resolver genuinely calls `-` against a truth of
`+`, with the unemitted-counterfactual case as its own separate test. Also: `--threshold` parsed
only a float, which made D3's `per_class` **scope unreachable from the CLI** (now a JSON mapping);
`payload_manifest` claimed a `(contig, locus, strand)` order it did not enforce for contigs;
`--context`/`--splits` refused an absolute path but not `..`; and a docstring said 320 nt where
the gap is 340.

::: {.callout-important}
## Review round 3 found the one composition failure that produced a NUMBER instead of an error

`run_two_stage` accepted a **duplicate `contig_id`** and silently merged the two contigs.
`contig_id` keys three things — the payload hash, the diagnostic's per-locus posterior map, and
the Stage-1 lookup — so a duplicate does not collide loudly, it **overwrites**: both contigs
reconcile against one contig's window logits, and the diagnostic reads one contig's posteriors
while attributing them to both. And nothing downstream could see it: `n_loci` and
`n_scored_payloads` are both summed per run, so `n_scored == 2 × n_loci` still held and
`strand_robustness_problems` returned `[]`. **Reproduced before fixing** — two records sharing an
id gave two rows, an empty problem list and an entirely plausible report. The mint script had an
id-uniqueness guard, which protected the *committed fixture* and nothing else; the guard now lives
in a set-level `normalise_contigs` that `run_two_stage`, `read_contigs` and the `payloads` leg all
route through. Table digest unchanged.
:::

**Sabotage found two real gaps.** The invariance denominator (`/n_confirmed` vs `/n_loci`) was
untestable while every fixture locus was confirmed, and the wrong-strand-only counter's `and`
could be relaxed to an `or` while no fixture ever confirmed *both* strands. Two tests now separate
each pair. Two further sabotages were badly aimed rather than gaps — they mutated the source while
their named test read the **committed** JSON, which no source edit can reach. Two more (added
with the r1 fixes) target the **torch-only** mint legs, which no CI-runnable test can execute;
both were verified by **execution** instead — the tolerance check was forced to fail with
`--max-log-prob-delta 0.0`, and the attn-match field was regenerated by the shipped code — and
they are reported as uncovered-by-test rather than counted as bites.

**Commit.** one atomic commit on `p3-14-two-stage`, parent `81b6cd1`.

## Step P3-15 (ENCODE) — 2026-08-05: the fourth spare-rule disjunct, and the refusal that replaces a no-op round

**Inputs.** `mining/spare_rule.py` + `mining/hard_negative.py` + `mining/mine_round.py` (the P2
round, P2-07/P2-10e), `data/processed/mining/round0_fp_manifest.json` (941 FPs), the P2 production
scanner, `eval/tier2n_probe.py`, ADR-0005 D14/A9/A10, ADR-0006 D9 row 5 / D11 / A2, PRD §9.1.

**Process.** ADR-0005 D14 phase-conditions the mining spare rule: three model-independent
disjuncts at P2, **plus a high Stage-2 posterior at the P3 re-mining round**. The pinned predicate
`masking.spare_rule_excludes_from_mining` has carried `stage2_posterior`/`stage2_threshold` since
P2-07 — but *two*-valued. Measured by execution before touching anything: with all three
model-independent disjuncts `failed` and `stage2_threshold=0.9`, a candidate carrying
`stage2_posterior=None` came back **`minable`**. Three of four disjuncts consulted, the answer
called complete. `spare_rule.stage2_status` + `unavailable_disjuncts` close that (unscored ⇒
`unavailable` ⇒ spared — ADR-0005 A10 Pin 3's direction, verbatim), and both `is_mining_excluded`
and `spare_reason` now read the **one** derivation so decision and attribution cannot diverge.
`hard_negative.mine_round` gains the mirror cross-check (a posterior with no declared threshold
raises). `mining/remine.py` is the P3 round driver; `mine_round.load_union_mask` was **promoted**
so both rounds mask through one arithmetic.

**The structural finding, measured.** Sparing is a disjunction; **mining is a conjunction** — a
candidate is mined only when *every* disjunct ran and failed. `relaxed_architecture` and
`downstream_aaRS_synteny` have no backend, so one unavailable disjunct caps the round's yield at
**0** for every candidate, whatever Stage-2 scores. Adding a fourth disjunct cannot relieve this;
it adds a conjunct. The shipped readiness gate still returns `ready=True` (covariation is
protective), which is the "no-op that reports success" state ADR-0005 A10's Phase-2 §7 deferral
recorded at P2. `remine.max_possible_yield` turns it into a computed refusal, and
`plan_remine_round`'s `may_run = readiness ∧ yield` is what `slurm/p3/stage1_remine.sbatch` exits
on — before any GPU time. Executing the sbatch's own `plan` invocation returns **rc=1** with
`max_mined: 0` and all four disjuncts named. The zero is enforced **twice over**: even with the
availability flags forced on, `candidate_evidence` has no path that sets a relaxed-architecture or
synteny status, so the evidence stays `unavailable` and `mine_round` raises on the contradiction.

**Outputs.** `src/tbox_finder/mining/remine.py` (`max_possible_yield`, `plan_remine_round`,
`apply_remine_spare_rule`, `remine_candidate_evidence`, `load_stage2_posteriors`,
`exclude_probe_members`, `remine_problems`, CLI `plan`/`apply-spare-rule`);
`slurm/p3/stage1_remine.sbatch`; `spare_rule.stage2_status`/`unavailable_disjuncts`/
`STAGE2_DISJUNCT`/`ALL_DISJUNCTS`; `mine_round.load_union_mask`; `tests/unit/test_mining_spare_rule.py`.

**Nothing pinned.** The Stage-2 operating point is keyword-only with **no default** and
`argparse required=True`; `no_remine_parameter_has_a_default` re-derives that from the live
signature. `STAGE2_DISJUNCT` is deliberately **outside** `MODEL_INDEPENDENT_DISJUNCTS` and outside
`TIER2N_PROTECTIVE_DISJUNCTS` — folding the project's own model into either would let a P3 round
go green on its own posterior with no model-independent evidence at all.

**Validation.** 44 tests in the new file; full unit+golden **4,240 passed / 13 failed** vs a
**matched baseline worktree** at `96fcbc7` at **4,195 / 13** — failure sets **identical**, `comm`
empty both ways; the +45 is the 44 new tests plus one, and that one is explained: the shipped
`test_sbatch_rm_targets.py` parametrizes over the sbatch inventory and collected the new file
(47 vs 46), passing its tracked-path gate. **21 sabotages, 20 RED against their NAMED test**, the
21st the declared no-op control; each restored by rewriting the original bytes + sha256-verified,
`__pycache__` cleared. ⚠ **One sabotage did not bite first time and the gap was real:** `>=` → `>`
in `stage2_status` left the boundary test green, because that test asserted the *delegated* verdict
— which `masking.py`'s own comparison decides — so this module's comparison was never read. The
test now reads `stage2_status` directly and cross-checks it against the pinned predicate at three
points around the threshold. The campaign was re-run after `black` reformatted `remine.py`.
ruff 0.15.15 + black 25.11.0 clean; no `.smk` touched.

**Decisions.** The RUN is **not** submitted: it is a CLAUDE.md §7 stop (structural-0 yield +
SLURM submit-ack), the P3 inheritance of the ADR-0005 A10 Phase-2 deferral. Cross-link ADR-0005
D14/A9/A10, ADR-0006 A2.

**Commit.** one atomic commit on `p3-15-remine`, parent `96fcbc7`.

## Step P3-15 (review r1) — 2026-08-05: two real findings, one refuted, and a sabotage that had to be re-aimed

**Review r1 (CodeRabbit CLI, 3 findings: 2 major + 1 minor).** The `CodeRabbit` PR check read
`pass` on a *"Review rate limited"* notice — §5.1's trap for the **eighth** step running — so the
CLI carried the gate; no Greptile credit spent.

**Finding 1 (major, real, and worse than reported) — the reverse Stage-2 cross-check was missing,
and it was the fail-OPEN direction.** The first draft guarded only "a posterior with no declared
threshold". The opposite contradiction — a round that *declares* `stage2_threshold` while the
Stage-2 backend is unavailable — left a low posterior resolving to `failed`, so the candidate
counted as *"every disjunct ran and failed"* and was **mined on evidence for a backend the round
said was absent**. Reproduced by execution before fixing: `n_mined = 1`, and the published reason
read *"no disjunct passed and every disjunct was evaluated"* — the attribution asserting the very
thing that was false. The per-disjunct loop iterates `MODEL_INDEPENDENT_DISJUNCTS`, which the
Stage-2 key is deliberately not in, so nothing else covered it. Guard added; the test that had
accepted the shape was rewritten, and both directions now carry a positive control.

**Finding 2 (major, real) — the shipped CLI leg never excluded Tier-2N probe members.**
`probe_set` was optional and `_cmd_apply_spare_rule` never passed one, so `exclude_probe_members`
did not run on the path `stage1_remine.sbatch` invokes, and the report's
`n_excluded_probe_members: 0` read as *"no probe member was in the substrate"* rather than *"no
exclusion happened"* — [[namespace-mismatch-invisible-noop]] again, in my own new code. Both ends
are now unrepresentable: the parameter has **no default**, the CLI flag is `required=True`, the
report carries `n_probe_members_considered` as the denominator a 0 is read against, and
`remine_problems` flags a run round whose denominator is 0. `load_probe_set` additionally
**refuses an empty probe set**, because the committed `reports/p2/tier2n_probe.json` carries
*counts, not member ids* — a loader pointed at it would build an empty set and the exclusion would
report 0 while excluding nothing.

**Finding 3 (minor) — REFUTED by inspection.** *"Confirm `reports/p3` exists before submission"*:
`reports/p3/` is git-tracked (`gate2_figure_data.json`, `stage2_scores.json`, `stage2_sizing.json`,
`sweep/`), so it is present in any checkout including the cluster's, exactly as `slurm/p2/*`
already relies on `reports/p2/`. No change. **Judge the finding and the fix separately** — here the
finding itself did not survive.

**⚠ A sabotage had to be re-aimed, and the gap was real.** Removing the `exclude_probe_members`
call from the shipped round leg left the end-to-end test **green**: its probe set was disjoint
from the substrate, so *"excluded nothing"* and *"never excluded"* were indistinguishable — the
same defect finding 2 named, one level down. The fixture now plants a probe member **in** the
substrate and asserts its **identity** (absent from `reasons`, named in
`excluded_probe_member_ids`, `n_probe_members_considered == 2`), not a count.

**Validation.** 51 tests in the file (44 → 51); full unit+golden **4,247 passed / 13 failed** vs
the matched baseline at `96fcbc7` (**4,195 / 13**) — failure sets identical, `comm` empty both
ways. **26 sabotages, 25 RED against their NAMED test**, the 26th the declared no-op control;
campaign re-run after the fixes and after `black`. ruff 0.15.15 + black 25.11.0 clean.

## Step P3-15 (review r2) — 2026-08-05: three more, all real, all in the guards themselves

**r2-1 (major) — the no-default pin had a hole exactly the shape it exists to catch.**
`no_remine_parameter_has_a_default` treated `None` as *"no default"*, so
`stage2_threshold: float | None = None` would have **passed the pin while giving the operating
point a default**. Confirmed by execution before fixing. The only parameter legitimately needing a
`None` sentinel is `stage2_supply_available`, already exempt by name, so the tightening keeps the
shipped signature green — asserted as the positive control beside the new refusal. Same shape as
[[pinned-constant-that-nothing-reads]]: a pin that cannot fail is decoration.

**r2-2 (minor) — `load_stage2_posteriors` raised a bare `KeyError` on a flat mapping.** Both a
wrapper object and a flat `candidate_id → posterior` map are plausible producer output; the module's
contract is a named refusal carrying the path. Both shapes now load, and a genuinely wrong shape
refuses by name.

**r2-3 (major) — the top-level exclusion fields were never compared to the round's.**
`build_remine_report`'s `excluded_probe_ids` **defaults to `()`**, so a caller that omits it
publishes `n_excluded_probe_members: 0` beside a non-empty round-level list — the same unreadable 0
r1's finding 2 was about, one layer up, and no clause compared them. Reproduced by execution
(top-level `0 / []` beside round-level `['syn1']`, `problems == []`). Clause added, with the
forwarded case as its positive control.

**Validation.** 54 tests in the file (51 → 54); full unit+golden **4,250 passed / 13 failed** vs
the matched baseline at `96fcbc7` (**4,195 / 13**) — failure sets identical, `comm` empty both
ways. **29 sabotages, 28 RED against their NAMED test**, the 29th the declared no-op control.
ruff 0.15.15 + black 25.11.0 clean.

## Step P3-15′-a — 2026-08-05: the covariation-(a) unblock, and a constant that now has to prove itself

**Inputs.** `data/interim/homolog_db.dvc` (md5 `db1ff864…dir`, 10 files, 18.4 GB — the D7/A1
homolog-search target DB, SLURM job 741) · `data/interim/homolog_msa/{provenance.json,
certified_positive.sto}` (the must-fire matched-control certification, job 766) ·
`src/tbox_finder/mining/covariation_producer.py` · `src/tbox_finder/mining/mine_round.py`.

**Process.** Executing the §7 decision of 2026-08-05 (option **b**), and with it two consequences
already signed — ADR-0002's covariation-env amendment (*"a green certification flips
`mine_round.MSA_SUPPLY_AVAILABLE → True`"*) and ADR-0006 **A3**'s cross-reference (*"this supply
flips `msa_supply_available` TRUE, unblocking the round-readiness gate"*) —
`MSA_SUPPLY_AVAILABLE` is now `True`. **No ADR was amended, no threshold moved and no value was
pinned:** the flip performs a decision, it does not make one.

**The flag is a declaration, so it is now checked rather than trusted.**
`derive_msa_supply_available()` re-derives the same fact from the shipped evidence in six
fail-closed clauses — the DB pointer is a well-formed non-empty directory pointer; the producer
imports and exposes its search → align → score chain; a produced status actually *reaches* the
candidate (measured by calling `candidate_evidence`, not by reading a signature); the
certification is green **as a control** (real seed `passed`, shuffled twin `failed`, composition/
depth/width/`SS_cons` matched, depth ≥ `MIN_REAL_HOMOLOG_N` **imported**, not a re-typed 20); that
certification names the DB version the pointer names *today*; and the certified MSA still hashes
to what the run recorded. The unit pin asserts `MSA_SUPPLY_AVAILABLE is derived["available"]`, so
the constant cannot drift from reality in **either** direction — the old `assert … is False` could
only ever have caught one. All three evidence files are git-tracked and neither DVC- nor
LFS-shaped, so the derivation answers identically in CI, on the laptop and on the cluster (it runs
green in this worktree, which has **no** materialised 18 GB DB — repo-level evidence is the claim,
materialisation is separately guarded by `mine_round_producer.sbatch`'s `[ -s "$FM_INDEX" ]`).

**⚠ The flip has two consequences that a flag flip does not look like it has.**
(1) `store_true` with a `True` default is a **one-way** declaration: after the flip nothing could
declare the supply *unavailable*, so a checkout that had not staged the DB would have discovered
the gap in the producer array — after the 8-GPU scan legs. `--no-msa-supply-available` is added
(mutually exclusive with its positive twin). (2) `slurm/p2/mine_round.sbatch` was **self-limiting
because the round was refused**: leg 0 exited before any GPU time. Readiness now *passes*, so that
job would fall through to the scan legs and mine **nothing** — mining is a conjunction and (b)+(c)
still have no backend. Its ⛔ header is rewritten to say so and a required `STRUCTURAL_YIELD_ACK`
turns "do not submit" from prose into a failure.

**Outputs.** `MSA_SUPPLY_AVAILABLE = True`; `derive_msa_supply_available` / `read_dvc_dir_pointer`
/ `msa_supply_declaration_unevidenced`; `plan_round` publishes the derivation beside the claim and
takes `repo_root`; the `plan` and `apply-spare-rule` CLIs **refuse with a distinct exit 4** when a
run declares a supply its own checkout cannot evidence — distinct because `mine_round.sbatch`
converts the clean refusal (3) into `exit 0`, so sharing the code would have turned a staging
fault into a silent "no round today".

**Four stale disclosures corrected, two more than `imp.md` named.** Named: `mine_round.py`'s
docstring and the flag comment; `data/interim/homolog_msa/provenance.json`'s `extra.note` (whose
three claims — producer not composed, legs stubbed, flag False — are all now false; corrected in
place with the superseded text quoted, and **no measured field, input, output or hash touched**).
Not named but falsified by the flip: `slurm/p2/mine_round.sbatch`'s ⛔ header, which told an
operator `MSA_SUPPLY_AVAILABLE=False … Do NOT submit`, and `covariation.py`'s *"the repo has **no**
homolog-search target database … and no `hmmer`/`blast` in any `envs/*.yml`"* — true at P2-10c,
false since job 741 / `envs/homology.yml`.

**Validation.** The gate `imp.md` specifies, asserted as one test: `plan_round(rscape_installed=
True)["ready"] is True` **and** `remine.max_possible_yield` still refuses with `max_mined: 0`,
naming `relaxed_architecture` + `downstream_aaRS_synteny`. **The two gates disagreeing is the
correct state until P3-15′-c/-d land**, so a change that makes them agree in either direction is a
regression and the test says so. 56 tests in `tests/unit/test_mine_round.py` (32 → 56); full
unit+golden **4,272 passed / 15 failed** vs a **matched baseline worktree** at `0b9ad0c`
(**4,248 / 15**) — failure sets **identical**, `comm` empty both ways, and the **+24 is exactly the
new tests**. **25 sabotages, 24 RED against their NAMED test**, the 25th the declared no-op
control; each restored by rewriting the original bytes + sha256-verified, `__pycache__` cleared.
ruff 0.15.15 + black 25.11.0 clean; no `.smk` touched.

**⚠ Two sabotages did not bite first time, and neither was a gap.** (i) Swapping one entry of
`PRODUCER_ENTRY_POINTS` left `align_shard` — the entry the test deletes — still in the tuple, so
the mutation never removed what the test measures; emptying the tuple bites. (ii) *Renaming*
`--no-msa-supply-available` stayed green because **argparse accepts unambiguous prefixes**, so the
old name still parsed against the renamed option — a rename is invisible to any argparse test.
Deleting the argument bites. Both were badly aimed mutations, not missing coverage — but a
campaign that had stopped at "2 misses, close enough" would have recorded the opposite.

**Decisions.** No ADR amendment and no §7 sign-off: this executes ADR-0002's and ADR-0006 A3's
already-signed consequence. ADR-0006 **A2**'s scope-guard correction still reads *"At P2 neither
protective backend exists"* — left untouched, since it is a dated record of the P2 state, not a
current-state claim, and amending signed ADR prose needs sign-off. `slurm/p3/stage1_remine.sbatch`
still gates its `--msa-supply-available` on an operator env var defaulting to `0`; left as is —
stale in the **fail-closed** direction (it can only cause a refusal, never a false ready), and the
P3 RUN's flags belong to P3-15′-b/-d.

**Observed, not changed.** `remine.max_possible_yield` treats *no* `stage2_threshold` as a hard
0, while `spare_rule.unavailable_disjuncts` does **not** count the Stage-2 disjunct as unavailable
when the threshold is `None` — the conservative direction, and its docstring declares it as
policy, so it is recorded here rather than relitigated. It does not affect this step's verdict:
(b) and (c) block the yield on their own.

**Commit.** _(see the squash-merge SHA in `TODO.md`)_

## Step P3-15′-a (review r1) — 2026-08-05: a guard that reported after the side effect it prevents

**CodeRabbit CLI r1: `No findings ✔`** across all six files. **The GitHub app, reviewing the same
commit, returned one — major, and right.** Two independent paths, one finding between them, found
by the path the CLI missed: run both.

**The finding.** `_cmd_plan` wrote `--out` and printed the plan, *then* returned 4. So on a
checkout that cannot evidence the supply, `reports/p2/mine_round_plan.json` was left on disk saying
`ready: true, msa_supply_available: true` — and the §9.3 artifact verify gates on **exactly that
key**. The job exits non-zero and writes no `DONE`, but the stale artifact reads as a good plan.
This is [[guard-runs-after-what-it-guards]] in my own new code, one step after writing a derivation
whose entire purpose is that a declaration cannot outrun its evidence. **Reproduced by execution
before fixing** (rc 4, file present, `ready` `True`).

**The fix is not the one proposed, and the difference is load-bearing.** CodeRabbit suggested
moving the gate above the write, i.e. *not writing at all* on the refusal. That leaves the worse
half of the same hole: a plan from an **earlier, good** run sitting at that path survives untouched
and still reads `ready: true`. The artifact is therefore still written, but with the top-level
`ready` forced `False` and `ready_overridden_by:
"msa_supply_declaration_unevidenced"` naming what overrode it — while the nested `readiness` object
keeps the readiness gate's own untouched verdict (`ready: true`, `refusal_reason: null`). Nothing
is misreported: the top-level key means *"may this round proceed"*, and it may not.
[[review-finding-right-fix-wrong]], fourth occurrence in this repo — judge the finding and the fix
separately. The proposed fix is shipped **as a sabotage** (S29) and is RED against the same test,
which is what "the difference is load-bearing" means operationally.

**One more, self-found before the gate, of the same family.** `certification_green` read the
matched-control flags off the evidence record's **own key set**, so an emptied
`matched_control: {}` had nothing left to be unmatched and certified green — a clause vacuously
satisfied exactly when the evidence is missing. `REQUIRED_MATCHED_CONTROL_FLAGS` names the four
dimensions; a missing key now counts as unmatched. Re-aiming the sabotage this fix staled is how
it stayed honest: the harness reported the stale anchor as a **MISS**, not a pass.

**Validation.** 60 tests (56 → 60); full unit+golden **4,276 passed / 15 failed** vs the matched
baseline worktree at `0b9ad0c` (**4,248 / 15**) — failure sets identical, `comm` empty both ways.
**29 sabotages, 28 RED against their NAMED test**, the 29th the declared no-op control. ruff
0.15.15 + black 25.11.0 clean.

## Step P3-15′-a (review r2) — 2026-08-05: a fail-closed function that could still crash, and a test that was green for nothing

**CodeRabbit CLI r2 (minor), and it is right.** `derive_msa_supply_available` is documented as
fail-closed on *every* clause, but the producer-import handler caught only `ImportError` — a
module-level `RuntimeError` / `OSError` / `AttributeError` anywhere in
`covariation_producer` or its transitive imports would propagate straight out, so `plan` and
`apply-spare-rule` would abort with a **traceback** instead of the exit-4 refusal. A producer too
broken to import is exactly the state the clause exists to report. **Reproduced by execution**
(a `MetaPathFinder` raising `RuntimeError` for that module name) before broadening the handler.

**⚠ AND THE TEST FOR IT WAS VACUOUS ON THE FIRST TRY — GREEN ALONE, MEANINGLESS IN THE FILE.**
It passed in isolation and **failed in the full run**, which is the good direction to fail in.
Cause: `from pkg import sub` **skips the submodule import entirely** when `hasattr(pkg, "sub")`
(CPython's `_handle_fromlist`), and an earlier test in the same file imports the producer, which
sets that attribute on `tbox_finder.mining`. Deleting the `sys.modules` entry is therefore not
enough — the finder never fires and the fixture measures nothing. The attribute is deleted off the
**parent package** too. Had the ordering been the other way round, this would have shipped as a
test that asserts a refusal it never triggers — the [[raises-test-needs-a-positive-control]] family,
reached through an import-system detail rather than an assertion.

**Validation.** 61 tests (60 → 61); full unit+golden **4,277 passed / 15 failed** vs the matched
baseline worktree at `0b9ad0c` (**4,248 / 15**) — failure sets identical. **30 sabotages, 29 RED
against their NAMED test**, the 30th the declared no-op control; S30 restores exactly this
finding (`except Exception` → `except ImportError`) and is RED. ruff 0.15.15 + black 25.11.0 clean.

## Step P3-15′-a (review r3) — 2026-08-05: two more fail-closed holes, both reachable, both measured

**r3-1 (minor) — the DVC-pointer reader could raise instead of returning `None`, twice.** Its
contract is *"`None` on anything unexpected"*, but `read_text(encoding="utf-8")` raises
**`UnicodeDecodeError`** (not an `OSError`) on non-UTF-8 bytes, and `int()` raises **`ValueError`**
past CPython's 4300-digit `str`→`int` cap — `\d+` guarantees *digits*, not that `int` accepts them.
Either escapes `derive_msa_supply_available` and crashes the exit-4 refusal path. **Both reproduced
by execution** before fixing (`UnicodeDecodeError`; `ValueError: Exceeds the limit (4300 digits)`),
and both ship as sabotages (S31, S32) RED against their own parametrised case.

**r3-2 (minor) — a mutation that could silently become a no-op.** The `target_db_versioned` test
mutated the fixture with a literal `replace("nfiles: 10", "nfiles: 0")`, matching only the value
`data/interim/homolog_db.dvc` happens to carry today. A regenerated DB with a different file count
turns that into a no-op: the pointer stays well-formed, the clause stays `True`, and the test fails
with an unrelated message instead of measuring what it names. The count is now **read through the
production reader** and the mutation is asserted to have taken effect — which is what the two
neighbouring pointer tests already did, so this was an inconsistency as much as a latent bug.

**Validation.** 63 tests (61 → 63); full unit+golden **4,279 passed / 15 failed** vs the matched
baseline worktree at `0b9ad0c` (**4,248 / 15**) — failure sets identical, `comm` empty both ways.
**32 sabotages, 31 RED against their NAMED test**, the 32nd the declared no-op control. ruff
0.15.15 + black 25.11.0 clean. CI green on every head so far (`2e2a97a`, `378974f`, `02d178d`,
`7982cc6`) — which also settles the one environment question the derivation raised: `REPO_ROOT`
resolves correctly under CI's editable install, so the evidence-derived pin holds there too.

## Step P3-15′-b — 2026-08-05: the per-candidate Stage-2 posterior producer

**Inputs.** `data/processed/mining/round0_fp_manifest.json` (941 coordinate-only candidates,
git-tracked); `data/interim/production_genomes/*.fna` (2,500, DVC); the P3-06 production arm
`aux1.0_lr1e-4`; `reports/gate2_p3_ece.json` → `gate.calibration.temperature`
= 1.140627294282911, **read, never re-typed**.

**Process.** `src/tbox_finder/mining/stage2_producer.py` composes the shipped primitives and
re-derives none of them: `homolog_msa.resolve_candidate_sequence` → `infer.handoff.transcribe_to_rna`
→ `stage2.eval.score_rows` → `calib.recalibrate.calibrated_posterior`, with the calibrated array
read back through `payload[payload["gated_posterior_key"]]` rather than a literal, so the ADR-0005
D11 indirection has one implementation. `calibrated_posterior` is called with **no priors**, so what
is published is the D11 *named* (temperature-scaled, PRE-prior-shift) object. The span is the **bare
locus**: `stage2/dataset.py` raises on a non-zero flank, so the head was trained and its temperature
fitted on bare loci and there is deliberately no flank knob to decalibrate them with. Four
subcommands (`make-shards` / `score-shard` / `merge` / `control`) reuse `covariation_producer`'s
partition skeleton **by import**; `slurm/p3/stage2_producer.sbatch` runs a 2-task GPU array whose
last-finishing task takes an flock and merges.

**Outputs.** `$ROUND_DIR/stage2_posteriors.json` in the wrapper form `load_stage2_posteriors`
unwraps (the flat form validates every top-level key as a posterior, so no metadata could ride
along); `reports/p3/stage2_producer_control.json`; `remine.STAGE2_SUPPLY_AVAILABLE = True` plus the
two-way `--stage2-supply-available` / `--no-…` flag pair and an exit-4 unevidenced preflight.

**Measured, on all 941 (laptop RTX 4060).** 941/941 resolved, **coverage 1.0000**, 0 unresolved.
2.0 s resolve + 18.9 s load + 38.7 s scoring for 1,882 rows (0.0206 s/row), **1.33 GiB peak VRAM**.
The designed control fires: positive **0.999420**, dinucleotide shuffle **0.000036**, margin
**0.999384**, against floors of 0.90 / 0.10 / 0.50 fixed *before* the measurement.

**Decisions.** (1) **Strand — a §7 fork, resolved on measurement (bioedca, 2026-08-05:
`max_over_strands`).** The manifest carries no strand and Stage-1 is RC-equivariant, so a Stage-1
window asserts no orientation. Scoring both strands of all 941: the minus strand is higher on
**458/941**, and at a 0.9 operating point **119 candidates (12.6 %) pass only on the minus strand** —
`+ = 7e-6` vs `− = 0.9997`. A plus-only reading returns `failed` on those, i.e. a *satisfied mining
conjunct*, on loci Stage-2 calls near-certain T-boxes — exactly what D14 exists to prevent.
`--strand-policy` ships `required=True` with **no default** (D14 pins the rule, the round supplies
the value, as with `--stage2-threshold`), both per-strand posteriors ride in the report, and
`posterior_kind` states in the artifact that a max of two draws is a **selection** on the object
GATE-2 graded. (2) **`STAGE2_THRESHOLD` stays unpinned** — a §13.1 phase-gate value.
(3) The supply derivation reads **only git-tracked, non-DVC evidence**, so CI, laptop and cluster
answer identically; that rules out a "checkpoint on disk" clause and replaces it with a control tied
to the arm's own committed run report.

**⚠ This step does not move the yield.** Mining is a conjunction: `relaxed_architecture` and
`downstream_aaRS_synteny` still have no backend, so `plan_remine_round` reports `ready=True`,
`may_run=False`, `blocking_disjuncts = [relaxed_architecture, downstream_aaRS_synteny]`,
`max_mined = 0`. A change that makes those two gates agree is a regression, and the test says so.

**Validation.** 58 unit + 8 ml-tier tests; full unit+golden+ml **4,818 passed / 14 failed** vs a
matched baseline worktree at `028e508` (**4,755 / 14**) — failure sets identical, `comm` empty both
ways. **39 sabotages, 38 RED against their NAMED test**, the 39th the declared no-op control; a 40th
(`run_control` fabricating its matchedness flags) targets the torch-only tier and was verified by
execution against the real checkpoint, restore sha256-verified. ⚠ Three sabotages initially read
green because their node ids named a *parametrized* test without its parameter and so selected
**zero** tests — the harness now refuses a run that collects nothing, which is the same
"absence reads as a pass" failure the campaign exists to catch. ruff 0.15.15 + black 25.11.0 clean.
