**Review.** **Ten CodeRabbit-CLI rounds; 27 findings, all 27 real** (6 major), then r10 returned
**"No new findings"** and the gate closed. Sequence: 9, 4, 3, 1, 2, 2, 1, 2, 5, 0 — note that it did
**not** decay monotonically; r9 carried two majors after four quiet rounds, so "the last round was
small" was never evidence of convergence. Every major was a hole in a guard rather than in the
science. r1: the supply derivation
could return `available: True` **with a clause missing** — set in the `except` branch *or* the `if`
branch, and with `production_arm_config()` returning `None` while `sweep_fingerprint` succeeded
neither ran, so `all(...)` skipped an absent key (reproduced: 5 of 6 clauses, `available=True`);
two array jobs sharing a `ROUND_DIR` both published to it; and `N_SHARDS=3` with `--array=0-1`
passed the per-task bound check while **nobody merged**. r2: `flock -n` could leave **nobody
merging** even with a matched array (A counts 1 of 2 under the lock, B fails the lock and exits, A
exits on the stale count — reproduced on a harness, fixed by a blocking lock plus a `MERGE_OK`
re-check), and a control record made of **booleans** certified, because `isinstance(True, int)` is
True so `true`/`false` clears both floors and the margin. ⚠ The `CodeRabbit` **check read `pass` on
a rate-limit notice** throughout — §5.1's trap for the tenth step running; no Greptile credit spent
(budget 4/16 used, `available`), since the CLI resets shortly and is free.

**The later rounds kept finding ONE recurring shape, in four different places:** a malformed field
escaping as a traceback instead of the named refusal + `exit 3` (`posteriors` non-mapping at r2;
**coerce-before-validate** at r3, where `true` merged as `1.0` and `"0.5"` as `0.5` and both
*certified*; `strand_posteriors` and `unresolved` at r5). Two more were the emptiness pattern this
repo keeps meeting: the supply derivation could return `available: True` with a clause **missing**
(`all({})` is True), and a duplicate `candidate_id` **inside one shard** collapsed silently while the
cross-shard guard could not see it. r9's two majors were the sharpest: **the control never asserted
the context window**, so an over-length tbdb positive would have certified against *bytes the model
never scored* (the record hashes the full sequence; `score_rows` calls the bare `encode`); and **the
merge never checked that a merged id belongs to this round**, so a foreign shard table could lift
coverage past the very floor the function exists to enforce. ⚠ Also r9: `--min-coverage 0` disabled
the floor outright.

**⚠ The Fair-Usage limit blocked three separate rounds** (41, 37 and 33 minutes) — for a change this
size, budget review in **hours**. And the `CodeRabbit` PR check read `pass` on every one of those
notices, §5.1's trap for the tenth step running; only on the final round did it read
*"Review completed"*.

**Also worth recording: `sbatch --test-only` was green on a job that could not run.** The cluster's
`tbox-ml-rna` has no editable install and the sbatch lacked `PYTHONPATH=src`. The preflight
validates partition/gres/time and nothing about the body, so the §9.3 preflight is **not** evidence
that a job will start doing work — executing the entry point on the login node is.

**Commit.** `8d67169` (step) + `002f235` (PYTHONPATH) + `9594362` (review r1) + `1a4ba52` (review r2),
PR [#111](https://github.com/bioedca/tbox-finder/pull/111)

### Step P3-15′-b RUN — 2026-08-06: SLURM job 1163 (submit-ack given 2026-08-06)

**Submitted** `slurm/p3/stage2_producer.sbatch` at `dbba68f`, `--array=0-1`, one A4000 per task,
`ROUND_DIR=$HOME/tbox-scratch/round_p3_15b`, `STRAND_POLICY=max_over_strands`. Elapsed ≈ 5 min.

**Verification — artifact-based (`sacct` off, CLAUDE.md §9.3 step 8).** `squeue -j 1163` terminal;
`markers_1163/` carries `shard_000.SHARD_OK`, `shard_001.SHARD_OK` **and** `MERGE_OK`; `.owner`
reads `1163`; both shard tables written; `stage2_posteriors.json` reports **941/941, coverage
1.0000, 0 unresolved**, and the in-job readback through `remine.load_stage2_posteriors` accepted
**941 posteriors, range [3.99e-06, 0.999673]`. The two `.err` files are 1,177 B each and carry no
traceback (non-empty on success is expected here and is declared in the header).

**The merge leg behaved as designed under the round-2 fix.** Task 0 finished first, took the
blocking lock, counted `1/2` and deferred; task 1 counted the complete set and merged. That is
precisely the interleaving the pre-fix `flock -n` turned into "nobody merges".

**⚠ MEASURED: the produced posterior is NOT bit-reproducible across device + sharding, and the
spare/mine verdict is sensitive to it only at the boundary.** The cluster table (A4000, 2 shards)
vs the laptop table (RTX 4060, 4 shards) over the same 941 candidates and the same policy — the two
runs differ in **both** device and batch composition, so neither cause is isolated here, and P3-14
already recorded that `score_rows` is batch-position sensitive:

| quantity | value |
|---|---|
| identical values | **0 / 941** |
| median \|Δposterior\| | 1.25e-06 |
| p90 / p99 / max | 1.17e-03 / 1.10e-02 / **3.79e-02** |
| \|Δ\| > 1e-2 | 12 / 941 |
| in the ambiguous band (0.01, 0.99) | 149 / 941 (the rest saturate) |

Verdict flips, cluster vs laptop, by candidate operating point: **0 at 0.5, 0.7, 0.9, 0.95 and
0.999; 3 at 0.99** — and all three sit *on* the threshold (`0.990143` vs `0.989780`, Δ = 3.6e-04;
`0.990059` vs `0.989734`, Δ = 3.3e-04). All three flip in the **spared-on-laptop / mined-on-cluster**
direction, i.e. the fail-open one for those candidates.

**Why this is worth carrying to the §13.1 gate.** `STAGE2_THRESHOLD` is deliberately unpinned, and
this says something about where it may be put: an operating point at **0.99 lands in a region where
3 of 941 candidates are decided by numerics rather than by evidence**, whereas 0.9 decides the same
236 candidates on either machine with a wide margin. The disjunct is a *sparing* one, so a boundary
flip costs at most one spared hard negative — but it is a reproducibility property of the published
column, not of the rule, and a future round that re-runs the producer on different hardware will not
reproduce this table byte-for-byte. The report records `device`, `arm`, `batch_size` and the loader's
`adapter_sha256`/`heads_sha256` so a re-run is comparable rather than merely different.

**Not committed, deliberately.** `$ROUND_DIR` is scratch (`stage1_remine.sbatch:63-64`), so the
table is a run artifact; it was retrieved by `rsync` for this comparison and stays out of git.

## Step P3-15′-c-i — 2026-08-06: is the (c) synteny backend supplyable from NCBI annotation?

**Inputs.** `data/processed/audits/production_fetch_report.json` (git-tracked, 2,500
`per_genome` rows written by `mining/pilot_fetch.py` at P2-10c′-fetch — each carrying the
`source_url` its `_genomic.fna.gz` was fetched from); `data/processed/mining/round0_fp_manifest.json`
(941 candidates); `mine_round.load_admissible_accessions()` → the 660 a2 hosts.

**Process.** `src/tbox_finder/mining/annotation_supply.py` measures whether ADR-0006 **D4** can
be supplied without a gene caller. It introduces **no transport**: the annotation lives in the
same NCBI directory as the genome this repo already fetched, so the probe is a *sibling lookup
on a committed URL* and `esearch`/`esummary` are never called. One GET of each assembly's
`md5checksums.txt` returns that directory's complete file list plus checksums, so one request
answers every suffix at once. An assembly is `annotated` **iff** it serves
`<basename>_genomic.gff.gz`; the outcome is three-valued (`annotated` / `unannotated` /
`unknown`) and a transport failure is `unknown`, never folded into `unannotated`. The route rule
is **pre-registered in the module above the measurement** (§10.3) and is a function of counts
alone. A control runs beside every sweep: a fixed assembly that must resolve *and* be annotated,
plus that same directory with its accession corrupted, which must not resolve.

**Outputs.** `reports/p3/annotation_supply.json` (216 KB, git-tracked, no DVC object) —
per-assembly status, GFF URL, GFF md5, GFF `Content-Length`, `_protein.faa.gz` presence, plus the
counts, the control and the derived route. 97 unit tests. No ADR amendment, no value pinned, no
SLURM job, LOCAL only.

**Measured, all 660, zero unknown, control powered** (positive `GCF_000007185.1` → 16 files,
annotated; negative → 404):

| set | annotated | unannotated | unknown |
|---|---|---|---|
| 660 admissible hosts | **339** (51.4 %) | 321 | 0 |
| 76 candidate-carrying assemblies | **48** (63.2 %) | 28 | 0 |
| 941 candidates, by their host | **655** (69.6 %) | 286 | 0 |

Cross-tabulated against the accession prefix — the proxy `imp.md` framed the question with:

| | annotated | unannotated |
|---|---|---|
| `GCF_` (115) | **115 (100 %)** | 0 |
| `GCA_` (545) | **224 (41.1 %)** | 321 |

**Decisions.** (1) **The prefix proxy is sound in one direction only, and the route it implied is
wrong.** `imp.md` P3-15′-c-i pre-committed that *"if the GCA share is large, `prodigal` is
required after all ⇒ an ADR-0002 env amendment"*. The GCA share **is** large — 545 of 660,
82.6 % — but **224 of those 545 GenBank assemblies already ship a GFF**, so the implication does
not hold: acting on the proxy would have commissioned an env amendment while 41 % of the
GenBank hosts were already supplied. Every `GCF_` is annotated (115/115), which is why the proxy
looked plausible. (2) **The route is `mixed`, and `mixed` does not block the round.** Mining is a
conjunction, so a host with no annotation makes (c) `unavailable`, and an unavailable disjunct
*spares* its candidates under ADR-0005 D14 — it never mines them. The NCBI-GFF route therefore
supplies (c) for 655 of 941 candidates outright; `prodigal` would raise that ceiling to 941
rather than make the round possible. Whether to pay for the remaining 30.4 % is a CLAUDE.md §7
call, not an implementation detail, and it is left open here. (3) **`_genomic.gbff.gz` is not
evidence of annotation** — NCBI serves one for unannotated assemblies too (measured on the real
`GCA_000372225.1`: a gbff and a wgsmaster gbff, no gff). Keying on it would have called all 660
annotated. A unit test pins the distinction. (4) **D4's Pfam/KO fallback has its protein input
exactly where the GFF is** — `_protein.faa.gz` is present on 339 assemblies and absent on 321,
matching the GFF partition one-for-one, so no separate acquisition is needed for the
hypothetical/pseudogene arm. The profile database itself is still absent and remains owed.
(5) **The acquisition is not a SLURM job.** Measured `Content-Length` over all 339 annotated
hosts: **68,855,450 B = 68.9 MB** total (min 33,003 / median 177,764 / max 898,247), of which
**9.5 MB** covers the 48 candidate-carrying hosts. At the shipped 3 req/s that is minutes of
wall on the laptop — LOCAL by §9.1 — so the "SLURM acquisition ack" this block was gated on does
not apply to the NCBI route.

**Review (two paths, and they overlapped by one).** The CodeRabbit **CLI** returned **3
majors** and the GitHub **app** returned **2**, on the same commit, with **one in common** —
running both was worth it rather than redundant, the P3-15′-a lesson recurring. All five are
real and all five are fixed. (i) *Shape assumed before validated*, twice: a list-rooted fetch
report makes `payload.get` an `AttributeError`, and a non-Mapping candidate row makes
`row["accession"]` a `TypeError` — both escape as a traceback and **exit 1** instead of the
documented refusal and **exit 3**, the same shape P3-15′-b hit four times. (ii) *A route
certified from an understated candidate denominator*: `cand_rows` silently drops a candidate
host absent from the probed set, and `sweep_complete` compares only the **admissible**
denominator — the guard that already existed for the admissible set had no counterpart for the
candidate set. Found by **both** paths, at different layers: the CLI at the derivation, the app
at the API input. Both are now guarded. (iii) *`urlopen` reachable with an arbitrary scheme and
host*: `source_url` flows from a committed report into `urlopen`, so a `file://` or third-party
value would be a local-file read or an off-host request. An allowlist on **scheme and host**
(not a substring — `https://evil.test/?x=ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov` defeats that, and
`ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov.evil.test` defeats a prefix test) is enforced where URLs are built **and
at the transport boundary**, because `fetch_file_manifest`/`head_content_length` are public and
take a URL directly — guarding only the builders leaves the actual boundary open. (iv) *The
`(accession, source_url)` pair was never checked to agree*: the row is **labelled** with the
accession but **classified** from whatever directory the URL names, so a mis-joined pair yields
well-formed evidence filed under the wrong assembly, never surfaces as `unknown`, and moves the
counts the route is read from ([[namespace-mismatch-invisible-noop]]). The app's committable
suggestion raised while its agent prompt said to return `unknown`; **raising is right** — a
mis-join is a join error, not a per-host unknown, and degrading it to `unknown` would hide a
systematically mis-joined mapping behind 660 uninformative rows
([[review-finding-right-fix-wrong]], judged separately again). Verified on the real data before
committing: **0 binding violations across all 2,500 `ok` rows** and 0 host-allowlist violations.

**One defect found without a reviewer.** The retry loop had **no backoff** — `pilot_fetch` waits
`1.5 * (attempt + 1)`, and the rate limiter is not a substitute: it meters the steady state at
3 req/s, so a 429 would have been re-sent four times inside ~1.3 s, which is precisely what the
limiter exists to prevent. Added, with the schedule asserted and a companion test that a
*permanent* failure does **not** sleep (660 pointless waits is the difference between a
two-minute sweep and a twenty-minute one).

**Review round 2 — both paths converged on ONE defect, and it was mine.** `run_control`
declared a `sleep` parameter and forwarded it to neither control leg, so a caller injecting a
fake clock still blocked on the real `time.sleep` — and **no test observed it**, because none
made the control retry ([[pinned-constant-that-nothing-reads]]: a parameter a function accepts
and never reads is a parameter nothing tests). It was introduced by my own backoff fix, whose
threading patch had silently not applied at those two call sites because `black` had already
collapsed them to one line — a `.replace` that matched nothing and said nothing. The CLI graded
it **minor**, the app **major**. ⚠ The app also prescribed the assertion `[1.5, 3.0]`; the real
schedule is `[1.5, 3.0, 4.5]` **per leg** (`retries=4` ⇒ three waits, 9.0 s, which is the very
number its own prose quoted), so the finding was right and the value wrong again — derived here
by execution rather than transcribed.

**Measured, and it is the number the §7 call turns on: annotation coverage is strongly
clade-structured.** Joining the per-assembly status to `production_host_orders_v0.parquet`
(`resolved_phylum`), the annotated fraction across the 660 ranges from **0.10 in Calditrichota
(1/10)** and 0.21 in Bacteroidetes (4/19), 0.25 in Nitrospinota, 0.30 in Campylobacterota, up to
**0.75 in Methanobacteriota (56/75)** and 0.79 in Fusobacteria. So the annotation-driven recall
cap the NCBI route implies is **not uniform** — it falls hardest on exactly the under-annotated
lineages the discovery aim lives in. ADR-0006 **D4** already requires a *"false-FAIL rate +
per-clade (c)-exclusion + pseudogene diagnostic … symmetric with the false-pass rate"*, so this
is that diagnostic's first data point rather than a new obligation; the full version is a
`-c-ii` deliverable. It is deliberately **not** folded into
`reports/p3/annotation_supply.json`: reading the parquet needs pandas, and the module is a
bare-CI-tier, pure-stdlib probe.

**Review round 3 — the two paths disagreed about whether there was anything left.** The GitHub
app reviewed `69cde0b→35712d1` and returned *"No actionable comments"*; the **CLI, on the same
head, returned two more — one of them a major**. A clean round on one path is not convergence.
(i) **`urlopen` follows redirects, and the allowlist checked only the initial URL**, so a 302
moves the request off-host one hop past the guard. Fixed with a redirect handler that
re-validates every hop, installed on a single shared opener both transport helpers use — and an
allowlist violation now *propagates* instead of being caught by the transient-retry arm, because
retrying it four times and reporting the host `unknown` would read as "NCBI was flaky" rather
than "this run was pointed somewhere it must never go". (ii) **A duplicate accession was not
refused** — it is probed twice, `by_acc` collapses it, `len(rows)` counts it, so it inflates
`n_probed`, the prefix tally and the status counts, i.e. every denominator the route is read
against, while doubling that host's request cost. It is the exact mirror of the silently-dropped
accession the module already refuses, and it now refuses the same way, for both the admissible
and the candidate sequence.

**Reproducibility, measured three times.** The sweep was re-run end-to-end after each fixing
round — three independent 999-request sweeps on three different code versions — and **all 660
measured rows are byte-identical** every time. The only fields that move between runs are
`generated_at_utc` and the provenance `git_sha`.

**Review round 4 — and the worst finding in the whole step was in my own tests.** Three
end-to-end tests **were making real HTTP requests to live NCBI**, directly contradicting this
file's own docstring claim of *"no network"*: they passed `opener=` but not `header=`, and
`measure_sizes` defaults on, so the size pass fell through to the real `_urlhead_length`.
Nothing went red — a failed HEAD yields `None` and no assertion reads a size — so the cost was
hidden runtime and offline flakiness behind a docstring asserting the opposite. **Verified by
execution before fixing: 30 real requests, 45 s.** Two further minors, both the
already-familiar shape: `payload["candidates"]` raises `KeyError` on an object lacking the key
(exit 1 + traceback instead of exit 3 + the refusal), and a *conflicting* duplicate accession in
`per_genome` silently overwrote the first, so the sweep would report whichever directory
survived as that accession's evidence with no record a conflict existed — the mirror, at the
load boundary, of the duplicate guard round 3 added one layer up.

**⚠ The structural fix for the network leak was itself a no-op on the first attempt.** Patching
the three call sites is not enough — the docstring's claim needs *enforcing*, so an autouse
fixture now replaces both transport primitives with a raising stub. The first version raised
`AssertionError` and **the suite still went to the network and still reported 89 passed**, in
**22.66 s** instead of 0.17 s: the transport wraps its calls in `except Exception`, converts the
failure to a retry and then to `None`, and so **swallowed the guard's own signal**. The stub now
raises a `BaseException` subclass, which `except Exception` cannot absorb. Verified both ways by
execution — with the guard armed and one `header=` injection removed, the suite goes RED in
0.21 s naming the leaked URL. *A guard whose signal the subject can absorb is not a guard.*

**Review round 5 — a gate leaning on an invariant enforced somewhere else.** The route
derivation checked only the **admissible** unknown count, and took its denominator from a sum it
never reconciled with `n_candidate_hosts`. So a report declaring 76 candidate hosts, 76 probed
and zero admissible-unknown could still carry an unknown *candidate* host and come back `mixed`
with no refusal — and an annotated fraction could be read against a base that is not the number
of candidate hosts. In a report this module writes neither can happen, because the candidate
rows are a subset of the probed rows; that is precisely the point
([[gate-clauses-need-re-derivation]]). Both clauses added, both sabotaged.

**Review round 6 — a refusal that recorded a wrong number.** The unprobed-candidate reason was
built from a `-1` sentinel, so with the field *absent* it announced `n_cand + 1` hosts unprobed,
and with a probed count above `n_cand` it announced a negative one. The refusal was correct
either way; the number in it was not, and a number in a recorded reason is one a later reader
acts on. It now states the measured pair, and a missing field gets its own distinct reason.
Round 6 also applied the app's round-4 nitpick: the mixed end-to-end test asserted only
`n_candidate_hosts == 2` while claiming a 1-annotated / 1-unannotated split, so a regression in
candidate classification could hide behind the full admissible sweep.

**Review round 7 — the refusal contract had a hole in its own arithmetic.** `derive_acquisition_route`
is handed an arbitrary report, and every count was read with a bare `int()`, which raises on a
non-numeric field and so escapes as a traceback and **exit 1** instead of the documented refusal
and **exit 3** — the shape this suite already treats as a defect two files over. Fixed with a
single `_as_count`, and **stricter than the reviewer proposed**: a real `int` only, `bool`
excluded (`isinstance(True, int)` is True), `float` and `str` excluded, because coercing `"76"`
or `76.0` into a count is precisely the coerce-before-validate mistake P3-15′-b shipped, where
`"0.5"` merged as `0.5` and *certified*. A count that is not an int means the report is
malformed, and the honest answer is a refusal naming the field.

**Validation.** 97 unit tests; **44 sabotages, 43 RED against their named test**, the 44th a
declared no-op control. The measurement was **re-run end-to-end on the reviewed code** and
reproduced byte-identically — 339/321, 48/28, 68,855,450 B — on an independent second sweep of
999 requests. Two of the original 23 did not bite first time and neither was noise: the
`run_control` refusal was satisfied by *any* `AnnotationSupplyError` — deleting the guard still
raised, one frame down, from `assembly_basename("")` — so a bare `pytest.raises` was passing on a
crash rather than on the named refusal (test now matches the message,
[[raises-test-needs-a-positive-control]]); and the "never HEAD an unannotated host" property is
defended **twice** (the annotated filter *and* `head_content_length`'s empty-URL early return), so
neither edit alone could falsify it and the sabotage is declared compound. Full unit+golden
**4,470 passed / 13 failed** against a matched baseline worktree at `8a82425` (**4,373 / 13**) —
failure sets **identical**, `comm` empty both ways, and the +97 is exactly the new tests. ruff
0.15.15 + black 25.11.0 clean; no `.smk` touched. §6.4 fires on nothing (no README,
`paper/manuscript.qmd` or ADR reference to the new API). The shipped refusal path was executed,
not inferred: `measure --limit 5` exits **3** with `route=refused`, and the report it writes
carries the refusal inside it rather than a verdict a later reader could mistake for a pass.

**Commit.** see `TODO.md` for the squash SHA on `main` (PR #112).

## Step P3-15′-c-i (acquisition) — 2026-08-06: fetch the 339 annotated hosts' GFF, and read a coordinate

**Inputs.** `reports/p3/annotation_supply.json` — the committed measurement half of this step,
which already carries every annotated host's `gff_url` **and** the `gff_md5` NCBI publishes for
it. **Process.** Two new pure-stdlib modules. `src/tbox_finder/mining/annotation_fetch.py`
downloads each of the 339 annotated hosts' `*_genomic.gff.gz`, verifies it against the committed
md5, and stores it **byte-identical to what NCBI served** (never decompressed, never rewritten) so
`md5(file) == report.gff_md5` stays checkable forever; `src/tbox_finder/mining/gff3.py` parses
GFF3 into CDS features. There is **no URL discovery at all** — no `esearch`, no `esummary`, not
even a directory listing — so the acquisition adds no transport. `annotation_supply`'s redirect
allowlist was **promoted** to a public `build_allowlisted_opener()` rather than copied, so "both
modules re-check every redirect hop" stays one claim instead of two that can drift.
**Outputs.** `data/interim/production_annotations/` (339 files, 68,855,450 B, DVC `md5
8fe382680893cba0e045c0017749cee2.dir`); `reports/p3/annotation_fetch.json`;
`reports/p3/annotation_parse.json`; 180 new unit tests; the real 33,003 B
`tests/fixtures/annotation/GCA_002790315.1.gff.gz`.

**Measured, and this is the part `-c-ii` will build on.** 339/339 acquired, 0 md5 mismatches, and
the bytes on disk sum to **exactly 68,855,450** — reproducing the supply report's independently
measured `Content-Length` total, a cross-check between two runs that never shared a number.
Offline re-verification parses all 339: **897,096 CDS across 44,291 contigs**, every one with a
resolved strand and non-empty gene-identity text; **11,671 (1.30 %) carry `pseudo=true`**, which is
the population ADR-0006 D4 routes to its Pfam/KO fallback, now counted rather than assumed; **273
CDS span more than one row**; and **0 of 339 carry a `##FASTA` section** (NCBI does not emit one —
bakta/prokka will, which is why the parser stops dead at the directive).

**Three things the real data settled that synthetic fixtures would not have.** (1) **Multi-row
CDS is real here** — a per-row reading would have invented 273 genes that do not exist and put a
spurious "CDS start" in the middle of each, so grouping by `ID` is correctness, not tidiness.
(2) **Attribute values are URL-escaped**: `country=USA: Crystal Geyser near Green River%2C Utah`
is a real value from the fixture, which is why the split order (`;` → `=` → `,` → unescape) is
load-bearing — unescaping first shatters one product name into two. (3) **D4 measures to the CDS
*start codon*, which on a `-` strand is the feature's `end`, not its `start`** —
`cds_start_position` is the only sanctioned way to ask, and it **refuses** an unresolved strand
rather than defaulting to `+` on exactly the divergent loci where the §6 resolver is least sure.

**The control had to be rebuilt, because the first version could not fail.** The md5 control's
negative legs were written inline as `md5_hex(payload + b"\x00") != expected_md5` — which asserts
only that md5 has no collisions. True, and completely uninformative about this code: the legs
could not go False whatever the acquisition did, so a hardcoded `True` was behaviourally
indistinguishable from a computed one, and the sabotage campaign said so by **not biting**. Fixed
by extracting the single comparator `digest_matches` that `fetch_one`, `parse_census` and all
three control legs now share: a comparison that always answers True makes both negative legs fail
and the control reports **itself** unpowered ([[control-matchedness-must-be-asserted]]).

**A second sabotage miss was a `pytest.raises` passing on the wrong refusal.** The allowlist check
sat *behind* the GFF-suffix check, so it was unreachable for any URL not ending in
`_genomic.gff.gz` — and deleting the allowlist entirely left the test green, because the suffix
rule refused first. The order is now allowlist-first, every URL in that test ends in the suffix
and carries the right accession so **only** the allowlist can refuse it, and the assertion matches
the message ([[raises-test-needs-a-positive-control]], again).

**Validation.** 180 new unit tests (65 GFF3 + 115 acquisition); **57 sabotages, 56 RED against
their named test**, the 57th a declared no-op control that stayed green. The harness refuses a run
that collects zero tests — which is what caught four of my own node ids naming a parametrized test
without its parameter, exactly the "absence reads as a pass" failure the campaign exists to find.
The acquisition was **re-run end-to-end on the reviewed code with `--force`** — a second
independent 339-file download, 678 in total — and both reports are **byte-identical** except
`generated_at_utc` and the provenance `git_sha`. Full unit+golden **4,422 passed / 13 failed**
against a matched baseline worktree at `2be5ff4` (**4,242 / 13**) — failure sets **identical**,
`comm` empty both ways, and the +180 is exactly the new tests. ruff 0.15.15 + black 25.11.0 clean;
no `.smk` touched; no `envs/*` touched and no dependency added beyond the standard library, so
the ADR-0002 amendment the annotator arm needs is **not** triggered by this half. §6.4 fires on
nothing (no README, `paper/manuscript.qmd` or ADR reference to the new API).

**Decisions.** The step block frames this as "a suffix extension of `mining/pilot_fetch.py`". It
is not built there, deliberately: `pilot_fetch` is Entrez-dependent (biopython, which CI does not
install), has **no URL allowlist at all**, and its `validate_report` re-derives a fixed row schema,
so adding GFF fields means lockstep edits to `GENOME_COLS`, `build_report`, `genome_digest` and the
validator — for a fetch that needs none of its e-utils machinery. A sibling module reusing
`annotation_supply`'s guards is the same cheap path with a smaller blast radius, and it stays in
CI's bare tier where the sabotage campaign can reach it. Cross-links: ADR-0006 D4 (the predicate
this supplies coordinates for), D9 row 5 (Tier-2N), ADR-0005 D14 (an unavailable disjunct spares).

**Commit.** see `TODO.md` for the squash SHA on `main`.

**Review (this step's gate).** Two CodeRabbit rounds, both paths. The GitHub app reviewed the
first push **unasked**, so automatic review is ENABLED right now — detected on this PR, not
recalled, because CLAUDE.md §5.1 records that setting inverting twice already. r1 returned
**9 findings across the two paths** (CLI 7, app 2) of which **6 were real**; r2 returned 2, of
which **1 was real**. The remaining three were the same false positive raised three times, and
it is worth recording how it was settled: *"a clean checkout does not contain the GFF3
fixture"*, escalating to *"59,693 bytes with header `1f ef`, neither valid gzip nor an LFS
pointer"*. `1f ef` **is** `1f 8b` after a lossy text round-trip, so the sandbox was mangling the
binary; the blob on the pushed remote reads `1f 8b` at 33,003 B, and a fresh
`git clone --depth 1` of the branch runs all 180 new tests green. Refuted by execution rather
than by argument — and then turned into a permanent guard, with a **positive control**, since
deleting an assertion can never fail its own test.

**The two findings worth keeping.** (1) The app caught that **ID-less CDS rows at *identical*
coordinates collapsed into one feature** — my own test used rows at *different* coordinates, so
the coordinate-derived fallback key already distinguished them and the merge was invisible to
it. Grouping is now on a **declared** `ID` only. (2) The CLI caught that
**`annotation_parse.json` was generated two minutes *before* the `annotation_fetch.json` it
claims to describe**, and declared only the supply report as an input — so nothing in either
artifact could show the census parsed the files the acquisition validated. Both reports now
carry a **`corpus_digest`** over their own `(accession, md5)` pairs, `verify` refuses when they
disagree, and the refusal **names which of the two failure modes fired** — because collapsing
"no digest declared" and "digests differ" into one `False` made the first half of the check
unable to change any outcome, which is the same unfalsifiable-clause shape the md5 control had
to be rebuilt to escape.

**Validation after review.** **70 sabotages, 68 RED against their named test**, 2 declared
no-op controls. Full unit+golden **4,438 passed / 13 failed** against the matched baseline at
`2be5ff4` (**4,242 / 13**) — failure sets **identical**, `comm` empty both ways. The
acquisition was re-run end-to-end **four** times (`--force`, 1,356 downloads in total) and the
reports reproduce byte-identically except `generated_at_utc` and the provenance `git_sha`; the
final pair was produced in the correct order, `fetch` then `verify` 31 s later, with matching
corpus digests.

**⚠ MERGE GATE UNMET — GitHub Actions was in a `major_outage` for the whole of this step**
(githubstatus.com components API), so **no CI run was created for any push on this branch**;
the newest run in the repo predates the branch. Actions is enabled and the `CI` workflow is
`active` with `branches-ignore: [main]`, so this is infrastructure, not configuration. A
missing run is an **absence, not a pass** — the same rule §5.1 records for a CodeRabbit
rate-limit notice — so the PR is left open rather than merged. Locally the CI-exact tooling was
run in full: ruff 0.15.15 + black 25.11.0 clean, and the whole unit+golden tier green against
the matched baseline.

**Review round 3 — two findings that made the parser stricter, and one that closed a
self-certification loop.** (1) `iter_gff3_features` *skipped* `##gff-version` instead of
requiring it, so any nine-column TSV parsed as GFF3. A strict `parse_gff3_document` now
requires the directive first and refuses an unsupported major version; the census uses it,
while the line-level `parse_gff3_cds` stays lenient for the unit tests that drive it with bare
feature lines. All **339** real NCBI files pass the new check. (2) Merging a multi-row CDS was
**first-wins**, so a `pseudo=true` or `product=` written only on the *second* row of a
frameshifted CDS was discarded — which would have silently undone `is_pseudo`'s
read-every-value contract one layer up, leaving the CDS with no `pseudo` at all. Values now
append in segment order. (3) The census read `corpus_digest` out of the fetch report **without
validating it**, so a hand-edited report could declare whatever the census had just computed
and the binding would certify itself; `validate_fetch_report` now re-derives the digest from
its own rows as a clause, and the census refuses any fetch report that fails *any* clause.
The corpus census is unchanged by all three (897,096 CDS / 11,671 pseudo / 273 multi-segment),
so the stricter reader accepts exactly the same real corpus.

**Final validation.** **76 sabotages, 74 RED against their named test**, 2 declared no-op
controls. Full unit+golden **4,447 passed / 13 failed** vs the matched baseline at `2be5ff4`
(**4,242 / 13**) — failure sets **identical**, `comm` empty both ways. ruff 0.15.15 + black
25.11.0 clean.

**Review round 4 — five more, and the counts never converged: 9, 2, 4, 5.** The most
interesting was an identity collapse: `urllib.parse.unquote` defaults to `errors="replace"`,
so `%FF` and `%FE` both decode to U+FFFD and two CDS records carrying those as `ID` **merge**
in `group_cds` — [[duplicate-key-merges-instead-of-colliding]] a third time in this step, now
at the level of the identity itself. Decoding is strict, and a `%` not followed by two hex
digits is refused outright (GFF3 requires a literal percent to be written `%25`). Also: the
census hashed a byte snapshot and then **re-opened the path to parse it**, so an md5 and a CDS
census could describe different bytes — it now parses the snapshot it verified; the cache write
was non-atomic and its `OSError`s escaped as tracebacks rather than per-assembly failed rows;
`##gff-version3` (no separator) satisfied `startswith`; and a `CDS` with `phase=.` was accepted
though GFF3 requires one. That last was checked against the corpus before being enforced —
**0 of 897,369 real CDS lines omit a phase**, so the stricter rule refuses nothing real.

**A third dead guard, found the same way.** The fix for the non-atomic write added a
`startswith(".")` filter to the orphan sweep — which can never fire, because the temp name ends
in `.part` and the sweep globs `*.gff.gz`. The sabotage did not bite, the filter was removed,
and the property was moved to where it is real: `_temp_name` must not end in `.gff.gz`, which
is what the test now asserts.

**Final validation.** **85 sabotages, 83 RED against their named test**, 2 declared no-op
controls. Full unit+golden **4,458 passed / 13 failed** vs the matched baseline at `2be5ff4`
(**4,242 / 13**) — failure sets **identical**, `comm` empty both ways; +216 exactly the new
tests. The corpus census is **unchanged under every tightening** (897,096 CDS / 11,671 pseudo /
273 multi-segment / 44,291 contigs), so the stricter reader accepts precisely the same real
corpus the lenient one did. ruff 0.15.15 + black 25.11.0 clean.

**Review round 5 — 5 findings, all 5 real, and the counts went 9, 2, 4, 5, 5.** Five rounds in,
the round size has stopped falling; "the last round was small" was never evidence of anything
here. Two of the five are the same species this step keeps producing — **a check that compares
a thing with itself**.

**The major: the acquisition gate could not tell WHICH corpus it had fetched.** Every
cross-report clause — `n_targets` against `n_annotated_in_supply_report`, `bytes_total` against
`bytes_total_in_supply_report`, `every_ok_row_md5_matches` comparing a row's observed md5 with
that same row's expected one — compares numbers the report's own writer copied into it. A
self-consistent report about a *different* 339-assembly corpus therefore passes all of them and
`fetch` exits **0**, with only the later `verify` in a position to notice. `validate_fetch_report`
now takes the supply targets as a **required, no-default** keyword and re-derives a
`rows_bind_to_targets` clause over accession, URL **and** expected md5; the no-default is the
point, since `targets=()` would restore exactly the vacuous-clause shape
([[clauses-must-guard-emptiness]]) at every future call site. Adding a clause invalidates every
report written under the old set, so the set is now versioned (`CLAUSE_SCHEMA_VERSION = "2"`,
re-checked by its own clause) and both committed reports were regenerated
([[new-gate-clause-invalidates-old-reports]]).

**A consequence worth recording rather than hiding.** With the identity clause in place, a
*validating* fetch report can no longer describe other bytes — its digest is determined — so the
`corpus_digest` comparison's remaining job is the other direction: the **files on disk** moving
under an honest report. The r2 test was rewritten to assert the earlier refusal, and a second
test now exercises the digest on its own terms.

**Two `OSError`s that were refusals everywhere except where they were raised.** The control
file's `read_bytes` sat outside any handler, so a filesystem fault destroyed the very report
that would have said the run was untrustworthy (exit 1, no artifact) instead of yielding an
unpowered control and exit 3; and the census read sat *above* the `except OSError` written for
it, so one unreadable file among 339 aborted all 339 verdicts.

**Two parser over-acceptances.** `##FASTA` was matched case-folded and whitespace-stripped, so
`##fasta` or an indented variant would terminate the feature section and drop every CDS below it
**silently** — the one failure mode this reader refuses to have. Now exact
(`is_fasta_directive`, shared with the census so the two cannot diverge). And `group_cds` keyed
declared IDs and coordinate-derived fallbacks in one string space, so a declared
`ID=ctg1:10-20:+:CDS#0` merges with the ID-less row it names; the key is now a
`(namespace, value)` pair — [[duplicate-key-merges-instead-of-colliding]], a fourth distinct
instance in this one step.

**Final validation.** **14 sabotages, 14 RED against their named test** (the fourteenth was
declared a no-op — the census/parser `##FASTA` alignment — and was converted into a real test
rather than recorded as a non-bite). Full unit+golden **4,477 passed / 15 failed** vs a matched
baseline worktree at `2be5ff4` (**4,240 / 15**) — failure sets **identical**, `comm` empty both
ways. (The 15 is this environment's baseline, not a regression: it has no `pyarrow`, which is
2 more than the 13 recorded in earlier stanzas from an env that did.) The corpus census is
**byte-identical under every round-5 tightening** — 897,096 CDS / 11,671 pseudo / 273
multi-segment / 44,291 contigs — so the stricter reader still accepts exactly the same real
corpus. ruff 0.15.15 + black 25.11.0 clean; no `.smk` touched.

**Review round 6 — 5 more, all 5 real: 9, 2, 4, 5, 5, 5.** Three of the five are the same
species as round 5's pair, one layer further out: an input read from **outside** this process
that reaches a coercion or an unguarded read before any clause sees it.

**The major.** `validate_fetch_report` re-derived the byte total with `int(r.get("n_bytes") or 0)`
— and it reads an **on-disk** report (`parse_census` validates the committed one), so a
hand-edited or truncated `n_bytes` aborted `verify` with a `ValueError` and exit 1 instead of
returning the refusal the module exists to return. It would equally have accepted `"12"` as 12,
the coerce-before-validate shape `strict_count` was written for one function above. The counts
are now validated, and both byte clauses go False rather than raising.

**`read_supply_report` converted only `FileNotFoundError`.** A directory path, a permission
error or a non-UTF-8 file escaped as a traceback; `parse_census` inherits the fix, so an
unreadable fetch report is now a refusal *reason inside the census* rather than the end of it.

**The control's flip was case-dependent — and the failure was in the control itself.**
`digest_matches` lowercases the expectation but the flip did not, so on an uppercase digest
`"B3F…"` the "corrupted" value `"b3F…"` compared **equal**, `corrupt_expectation_fails` read
False, and the control declared itself unpowered on correct bytes. Latent (production
lowercases), but a control whose verdict turns on the caller's capitalisation is not measuring
the acquisition — the opposite direction of [[control-matchedness-must-be-asserted]], and just
as disqualifying.

**Two more "the docstring was stricter than the code".** `require_gff3_version` skipped leading
blank lines while claiming the directive must come *first* — measured before tightening, as with
the CDS-phase rule: **339 of 339** acquired files carry `##gff-version 3` as line 1, so the
strict reading refuses nothing real. And `CdsFeature.segments` was annotated as a tuple of pairs
but accepted a **list**, leaving the coordinates D4 measures from mutable behind `frozen=True`;
it is normalised in `__post_init__` alongside the attributes mapping.

**Validation.** **7 sabotages, 7 RED against their named test.** Full unit+golden **4,483 passed
/ 15 failed** against the same matched baseline at `2be5ff4` (**4,240 / 15**) — failure sets
identical, `comm` empty both ways. Both committed reports were re-derived from the round-6 code
into a scratch path and compared field-by-field against the committed ones: **identical apart
from `provenance` and `source.accessed`**, so none of these tightenings moves the corpus
(897,096 CDS / 11,671 pseudo / 273 multi-segment / 44,291 contigs). ruff + black clean.

**Review round 7 — one finding, and it *widens* the rule round 5 narrowed.** A line beginning
with `>` reached `parse_gff3_line` and raised a column-count refusal. The GFF3 spec: *"For
backward-compatibility with the GFF version output by the Artemis tool, a GFF line that begins
with the character `>` creates an implied `##FASTA` directive"* (Sequence Ontology GFF3 spec,
accessed 2026-08-06) — so the reader was **refusing valid GFF3**. Checked against the spec text
rather than taken on the reviewer's word, because it reverses a decision made two rounds
earlier; the two are consistent, and the same paragraph settles both: `##fasta` is not a
directive in any form, while `>` is one. Nothing that *is* a feature line can be lost, since the
spec forbids a seqid from beginning with an unescaped `>`. The predicate is
`implies_fasta_section`, used by the iterator **and** the census, and an indented `>` remains a
refusal.

**Validation.** 4 sabotages, **4 RED against their named test** — including both *divergence*
directions (iterator narrow / census wide, and the reverse), which is the property that made the
round-5 fix worth sharing a predicate for. Full unit+golden **4,487 passed / 15 failed** against
the matched baseline at `2be5ff4` (**4,240 / 15**) — failure sets identical, `comm` empty both
ways. The census re-derived from this code is **identical to the committed report** field for
field apart from provenance. ruff + black clean.

**Review round 8 — 3 findings, 2 real, and the third was the same false positive for the FIFTH
time.** Both real ones are the *last* two instances of the pattern rounds 5–7 kept surfacing.

**A published artifact stated the wrong filename.** `parse_census` reads the **fetch** report
through `read_supply_report`, so every refusal said *"supply report …"* while quoting the fetch
report's path — and the census copies that text verbatim into `corpus_check_reason`, i.e. into a
committed file. The function takes a `label` now, and the test carries a positive control (the
same function must still say "supply report" when *that* is the missing one), because a global
rename would satisfy a one-sided assertion.

**`_write` was the one `OSError` left escaping.** A read-only output directory or a full disk
aborted both subcommands with exit 1 — and the run whose report cannot be written is precisely
the one whose refusal has to be legible, since nothing is left on disk to read afterwards.

**The refuted one, fifth occurrence, now graded `major`:** *"the fixture is not Git-tracked and
its md5 is `3650a210…`"*. Refuted by execution on three independent facts: `git ls-files
--error-unmatch` resolves it, the **blob in `HEAD`** md5s to `3afa0aff910cfd08f9f0163981656308`
at 33,003 bytes with a `1f 8b` header, and CI — a clean GitHub-hosted checkout — ran the whole
pytest tier green on this head. The CLI sandbox mangles binaries; the permanent guard with its
positive control has been in the suite since round 4.

**Validation.** 3 sabotages, **3 RED against their named test**. Full unit+golden **4,489 passed
/ 15 failed** vs the matched baseline at `2be5ff4` (**4,240 / 15**) — failure sets identical,
`comm` empty both ways. Census re-derived from this code is **identical to the committed report**
apart from provenance. ⚠ This round cost a **19-minute Fair-Usage wait**; waiting is free and no
Greptile credit was spent. Counts across eight rounds: **9, 2, 4, 5, 5, 5, 1, 2**.

**Review round 9 — 2 findings, 1 real, and the fixture claim for the SIXTH time (now `minor`).**
The real one: `isinstance(True, int)` is True, so a hand-edited `"n_targets": true` compared as 1
and a one-row report satisfied `rows_match_targets` **and** `all_targets_ok` — while
`targets_match_supply_report`, reading the *same* field, already rejected it. Two of three
clauses disagreeing with the third is what a per-clause repeat of a type check produces, so the
predicate is derived once and all three read it. The test carries a positive control (the same
report with a real `int` must pass all three), because a clause broken outright would satisfy a
one-sided assertion equally well.

**Validation.** 3 sabotages, **3 RED against their named test** — one per clause and one for the
shared predicate, since breaking only the predicate would leave a per-clause repeat undetected.
Full unit+golden **4,490 passed / 15 failed** vs the matched baseline at `2be5ff4`
(**4,240 / 15**) — failure sets identical, `comm` empty both ways. Counts across nine rounds:
**9, 2, 4, 5, 5, 5, 1, 2, 1**.

## Step P3-15′-c-ii — 2026-08-07: the criterion (c) predicate, its per-candidate producer, and D4's two symmetric diagnostics

**Inputs.** `data/processed/mining/round0_fp_manifest.json` (941 candidates / 76 hosts);
`data/interim/production_annotations/*.gff.gz` (339, md5-verified at `-c-i`);
`data/interim/production_genomes/*.fna` (the contig-id bridge);
`data/processed/mining/production_genomes_v0.parquet` (GTDB clade);
`data/processed/negatives/{decoys,mining_pool}_v0.parquet` (the §9.1 arm).
**Process.** `mining/synteny.py` implements ADR-0006 D4's frozen `criterion_c` verbatim plus
the downstream walk, the tandem carve-out and the gene-identity vocabulary D4 delegates here;
`mining/synteny_producer.py` writes `$ROUND_DIR/synteny_status.json` (`candidate_id → status`,
the (a)-producer's shape) and the two committed diagnostic reports. `SYNTENY_SUPPLY_AVAILABLE`
was added beside `MSA_SUPPLY_AVAILABLE`, `candidate_evidence` / `remine_candidate_evidence`
gained the synteny status map with the same fail-closed absent-id rule, and `--synteny-available`
was promoted from a one-way `store_true` to the two-way pair with an exit-4 unevidenced preflight.
**Outputs.** `src/tbox_finder/mining/{synteny,synteny_producer}.py`;
`reports/p3/synteny_false_pass.json`; `reports/p3/synteny_exclusion_diagnostic.json`;
`tests/unit/test_synteny{,_producer}.py` (+112 tests).
**Validation.** 941/941 statuses (541 passed / 101 failed / 299 unavailable); the false-pass
control is **powered** (margin 0.975 ≥ 0.20); full unit+golden **4,604 passed / 13 failed**
against a matched baseline worktree at `95d0149` (**4,492 / 13**) — failure sets identical,
`comm` empty both ways; **19 sabotages / 19 RED against their named test**.
**Decisions.** ADR-0006 D4 (vocabulary delegated here, §10.1-verified); ADR-0005 D14 (fail-closed
`unavailable` ⇒ spared), D15 (both-strand carry-through).
**Commit.** see below.

**The criterion discriminates, and by a wide margin.** Candidates pass at **57.5 %** against a
clade-matched random-leader background of **1.67 %** and a §9.1 5′UTR-decoy background of
**4.52 %** — a 13–34× enrichment, with a positive-context arm at **99.20 %** proving the control
is powered rather than merely quiet. The reading is not that the criterion is loose: the
round-0 pool is Stage-1 *false positives* drawn from a masked negative substrate, and a 96-nt
element scoring 0.9977 that sits 19 bp upstream of an `alanine--tRNA ligase` is most plausibly
an uncatalogued T-box. ADR-0005 D14's spare rule exists precisely so those are spared rather
than trained against, and 541 of them now are.

**⚠ THE BIGGEST DEFECT WAS FOUND BY DISBELIEVING A NUMBER, NOT BY A TEST.** The first run
returned **541 of 941 passing** and the per-CDS background density of D4's four classes is
**4.14 %** — an irreconcilable gap. The cause was that the downstream walk bounded the distance
only from above: a bacterial genome is ~88 % coding, so a window buried inside a long gene found
that gene as its "downstream" gene and inherited its identity. D4's class-II case genuinely
needs a *negative* distance (a translational T-box abuts/overlaps the start codon), so the fix
could not be "reject overlap"; it is that the CDS start must lie at or after the **element's own
5′ end**, which pins no new number. The corpus-level counts barely moved because Stage-1
candidates land in leader regions rather than inside genes — so the number that exposed the bug
was not the number the bug corrupted.

**⚠ TWO DEFECTS THE DIAGNOSTIC FOUND IN ITSELF, AND BOTH WERE SILENT ZEROS.** (1) The pseudogene
diagnostic reported **0** pseudogenized first-downstream ORFs corpus-wide, because the tandem
carve-out hops exactly the population the diagnostic exists to size; the counts now accumulate
across the whole walk (15 pseudogenized, 88 unjudgeable). (2) D4's hypothetical/pseudogene route
was **entirely unreachable**: `gff3.gene_identity_text` collects `Dbxref`/`Name` as well as
`product`, and on NCBI CDS those are accessions (`Dbxref` is present on 29,852 of 30,273
measured CDS), so every `hypothetical protein` still had non-empty "identity text", never
resolved to unjudgeable, and was scored a *decided* `failed` instead of being routed to the
fallback. Identifier-shaped values are now filtered, with a positive control asserting the
filter removes identifiers rather than removing judgement.

**⚠ THE VOCABULARY IS PRECISION-FIRST BECAUSE THE PERMISSIVE VERSION WAS MEASURED FIRST.** An
"amino-acid word + enzyme word" rule looks reasonable and swallows `HAMP domain-containing
histidine kinase` (38 CDS over 12 hosts, two-component signalling), `serine/threonine protein
kinase`, `glutamine amidotransferase` (purine/His/Trp — **not** tRNA-dependent transamidation),
`methylated-DNA--[protein]-cysteine S-methyltransferase` (DNA repair) and `peptide-methionine
(S)-S-oxide reductase` (protein repair). Every `EXCLUSIONS` entry was observed on this corpus
before it was written down, exclusions are applied **before** every include rule, and the
transamidation rules all require the literal `tRNA`. Two ordering corrections came out of the
audit: the curated product name outranks the gene symbol (`hisJ` is the histidine transporter's
binding protein in the enterics and **histidinol phosphatase** in Firmicutes), and the symbol
route fires only when the product name says nothing at all — consulting it otherwise put `PTS
galactitol transporter subunit IIB` into the transamidation class via `gatB`, `cytochrome C-552`
into transport via `cycA`, and `homocitrate synthase` into aaRS via `lysS`. 24 of 4,991 matches
came from that route and 3 of the 24 were wrong.

**⚠ THE CONTIG BRIDGE IS BY IDENTITY, AND AN INDEX JOIN WOULD HAVE BEEN WRONG ON HALF THE
CORPUS.** A candidate's contig is `:c<ci>`, an index into the genomic FASTA's record order; a
GFF's `seqid` is the NCBI contig accession. **23 of the 48** candidate-carrying annotated hosts
serve their GFF seqids in a different order than their FASTA records, so `records[ci]` ↔
`seqids[ci]` would silently read the wrong contig on ~48 % of hosts. The id join resolves
**134 of 134** needed (host, contig) pairs.

**Three gaps reported rather than papered over.** (1) The **shipped §9.1 decoy rows carry
coordinates on 0 annotated production hosts** — `decoys_v0`'s three non-structured pools have no
accession at all, its 2,999 `structured_rna` accessions are Rfam source contigs, and
`mining_pool_v0`'s 45,988 leader/trail windows sit on the TBDB source genomes — so that arm is
`available: false` **with its counts**, and the §9.1 leader class is re-instantiated inside the
annotated corpus instead (5′UTR and tRNA-adjacent windows). (2) The **false-FAIL arm has almost
no positive denominator**: only **2 TBDB records on 1 assembly** intersect the 339, because the
production substrate is by construction a negative one. (3) The **joint a ∧ b ∧ c arm is
structurally unavailable** — (b) has no backend until P3-15′-d — and is withheld, never computed
from two unavailable disjuncts.

**Per-clade exclusion is the clade-structured cap D4 commissioned, and it is large.** 31.8 %
of candidates are `unavailable` (286 host-unannotated, 11 unjudgeable, 2 contig-absent), with
five phyla at **100 %** exclusion (Chloroflexota, Desulfobacterota, Fibrobacterota, Thermotogota,
Bdellovibrionota_C), Bacillota at 38.5 %, and Atribacterota / Sysuimicrobiota / Fusobacteriota at
0 %. That is the recall cap the commissioned bakta/prokka arm exists to lift. Empirical passing
distances: p50 117 bp, p95 269 bp, p99 364 bp, max 454 bp — all inside D4's 500 bp pad, which is
the sensitivity check D4 asks for.

**⚠ `n_mined` IS STILL STRUCTURALLY 0.** Sparing is a disjunction so mining is a conjunction:
`relaxed_architecture` remains the one unavailable backend, so `max_possible_yield` still caps
the round at 0 until P3-15′-d lands. This step removes one of the two blockers, not both.

**Review round 1 — 20 findings (app 5, CLI 15), all real, 8 major; only one in common.** The app
and the CLI overlapped on exactly the CLI-wiring finding, so running both was worth it rather
than redundant, as it was at `-c-i`.

**⚠ THE MAJOR ONE: THE TANDEM CARVE-OUT REACHED THE SEARCH BUT NOT THE DECISION.**
`resolve_downstream_gene` selected its target with the **re-anchored** window and then returned
that target's **element-relative** distance, which `synteny_status` judged against the 500 bp
pad — so the carve-out fired only where it was not needed, and turned exactly the tandem loci D4
built it for into **false FAILs**. `DownstreamGene` now carries both distances and `criterion_c`
sees `decision_distance_bp`. **Five candidates move `failed` → `passed`** (541 → 546), and the
decision-distance series is now p50 117 / p95 266 / p99 356 / **max 454 bp**, entirely inside the
pad, with the element-relative max of 1,652 bp explained by `n_passed_via_tandem_carve_out: 5`.
⚠ **My own test could not see this**: it asserted the walk reached the right *gene*, which was
always true. The search was never wrong; the decision was.

**⚠ A NUMBER I REPORTED WAS FROM A SUPERSEDED RUN.** The PR body, commit message, dev-log and
`TODO.md` all quoted "p95 269 / p99 364 / max 454, n 549" while the committed artifact said
"p95 272 / p99 389 / **max 1652**, n 554" — I read the field before the identifier-filter fix and
never re-read it after regenerating. The gap was also the symptom of the real bug: the statistic
collected every strand detail whose *class* was passing without checking its *status*, so
out-of-window hits that FAILED were counted (554 entries against 541 passed candidates). It now
filters on the detail's own status and reports both series.

**⚠ TWO ARTIFACT-PINNING TESTS WENT GREEN UNDER SABOTAGE, AND THAT IS THE CAMPAIGN'S BEST
OUTPUT.** `test_the_distance_statistic_counts_only_passed_evaluations` and
`test_provenance_never_records_an_absolute_local_path` both read the **committed report**, which
was generated by the fixed code — so breaking the source could not reach them. They still earn
their place as guards on the committed evidence, but `TestDiagnosticsComputedNotJustCommitted`
now calls the report builders directly so the *rule* is under test, not one frozen output of it.
Both new tests bite.

**⚠ A TEST THAT COULD NOT CATCH THE TRAP IT NAMED.** `test_no_clause_reads_dvc_tracked_data`
derived against `REPO_ROOT` — so on any laptop that has run `dvc pull`, a DVC-path clause would
read True and the test would still pass. It now derives against a `tmp_path` root holding only
the `SUPPLY_CLAUSES` files and asserts `n_annotated_hosts_on_disk == 0`, which is the environment
the clause set actually has to survive.

**⚠ THE PRODUCED TABLE WAS NEVER READ BY EITHER ROUND.** Both reviewers found it independently:
`candidate_evidence` accepted a synteny map but no CLI leg supplied one, so declaring the backend
available would have left every candidate `unavailable` — spared, with a zero yield
indistinguishable from an honest one. `--synteny-status` is wired into **both**
`apply-spare-rule` legs, and declaring the backend without a table (or supplying one without
declaring it) now raises rather than proceeding — the same answer this function's `probe_set`
parameter already got for the same reason.

**Also fixed.** A committed provenance record named an absolute `/home/<user>/…` path (out-of-repo
inputs are now hashed and recorded as `{name, sha256}`, which is *more* traceable than the path);
the unavailability reason scanned both strands under a single-strand policy; `merge_status_tables`
passed two inputs through unvalidated and accepted a shard contributing no rows; `_upstream_window`
bounded the plus arm but not the minus; `combine_strand_statuses` raised a bare `KeyError`;
`load_contig_ids` raised `IndexError` on a bare `>` header; `synteny._gene_symbols` was private
while the producer's control arm depended on it (now `synteny.gene_symbols`); the
`candidate_evidence` docstring still said no synteny backend exists.

**Validation (round 1).** Full unit+golden **4,621 passed / 13 failed** vs the matched baseline at
`95d0149` (**4,492 / 13**) — failure sets identical, `comm` empty both ways. **28 sabotages / 28
RED against their named test.** Both reports re-derive byte-identically from the final code apart
from `provenance`. ruff 0.15.15 + black 25.11.0 clean.

**Review round 2 — 7 findings (app 1, CLI 6), all real, 5 major.** Counts across two rounds:
**20, 7**.

**⚠ THE FALSE-PASS ARM THAT CONTAINED ITS OWN POSITIVE CLASS, AND THE NUMBER THAT CHANGED BY AN
ORDER OF MAGNITUDE.** The §9.1 5′UTR arm sampled *every* CDS, including the aaRS /
amino-acid-biosynthesis genes the positive-context arm is built from — and a 5′UTR sitting
upstream of an aaRS in a real genome may itself **be** a T-box leader, so counting it as a
*false* pass inflates the rate. Reporting one reading only would have been a choice disguised as
a measurement, so both now ship: drawn over all CDS the arm reads **5.28 %**; drawn over the CDS
naming none of D4's four classes — where every pass is unambiguously false — it reads **0.35 %**.
The gap *is* the ambiguity, and resolving it is not this step's to do.

**⚠ THE SUB-THRESHOLD HOP COULD SKIP A CDS THAT ALREADY SATISFIED THE CRITERION.** The docstring
already claimed the carve-out fires only on an ORF *"that cannot carry the criterion either
way"*; the length branch did not enforce it, so a short CDS naming a D4 class would be hopped in
favour of whatever sat further downstream. **No candidate verdict changed on this corpus** — the
case does not occur here — so this is latent correctness the new test pins rather than a numbers
movement, and it is recorded as such rather than dressed up as a fix that moved something.

**⚠ MY CLI-REACHABILITY TEST WAS VACUOUS, AND `argparse` IS WHY.** It probed the P2 leg by
parsing `[..., "--synteny-status", "t.json", "--help"]` and asserting exit 0 — but argparse
handles `--help` **before** it rejects an unknown option, so that exits 0 even for a flag the
parser has never heard of (verified by execution against a parser carrying no such option). The
test passed whether or not the option existed. `mine_round.build_parser` was extracted so the
assertion can be structural, and a negative control now checks the option set can answer False.

**Two more integrity findings.** `exclusion_reason_totals` fell back to `""` while the per-clade
breakdown fell back to `host_unannotated` for the **same row**, so one row was counted under two
keys and the closed `EXCLUSION_REASONS` vocabulary held in one place and not the other — both now
read one derivation, which *raises* on an unknown reason. And `merge_status_tables` wrote
`config.as_dict()`, which re-reads the **live** `HMM_FALLBACK_AVAILABLE`, so a merge on a checkout
where the flag had flipped would silently rewrite what the shards actually ran under; the
shard-recorded value now wins.

**Validation (round 2).** Full unit+golden **4,627 passed / 13 failed** vs the matched baseline at
`95d0149` (**4,492 / 13**) — failure sets identical, `comm` empty both ways. **32 sabotages / 32
RED against their named test.** ruff + black clean.

**Review round 3 — 4 findings (app 1, CLI 3), all real, 2 major.** Counts across three rounds:
**20, 7, 4**.

**⚠ A FILTERED SUBSET THAT OUTNUMBERED ITS SOURCE.** The strict 5′UTR arm reported **9,087**
rows against the wide arm's **9,065** — impossible for a subset, and the giveaway that the two
arms were **independent draws** each capped at `n_per_host` rather than a population and its
filter. The strict arm is now derived from the wide arm's own sample (`strict_subsample`), so
the nesting holds by construction: **8,662 ≤ 9,090**, and the rates are **4.96 %** wide against
**0.29 %** strict. The report's own wording had claimed the nesting all along.

**⚠ A THIRD ARTIFACT-PINNING TEST WENT GREEN UNDER SABOTAGE.** `test_the_utr_arm_is_reported_
under_BOTH_readings` reads the committed report, so breaking the derivation could not reach it —
the same species as rounds 1 and 2. The filter is now a named function (`strict_subsample`) and
tested directly for the subset property, the identity of what it removes, and the all-D4 edge
case. Three occurrences in one step is a pattern worth carrying forward: **a test that reads a
committed artifact validates the artifact, never the code that made it.**

**⚠ TWO UNITS IN ONE REPORT, UNLABELLED.** The per-clade block sums to **941 candidates**
(546 + 96 + 299) while the distance block reported **554** — not a discrepancy, since a
candidate passing on **both** strands contributes two strand evaluations, but a reader
subtracting one from the other would conclude something was missing. Both blocks now carry an
explicit `unit`, and the report states the reconciliation: `554 = 546 + 8`.

**Also fixed.** `test_the_control_is_powered_and_says_why` asserted `powered` and `margin` but
not `verdict` — the field a reader actually consumes and the one that would go stale silently,
so the name was writing a cheque the body did not honour. And a `decoys_v0.parquet` missing its
`accession` column raised a non-`ProducerError`, aborting the whole sweep **after** every arm
had been computed, over a schema change in a file this arm only reports the *absence* of.

**Validation (round 3).** Full unit+golden **4,635 passed / 13 failed** vs the matched baseline at
`95d0149` (**4,492 / 13**) — failure sets identical, `comm` empty both ways. **33 sabotages / 33
RED against their named test.** Both reports re-derive identically from the final code apart from

⚠ **A CLI review round that read `main → main` is an ABSENCE, not a pass.** Round 3's first CLI
invocation ran from the main checkout because the backgrounded `cd` did not apply to the session

**Review round 4 — 2 findings (app 2), both real, both major.** Counts across four rounds:
**20, 7, 4, 2**.

**⚠ "THE SAME WINDOWS, FILTERED" WAS STILL NOT TRUE.** Round 3 made the strict 5′UTR arm's *CDS
population* a subset of the wide arm's, but each arm still drew its own spans with a fresh
`rng.choice(lengths)` — so the windows were never the same windows, only the genes were. The two
lists now come from **one** draw (`utr_arm_windows` returns `(wide, strict)` where `strict` is a
sublist of `wide`), and the note says what the code does. Final rates: wide **4.74 %**, strict
**0.35 %**, over 9,097 and 8,693 windows.

**⚠ A FOURTH ARTIFACT-PINNING TEST WENT GREEN UNDER SABOTAGE, AND THIS TIME THE FIX WAS TO MOVE
THE RELATION INTO A FUNCTION.** `strict_subsample` was already tested directly, but the sabotage
targeted the **call site** — which no test could see, because the only assertion on the wide↔strict
relation read the committed report. `utr_arm_windows` now owns that relation and is tested for it
by identity (`strict == [wide[1], wide[3]]`, not by count), with a positive control for an
all-non-D4 sample and a refusal for a span-count mismatch. **Four occurrences in one step**; the
lesson is not "add another artifact assertion" but *"if the property is a relation, give the
relation a name."*

**⚠ THE PR DESCRIPTION DRIFTED FROM THE ARTIFACT A SECOND TIME.** It quoted a 99.35 % positive-
context rate while the report's own counts give **99.414 %**. Both drifts in this step came from
hand-copying a number that a later regeneration moved; the reconciliation is now asserted in
`test_the_reported_rate_matches_its_own_counts`, which recomputes every arm's rate and the
control margin from the counts beside them.

**Validation (round 4).** Full unit+golden **4,637 passed / 13 failed** vs the matched baseline at

RED against their named test.** ruff + black clean. ⚠ The CLI's round-4 invocation returned

**Review round 5 — 1 finding (app), real, minor.** Counts across five rounds: **20, 7, 4, 2, 1**.

**⚠ VALUE EQUALITY IS NOT THE CONTRACT.** The round-4 test asserted `strict == [wide[1], wide[3]]`
and `all(w in wide for w in strict)` — but windows are plain tuples, so a producer that *draws a
second time and lands on the same span* satisfies value equality while breaking the one-draw
contract the test exists to pin. The assertions are now `is`.

**⚠ AND THE FIRST SABOTAGE OF THAT FIX WAS ITSELF A NO-OP.** Replacing the returned windows with
`tuple(w)` left the test green — because CPython returns the *same object* for `tuple(t)` when
`t` is already a tuple, so the mutation changed nothing. Checked by execution
(`tuple(t) is t → True`, `tuple(list(t)) is t → False`) and re-run with a genuinely
reconstructing sabotage, which bites. A sabotage that does not mutate proves nothing about the
test; [[verify-the-line-you-ship]] applies to the sabotage as much as to the code.

**Validation (round 5).** Full unit+golden **4,640 passed / 13 failed** vs the matched baseline at
`95d0149` (**4,492 / 13**) — failure sets identical, `comm` empty both ways. **35 sabotages / 35
RED against their named test.** ruff + black clean; no report regenerated (test-only change).

**Review round 6 — 8 CLI findings, 7 real, 2 major (one refuted).** Counts across six rounds:
**20, 7, 4, 2, 1, 8**. The round-6 spike is the CLI's first clean pass since round 3 — its
round-4 invocation returned *"Review limit reached"*, an **absence** that was waited out rather
than counted, so these findings are the accumulated ones the CLI had not yet seen.

**⚠ THE SUB-THRESHOLD TEST USED A GENOMIC SPAN, NOT A CODING LENGTH.** `CdsFeature.length_bp` is
`end - start + 1` over the **span**, so a frameshifted CDS whose two segments sit far apart reads
as long even when it codes for very little — measured: a two-segment CDS spanning 901 bp carrying
152 coding nucleotides. There are **273** multi-segment CDS in this corpus, and §7.1's tandem loci
are exactly where the carve-out has to fire. `gff3.CdsFeature.coding_length_bp` (summed segments)
now drives the test. **No candidate verdict changed on this corpus**, so it is recorded as latent
correctness the new test pins.

**⚠ ONE MAJOR WAS REFUTED BY EXECUTION.** *"The sort tiebreak can raise `TypeError` when
`feature_id` is None."* It cannot: `gff3.CdsFeature.feature_id` is annotated `str` and is always
populated (the dataclass falls back to `<seqid>:<start>-<end>:<strand>:<type>`). The finding
reasoned from **`DownstreamGene.feature_id: str | None`** — a different type, whose `None` case is
the *no-gene-found* result and never reaches a sort. Checked against the declaration rather than
the review's word.

**Also fixed.** The `diagnostics` branch converted only three exception types while three calls in
it raise others (a malformed input aborted with a traceback instead of a refusal); the tRNA arm's
contig extents were built from a **CDS-only** map, so a tRNA on a CDS-free contig skipped the
minus-strand upper bound and could cut a window past the contig end; the strict-arm note had two
sentences welded together in a **committed** artifact; and `ProducerError` escaped both mining
boundaries as an unhandled `RuntimeError`, bypassing the return-code path the callers branch on —
the (c) table is now loaded **first**, so a malformed one is refused before any other input is
read.

**⚠ `ProducerError` WAS NOT THE FAILURE SURFACE.** Round 6 translated it at both mining
boundaries, but `load_status_map` reads **arbitrary JSON**, so a truncated file raises
`json.JSONDecodeError`, a non-object root raises `AttributeError`, and a malformed row raises
`KeyError`/`TypeError` — every one an input fault that bypassed the documented refusal path and
would have surfaced as an unhandled traceback on the leg that decides what gets mined. The catch
now covers all of them, and the test is parametrized over four *distinct* fault shapes rather
than the one the previous round happened to construct.

**Validation (round 7).** Full unit+golden **4,648 passed / 13 failed** vs the matched baseline at

RED against their named test.** ruff + black clean; no report regenerated (error-path change only).

**Review round 8 — 4 CLI findings, all real, 1 major.** Counts across eight rounds:
**20, 7, 4, 2, 1, 8, 1, 4**.

**⚠ [[duplicate-key-merges-instead-of-colliding]], NOW ON THE READ PATH.** `build_status_table`
refuses a repeated `candidate_id` at **write** time, but `load_status_map` rebuilt the map with a
dict comprehension — which collapses a duplicate to its **last** occurrence — and the
status↔rows cross-check then compared two maps built the same wrong way, so it agreed with
itself. Two rows saying `passed` and `failed` for one candidate would have picked one silently.
A table can reach the reader without having been written by the writer, so both ends refuse now.

**⚠ THE FIFTH VACUOUS TEST OF THIS STEP, AND ALL FIVE WERE MINE.**
`test_provenance_never_records_an_absolute_local_path` iterates `provenance["inputs"]` — and both
committed reports carry `"inputs": {}` (every input resolved outside the repo root at generation
time), so **the loop never executed** and `outputs` was never inspected at all. It now asserts the
evidence exists *somewhere* before checking its shape. Running tally of vacuous-test species in
this step: an artifact-pinning assertion (×4) and an empty-collection loop (×1).

**Also fixed.** `pyarrow.lib.ArrowIOError` subclasses `OSError`, so a present-but-unreadable
parquet aborted `false_pass_report` before it wrote anything; and `_annotated_set` carried a
second copy of the `accession → filename` contract, which would have undercounted every host —
looking like a smaller corpus rather than a bug — the day `destination_name` changed.

**Review round 9 — 3 CLI findings, all real, 1 major.** Counts across nine rounds:
**20, 7, 4, 2, 1, 8, 1, 4, 3**. ⚠ The **GitHub app has been silent since `b6234ec`** — five heads
with no app review — so from round 5 on **the CLI has carried the gate alone**, the documented
